lessons.title: Tenses Revision
lessons.grammar_topic: 12 ZAMON — TAKROR (Simple / Continuous / Perfect / Perfect Continuous × Present / Past / Future)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 1 – Tenses revision (12 qatorli jadval); LEARNING (63 so'z); AUDIO 1–10 (ixtiyoriy, uyda); Reading — Ishoqxon Ibrat (Jony Academy matni, moslashtirilgan); Writing 1: advantages/disadvantages essay; SPEAKING/WRITING mavzusi — rahbar rejasi (IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 1-qator): "Advantages and disadvantages of using public transport"
objectives: 12 zamon formulasini 3×4 jadvalda yoddan ayta olish va har biriga 1 gap tuzish.
Vaqt ko'rsatkichiga qarab zamonni tanlash (every day / now / yesterday / by 2030 / for two years…).
Bitta vaziyatni 4 zamon bilan ifodalash (I study / am studying / have studied / have been studying).
IELTS Listening Part 1 (form completion): 6 bo'shliqdan kamida 4 tasini to'g'ri to'ldirish (ism, raqam, sana).

SPEAKING (IELTS Part 3): Public transport: advantages and disadvantages — 4–5 savolga 3–4 gapli javob (javob → sabab → misol), 3+ xil zamon (Present Simple / Present Perfect / will) bilan; WRITING: Public transport: advantages and disadvantages — AD jadval va kirish sinfda, 150–200 so'zli insho uyda (W-B1-AD).
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 1 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.
CORE 20 varag'i — dars sahifasining Lug'at tabidan (PDF).
Kahoot: dars boshida — IELTS 2.0, 25-dars sahifasidagi Kahoot; shu darsning Kahooti L02 boshida o'ynaladi.
Listening: skript ustozda (yashirin transcript), ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi; audio fayl kerak emas.

Writing/Speaking rubrikasi — shu darsdagi W-B1-AD va S-B1-P3 jadvallari (WRITING mashqidan keyin); juftlik tekshiruvi — PEER-AD (WRITING mashqi izohida). Kursning umumiy W-B1 va S-B1 jadvallari va peer-b1 juftlik varag'i (S-B1 jadvali izohida) ham shu darsda qoladi (boshqa darslar uchun).
timeline: Warm-up: "learn" — 12 zamonda
Ustoz "learn" fe'lini aytadi; o'quvchilar navbat bilan 12 zamonda gap tuzadi (I learn / I am learning / I have learned…). Kim to'xtab qolsa — keyingisi davom etadi.
TAKROR: Kahoot — IELTS 2.0, 25-dars (Reflexive pronouns + revision)

IELTS 2.0, 25-dars Kahooti ('O'tgan dars Kahooti' kurslararo ishlamasa — o'sha dars sahifasidan). 20 savol × 15 s; kirish diagnostikasi: 50% dan past mavzular daftarga yoziladi. 2.0 ni Jony'da o'qimagan guruh — 12 zamon bo'yicha og'zaki diagnostika.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — IELTS 2.0, 25-dars (Revision, eng muhim 60 so'z) CORE 20
20 so'z o'zbekcha → inglizcha (4 daq), 1 daq juftlikda tekshirish; kalit — IELTS 2.0, 25-dars Lug'at tabi; 17/20+ — 2 coin. 2.0 ni o'qimagan guruh — 'Learning' bo'yicha 10 so'zlik so'rov.
Uy vazifasini tekshirish (1-darsda — kurs tartibi)
Uy vazifasi yo'q — kurs tartibi: dars boshida takror (Kahoot + CORE 20); uy vazifasi MAJBURIY / IXTIYORIY; Progress testlar — 6, 11, 15, 20-darslarda, Final — 26-darsda.
YANGI MAVZU: 12 zamon — takror (Simple / Continuous / Perfect / Perfect Continuous)

10 daq: doskada 3×4 jadval (Present/Past/Future × Simple/Continuous/Perfect/Perfect Continuous) to'ldiriladi va grammar.formulas bilan solishtiriladi; presentation 1, 2, 5, 6, 10-savollar. CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq: '12 zamon jadvali' (yakka + juftlik).
Lug'at: Learning — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

10 so'z: memorization, comprehension, retention, practice, concentration, curriculum, note-taking, assessment, study habits, study schedule. So'z → ma'no → 1 gap (zamonini ayting). Qolgani — flashcard; SUPER — kuchlilarga.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 12 qator)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. Juftlikda: biri aytadi, biri sanaydi; me'yor — normativ[2].
Sinf mashqlari: Vaqt ko'rsatkichi → zamon; Bitta vaziyat — to'rt zamon
Vaqt ko'rsatkichi (8 daq, yakka); Bitta vaziyat (6 daq, juftlik). ZAXIRA: Zamonni aniqlang (4 daq), Xatoni toping. Vaqt yetmasa: avval Xatoni toping, keyin Zamonni aniqlang tashlanadi.
Listening (IELTS Part 1): form completion

2 daq tayyorgarlik; 1-tinglash (ustoz transcript'ni ikki ovozda o'qiydi); 1 daq juftlikda solishtirish; 2-tinglash; 3 daq javoblar — dalil gap skriptdan; 2 daq 2 ta zamon gapini og'zaki tiklash (I've been studying it for five years. / By the end of August you will have finished the whole course.).
Reading: T/F/NG + sentence completion
3 daq gist: 'Why was Ibrat unhappy with the madrasa?' (students memorized without understanding); 5 daq T/F/NG (6 band); 4 daq sentence completion (5 band). ZAXIRA: Zamonlarni toping.
SPEAKING — Public transport: advantages and disadvantages

1 daq Part 1 lead-in (2 savol, juftlikda) → 6 daq Part 3 juftlikda: A savol beradi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashadi; har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol (+ qarama-qarshi fikr) → 2 daq 2 o'quvchi sinf oldida bitta Part 3 savoliga javob beradi, ustoz S-B1-P3 bilan baholaydi → 1 daq feedback (1 kuchli tomon + 1 tuzatish + 1 foydali ibora).
WRITING — Public transport: advantages and disadvantages

1 daq W-B1-AD rubrikasi (proyektorda) → 2 daq savol tahlili (savol turi: advantages/disadvantages; kalit so'zlar) → 3 daq juftlikda AD jadval: 2 afzallik + 2 kamchilik, har biriga misol (SPEAKING g'oyalaridan) → 4 daq yakka kirish (35–45 so'z: savolni o'z so'zlari bilan + reja/fikr) → 2 daq juftlikda PEER-AD tekshiruvi. To'liq insho — uyda (Writing 1).
Exit ticket

Qog'ozga yozib, chiqishda topshiradi: (1) I ___ (study) English for five years now. (have been studying / have studied); (2) 'eslab qolish, xotirada saqlash' inglizchasi? (retention); (3) Reading: matnda umuman yo'q ma'lumot uchun qaysi javob yoziladi — FALSE yoki NOT GIVEN? (NOT GIVEN).
Uyga vazifa
homework ro'yxati bo'yicha MAJBURIY (~60 daqiqa) va IXTIYORIY qismlarni ayting; WRITING — Public transport (Writing 1) — sinfdagi kirish davomi; SPEAKING — ovozli 2 javob.

intro: SIMPLE — fakt, odat, tugagan ish: reads / drove / will study.
CONTINUOUS — jarayon shu paytda: am learning / were sleeping / will be travelling.
PERFECT — nuqtagacha tugagan, natija: has read / had finished / will have finished.
PERFECT CONTINUOUS — nuqtagacha davom etgan jarayon: have been learning / had been sleeping / will have been waiting.
Qoida: Present — hozir; Past — o'tgan nuqta; Future — kelajak nuqta. Ustun ma'noni, qator vaqtni beradi.
formulas: He reads a book every day. / I am learning English.
U har kuni kitob o'qiydi. / Men ingliz tili o'rganyapman.
She drove a car yesterday. / We were sleeping.
U kecha mashina haydadi. / Biz uxlayotgan edik.
S + will + V1 / S + will be + V-ing
We will study hard next week. / We will be travelling around the world.
Kelasi hafta qattiq o'qiymiz. / Biz dunyo bo'ylab sayohat qilayotgan bo'lamiz.
S + have/has + V3 / S + have/has been + V-ing
He has read 10 books so far. / I have been learning English for 2 years.
U hozirgacha 10 kitob o'qidi. / Men 2 yildan beri ingliz tili o'rganyapman.
S + had + V3 / S + had been + V-ing
He had finished elementary level by 2020. / He had been sleeping for 2 hours by the time his mother arrived.
U 2020-yilgacha boshlang'ich darajani tugatgan edi. / Onasi kelguncha u 2 soat uxlagan edi.
S + will have + V3 / S + will have been + V-ing
We will have finished university by 2030. / I will have been waiting for 2 hours by noon.
2030-gacha universitetni tugatib bo'lamiz. / Tushga kelib 2 soatdan beri kutayotgan bo'laman.
presentation: How do you usually learn new words?
I usually write them down and review them every evening.
What are you learning right now?
I'm revising the twelve tenses.
What did you learn yesterday?
I learned twenty phrasal verbs about studying.
What were you doing at 8 pm last night?
I was doing my homework.
What will you have learned by the end of this course?
I will have learned more than 1,500 words.
How long have you been studying English?
I have been studying it for three years.
Had you studied any grammar before IELTS 2.0?
Yes, I had studied the basics at school.
Will you be studying at 9 tomorrow?
Yes, I'll be studying in the library.
How many lessons have you had so far?
I've had exactly one — this is the first!
By 2030, how long will you have been learning English?
I will have been learning it for eight years.
notes: Vaqt ko'rsatkichlari: every day/usually → Present Simple; now/at the moment → Present Continuous; yesterday/ago/in 2020 → Past Simple; while/at 8 pm → Past Continuous; so far/already/yet/since/for → Present Perfect (Continuous); by the time + Past → Past Perfect; by 2030 → Future Perfect.
Holat fe'llari (know, believe, own, belong) continuous'da ishlatilmaydi.
Writing 1 (advantages/disadvantages): kirish → afzalliklar → kamchiliklar → xulosa; 150–200 so'z, 3+ xil zamon. Reja — WRITING mashqida.
Learning lug'ati ikki qatlam: akademik otlar (retention, curriculum) + phrasal verbs (look up, brush up on, catch up on).
CCQ: I have lived here for 5 years. — Do I live here now? (Yes)
CCQ: I had finished when she came. — Which happened first? (finished)
CCQ: By 2030 I will have graduated. — Will I graduate before or after 2030? (before)
mistakes: She has studied here since two years.
She has studied here for two years.
By the time I arrived, the lesson started.
I will learn 500 words by June. (tugallik)
I will have learned 500 words by June.
He is reading books every day.

how: CORE 20 — ta'lim jarayonining asosiy otlari va iboralari (sinfda 10 tasi, qolgani flashcard); STRONG — o'rganish strategiyalari (uyda, ixtiyoriy); SUPER — phrasal verbs (look up, figure out, brush up on…) — kuchlilar uchun.
Har so'zga o'quvchi o'zi tanlagan zamonda gap tuzadi va zamonni aytadi: "I have been brushing up on my grammar — Present Perfect Continuous."

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Public transport: advantages and disadvantages
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda savolga mos zamon; jami 3+ xil zamon (Present Simple / Present Perfect / will).
items: Part 1: How do you usually get to school or to Jony Academy?
Part 1: Have you ever travelled on the Tashkent metro?
Part 3: Why do many people in big cities prefer buses and the metro to taxis?
Part 3: What are the main disadvantages of travelling by public transport?
Part 3: How has public transport in your city changed in the last few years?
Part 3: Is public transport better for the environment than cars? Why?
Part 3: What will public transport be like in twenty years?
answers: I usually take the metro, because the station is only five minutes from my house. The trip takes about twenty minutes, so I can review my notes on the way.
Yes, I have, many times. I have used it since I was a child. My favourite station is Kosmonavtlar, because it looks like a museum about space.

Well, I think the main reason is the price. A metro ride costs much less than a taxi, so students and workers can save a lot of money every month. Also, the metro is often faster in the morning. For example, my father has stopped using taxis for this reason.

The main drawback is that buses can be very crowded, especially in the morning. Sometimes you have to stand for the whole trip. Another problem is waiting: in some areas buses come only every thirty minutes. For example, last winter I waited at a bus stop for forty minutes and was late for a test.

It has changed a lot. The city has opened new metro lines, and part of a new ring line is already working. Many old buses have been replaced with electric ones, which are cleaner and quieter. Also, people have started paying with bank cards and phones, so travelling has become much easier.

Yes, I think it is much better. One bus can carry fifty or sixty people, but a car usually carries only one or two, so buses produce less air pollution per person. For example, in Tashkent one metro train takes hundreds of cars off the road. However, old buses with dirty engines are not so green.

I think it will be faster and smarter. Most buses will probably be electric, and the metro will reach every district of the city. Apps will show the exact time of every bus, so nobody will wait at a cold bus stop. However, I don't think cars will disappear, because some people will always want their own space.
class_ex.note: ICQ: Necha gapda javob berasiz? (3–4) — Misol kerakmi? (Ha). Gap boshlanmalari: Well, I think… / The main advantage is that… / On the other hand, … / For example, … / So overall, … Zamon: 'usually' → Present Simple; 'has … changed' → Present Perfect; 'in twenty years' → will. Baholash — S-B1-P3 (pastdagi jadval). Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 1-qator ("Advantages and disadvantages of using public transport"); savollar va namunalar — Jony Academy, original.

answers: I know a lot of study techniques now. (know — holat fe'li)
She has been doing research on memorization for three months. (for + davr)
When the assessment started, I had already finished my notes. (oldingi ish — Past Perfect)
Look! The students are taking notes in the library. (Look! — hozir, Present Continuous)
Yesterday I revised the whole curriculum. (yesterday — Past Simple)

class_ex.title: WRITING — Public transport: advantages and disadvantages
class_ex.instr: In many cities, more and more people are using buses and the metro instead of cars and taxis. What are the advantages and disadvantages of using public transport? Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval + kirish (35–45 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi (Writing 1)
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: advantages/disadvantages — ikkala tomon so'raladi; fikr so'ralmagan, xulosada qisqa fikr ixtiyoriy.
2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: more and more people / buses and the metro / instead of cars and taxis / advantages / disadvantages / public transport.

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: afzalliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + fikr, agar savol so'rasa)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of … is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, … also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …

5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: 3+ xil zamon — Present Simple (faktlar), Present Perfect (o'zgarishlar: has become / have opened), will (kelajak); jami 2+ marta. Mavzu so'zlari: fare, rush hour, crowded, reliable, traffic jam, convenient, timetable, air pollution.
answers: Namuna kirish (35 so'z): Today, a growing number of people in cities leave their cars at home and travel by bus or metro. This change has clear benefits, but it also has some drawbacks, which this essay will discuss.

Namuna AD jadval: Afzalliklar — 1) arzon: metro fare taksidan ancha arzon, o'quvchi pul tejaydi; 2) rush hour da reliable: poyezdlar har necha daqiqada keladi, traffic jam ga tushmaydi; yangi bekatlar ochilgan; Kamchiliklar — 1) ertalab avtobuslar crowded, butun yo'l tik turib boriladi; 2) chekka tumanlarda timetable noqulay: avtobusni 30 daqiqa kutish.

Namuna insho (190 so'z) — kirish: Today, a growing number of people in cities leave their cars at home and travel by bus or metro. This change has clear benefits, but it also has some drawbacks, which this essay will discuss.

Namuna insho — body 1: One advantage of public transport is its low cost. In Tashkent, a metro fare is much cheaper than a taxi, so students save money. Another benefit is that the metro is reliable during rush hour. For example, trains come every few minutes and never get stuck in a traffic jam, and the city has opened new stations.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, public transport has some drawbacks. Firstly, buses are often crowded in the morning, so passengers have to stand for the whole trip. Secondly, the timetable is not convenient in some districts. For instance, my cousin, who lives on the edge of the city, has often waited half an hour for a bus.

Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, public transport saves money, but crowded buses and long waits can make it uncomfortable. In my view, the benefits are greater, and if the city adds more buses, more drivers will switch to public transport and air pollution will fall.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — Present Simple (is, come, get stuck, lives, saves), Present Perfect (has opened, has often waited), will (will discuss, will switch, will fall); bog'lovchilar — Another benefit, For example, On the other hand, Firstly, Secondly, For instance, In conclusion, so/but, which/who/if; mavzu so'zlari — fare, rush hour, reliable, traffic jam, crowded, timetable, convenient, air pollution.
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 1-qator ("Advantages and disadvantages of using public transport"); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). PEER-AD (juftlik, Ha/Yo'q): 1) savol o'z so'zlari bilan? 2) afzallik va kamchilik alohida xatboshida? 3) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol? 4) 4+ bog'lovchi? 5) dars grammatikasi 2+? 6) 150+ so'z (sinfda kirish 35–45)? Namuna insho o'quvchiga uy inshosi tekshirilgandan keyin ko'rsatiladi.

reading.title: Ishaqkhan Ibrat — a teacher ahead of his time
text: Ishaqkhan Ibrat was born in 1862 in To'raqo'rg'on, a town near Namangan. He studied at a madrasa in Kokand, but the old system disappointed him: students memorized texts for years without understanding them. Ibrat believed that learning without understanding was useless.

Later, Ibrat spent several years travelling in the Middle East and India. While he was travelling, he was learning: he was reading books and collecting words from different languages. By the time he returned home, he had learned several new languages. He had been collecting words for years, and in 1901 he published a dictionary in six languages.

In To'raqo'rg'on he also opened a new-method school where children learned by understanding, not by memorization. In 1908 he started a printing house and printed books there. He also wrote 'Tarixi Farg'ona' (The History of Fergana). Many of his ideas — active learning, critical thinking, self-directed study — are exactly what modern schools are trying to do today.

Ibrat died in 1937. Many years later, his house in To'raqo'rg'on became a museum. Since then, thousands of students have visited his museum. If he were alive, he would probably be running an online school.

kahoot.q: I ___ English for two years now.
kahoot.explain: "for two years now" — hozirgacha davom etayotgan jarayon: Present Perfect Continuous (have been + V-ing).

kahoot.q: Look! The students ___ notes.
kahoot.explain: "Look!" — ish ayni paytda bo'lyapti: Present Continuous (am/is/are + V-ing).

kahoot.q: By the time I arrived, the lesson ___.
kahoot.explain: Men kelishimdan OLDIN dars boshlangan — oldingi ish: Past Perfect (had + V3).

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
kahoot.explain: know — holat fe'li, Continuous shaklda ishlatilmaydi: I know the answer.

kahoot.q: By June, I ___ 500 new words.
kahoot.explain: by + kelajak nuqta, ish shu nuqtagacha tugaydi: Future Perfect (will have + V3).

kahoot.q: She ___ in Tashkent since 2020.
kahoot.explain: since 2020 — o'tmishdan hozirgacha: Present Perfect (has + V3). Present Simple/Continuous since bilan ishlatilmaydi.

kahoot.q: While we ___, the phone rang.
kahoot.explain: O'tmishdagi jarayonni boshqa qisqa ish bo'lib yubordi: Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing).

kahoot.q: "Men har kuni kitob o'qiyman."
options: I read a book every day.
I am reading a book every day.
I have read a book every day.
I was reading a book every day.
kahoot.explain: every day — odat: Present Simple (V1). Odat uchun Continuous ishlatilmaydi.

kahoot.q: This time tomorrow we ___ to London.
kahoot.explain: "This time tomorrow" — kelajakdagi aniq paytda davom etadigan jarayon: Future Continuous (will be + V-ing).

kahoot.q: Qaysi zamon nuqtagacha DAVOM ETGAN jarayonni bildiradi?
kahoot.explain: Perfect Continuous — nuqtagacha davom etgan jarayon: have been learning / had been sleeping.

kahoot.q: She was tired because she ___ all day.
kahoot.explain: O'tgan nuqtagacha (was tired) davom etgan jarayon: Past Perfect Continuous (had been + V-ing).

kahoot.q: Qaysi savol TO'G'RI?
kahoot.explain: Savol: Have/Has + S + V3? you → have; fe'l V3 (finished).

kahoot.q: Writing down key points during a lecture is called ___.
kahoot.explain: note-taking — konspekt olish (ma'ruzada asosiy fikrlarni yozib borish).

kahoot.q: Good students ___ feedback from their teachers.
kahoot.explain: seek feedback — fikr-mulohaza so'ramoq. look/search keyin "for" kerak bo'lardi.

kahoot.q: The ability to keep information in your memory is ___.
kahoot.explain: retention — eslab qolish, xotirada saqlash. comprehension — tushunish.

kahoot.q: The list of subjects taught at a school is its ___.
kahoot.explain: curriculum — o'quv dasturi.

kahoot.q: "blended learning" nimani anglatadi?
kahoot.explain: blended learning — aralash ta'lim: onlayn + sinfdagi darslar.

kahoot.q: I can't study at home — it's too noisy. I need a quiet learning ___.
kahoot.explain: learning environment — o'quv muhiti (qayerda va qanday sharoitda o'qish).

kahoot.q: Learning from your classmates is called ___ learning.
kahoot.explain: peer learning — tengdoshlardan o'rganish (peer — tengdosh).

kahoot.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "comprehension"?
kahoot.explain: comprehension = understanding — tushunish.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 1 — form completion. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear a phone call between a student and a receptionist at a language centre about a summer English course.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (ism, raqam, daraja, sana, kun) belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: RECEPTIONIST: Good morning, Sunrise Language Centre. How can I help you?
AZIZA: Hi. I'd like to enrol on the summer English course.
RECEPTIONIST: Sure. Your name, please?
AZIZA: Aziza Karimova. That's K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A. [Q1]
RECEPTIONIST: And how old are you?
AZIZA: I'm seventeen.
RECEPTIONIST: How long have you been studying English?
AZIZA: I started when I was twelve, so I've been studying it for five years now. [Q2]
RECEPTIONIST: And what's your level?
AZIZA: I think I'm B2, but my placement test last week said B1. [Q3]
RECEPTIONIST: OK, I'll write B1. The course starts on the fourteenth of July — sorry, that was last year. It starts on the fifteenth of July. [Q4]
AZIZA: Great. Are the classes in the evening? I'm taking a maths course in the mornings this summer.
RECEPTIONIST: Yes, at six p.m. The groups usually meet on Mondays and Wednesdays, but the Wednesday group is full, so you'll be on Mondays and Thursdays. [Q5]
AZIZA: That's fine. What's in the curriculum?
RECEPTIONIST: Speaking practice, note-taking and a short assessment every two weeks. By the end of August you will have finished the whole course.
AZIZA: And how much is it?
RECEPTIONIST: Last summer it was eight hundred thousand so'm a month, but this year it's eight hundred and fifty thousand. [Q6]
AZIZA: OK, thanks.
RECEPTIONIST: We'll email you a study schedule. See you in July!
(Ustoz uchun — o'qilmaydi) Chalg'itgichlar: B2 → B1 [Q3], 14th → 15th [Q4], Wednesdays → Thursdays [Q5], 800,000 → 850,000 [Q6].

intro: USED TO + V1 — oldin bo'lgan, hozir yo'q odat yoki holat.
BE USED TO + V-ing / ot — o'rganib qolgan, odatiy, qiyin emas.
GET USED TO + V-ing — o'rganib bormoq (jarayon).
Farq: used to → o'tgan zamon, V1; be/get used to → V-ing (to — predlog!).
formulas: I used to play computer games all night.
Men oldin tun bo'yi kompyuter o'yinlari o'ynardim.
I didn't use to drink coffee.
Did you use to walk to school?
I am used to getting up early. / I'm used to the noise.
Men erta turishga o'rganib qolganman. / Shovqinga o'rganganman.
S + be + not + used to + V-ing / Be + S + used to + V-ing?
I'm not used to drinking coffee. / Are you used to working online?
Qahva ichishga o'rganmaganman. / Onlayn ishlashga o'rganganmisan?
S + get/is getting + used to + V-ing
She is getting used to living in a dormitory.
presentation: Did you use to have a phone at 10?
No, I didn't use to have one. I got my first phone at 13.
What did people use to do before the internet?
They used to write letters and read newspapers.
Are you used to studying online?
Yes, I'm used to it now — we did it for two years.
Are you getting used to the new version of the app?
Slowly. I'm still not used to the new interface.
Is your grandmother used to smartphones?
She's getting used to video calls with us.
notes: used to — faqat o'tgan zamon; hozirgi odat uchun Present Simple + usually. be used to = 'odatiy, qiyin emas', hozirgi odat EMAS.
"used to" holat uchun ham: I used to be shy / There used to be a shop here.
get used to — jarayon: It takes time to get used to living abroad.
CCQ: I used to walk to school. — Do I walk to school now? (No) Was it a habit? (Yes)
CCQ: I'm used to the noise. — Is it a problem for me? (No) Is it new for me? (No)

reading.title: Steve Jobs — phones used to have buttons
text: Steve Jobs was born in 1955 in San Francisco and was adopted as a baby. He used to be a difficult pupil at school, and he dropped out of college after six months. But he used to sit in on classes that interested him, such as calligraphy — years later, that class gave the Mac its beautiful fonts.

In 1976 Jobs and his friend Steve Wozniak started Apple. Computers used to be huge, expensive machines for big companies; the two Steves came up with a small computer for ordinary people. Apple grew fast, but in 1985, after a conflict with the company's board, Jobs had to leave. He later said that losing his job was the best thing that could have happened to him.

He returned to Apple in 1997, when the company was in serious trouble. Then Apple released the iPod (2001), the iPhone (2007) and the iPad (2010), and these products brought about big changes. Before the iPhone, most phones used to have small buttons. People didn't use to touch their phone screens, and at first many of them weren't used to it. Today we are so used to touch screens that small children sometimes try to swipe a TV.
Jobs died in 2011. In a famous speech at Stanford University in 2005, he advised students to 'stay hungry, stay foolish'.

listening.audios: Jony Academy original skripti — ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi (~1.5–2 daq). Kitob AUDIO 11–20 — ixtiyoriy, uyda.
intro: IELTS Listening Part 2 — Multiple choice. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
You will hear a radio interview with a guide from a technology museum.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollar va variantlarni o'qing, kalit so'zlarni belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: PRESENTER: Dilnoza, you're a guide at the Museum of Everyday Technology. What makes it special?
DILNOZA: Many people think we're famous for our old computers, but that collection is actually quite small. What we're really known for is that visitors can touch almost everything. [Q1]
PRESENTER: And what can people see?

DILNOZA: Every hall shows one innovation from daily life. In the Phone Hall you learn that most families used to have just one phone, fixed to the wall, and children didn't use to have their own phones. Next is the Music Hall. It's open as usual — oh, sorry: it's closed this month because we're repairing the roof. [Q2]
PRESENTER: What do young visitors enjoy most?

DILNOZA: They expect to love the old computer games, but their favourite thing is the typewriter. [Q3] They're used to typing on smart devices, so the heavy keys are a big surprise. Typewriters weren't very user-friendly!

DILNOZA: When the first mobile phones appeared, a few people were afraid to touch them. But most people soon got used to them. [Q4] Today we are used to cutting-edge technology, so our old machines look funny to tech-savvy teenagers.
PRESENTER: Any advice for our listeners?
DILNOZA: Weekends are very busy, so come on Saturday morning — no, actually, the best time is a weekday afternoon. [Q5]

tasks.title: IELTS Part 2: Multiple choice (Questions 1–5)
tasks.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
items: 1 The museum is famous for A) its large collection of old computers. B) letting visitors touch almost everything. C) its beautiful old building.
2 Which hall is closed this month? A) the Music Hall B) the Phone Hall C) the Computer Hall
3 Young visitors enjoy most A) the old computer games. B) the old phones. C) the typewriter.
4 When the first mobile phones appeared, people A) were afraid to touch them. B) quickly became comfortable with them. C) used them only at home.
5 The guide says the best time to visit is A) Saturday morning. B) a weekday morning. C) a weekday afternoon.

lessons.title: Question Tags
lessons.grammar_topic: QUESTION TAGS (…, isn't he? / …, do they?)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 3 – Question tags (12 qatorli jadval); BUSINESS (52 so'z); AUDIO 21–30 (ixtiyoriy).
objectives: Tag tuzish: tasdiq → inkor tag, inkor → tasdiq tag (10 gapdan 8 tasi to'g'ri).
Maxsus holatlar: aren't I, shall we, will you, nobody → they, there is → isn't there.
Ohang: ↘ (tasdiqlash) va ↗ (savol) — Speaking Part 1 da.
Listening Part 1: forma to'ldirish — harflangan nom, raqam, sana.
Speaking Part 1–2–3 va Task 2 body paragraf — biznes CORE bilan.
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 3 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.
CORE 20 varag'i — dars sahifasining Lug'at tabidan (PDF).
Kahoot: dars boshida — 'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi (L02); shu darsning Kahooti keyingi dars boshida o'ynaladi.
Listening: skript ustozda (yashirin transcript), ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi; audio fayl kerak emas.
Writing/Speaking rubrikasi — L01 dagi W-B1 va S-B1 jadvallari; juftlik varag'i peer-b1.
timeline: Warm-up: tag bilan salomlashish
Ustoz: "You're tired, aren't you? We don't have a test today, do we?" — javob: "Yes, we are / No, we don't". Savol: tag qanday tuzildi?
TAKROR: Kahoot — L02 (Used to / be used to)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi — L02 savollari (shu darsniki emas). 20 savol × 15 s; izohni faqat yarmidan ko'pi xato qilgan savollarga bering.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — L02 Technology CORE 20
Ustoz 20 so'zni o'zbekcha aytadi, o'quvchi inglizcha yozadi (4 daq); 1 daq juftlikda tekshirish, kalit — L02 Lug'at tabi. 17/20+ — bajarildi (2 coin).
Uy vazifasini tekshirish
L02 'Oldin va hozir — mening oilam': 3 o'quvchi bittadan gap o'qiydi, sinf xatoni topadi; flashcard natijasi (80%+) ilovada.
YANGI MAVZU: Question tags
10 daq: jadval (grammar.formulas) + presentation 1–5; CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq: 'Tag qo'shing' (1-mashq, yakka).
Lug'at: Business — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

revenue, profit margin, market share, entrepreneur, business model, customer loyalty, product launch, boost sales, close a deal, meet a deadline: so'z → ma'no → tag bilan 1 gap; 'Biznes lug'ati' (match) juftlikda.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 12 qator)
Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi.
Sinf mashqlari: Tasdiqmi, inkormi? + Zamonga qarab tag

'Tasdiqmi, inkormi?' — yakka, 6 daq; 'Zamonga qarab tag' — yakka + juftlikda tekshirish, 8 daq; 4 daq — javoblar. ZAXIRA: Xatoni toping, Ohang, Muzokara. Vaqt yetmasa: avval Muzokara, keyin Xatoni toping tashlanadi.
Listening (IELTS Part 1): form completion

2 daq tayyorgarlik; 1-tinglash; 1 daq juftlikda solishtirish; 2-tinglash; 3 daq javoblar — ustoz dalil gapni skriptdan o'qiydi; 2 daq skriptdagi 2 ta tag'li gapni og'zaki tiklash. Ikki xil ovozda o'qing.
Reading: T/F/NG + short-answer questions
3 daq gist: "How did Usmanov become rich?"; 5 daq T/F/NG; 4 daq short-answer. ZAXIRA: Tag'larni toping.
Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Business
Part 1 juftlikda 3 daq (ustoz tag'li savollarni ohang bilan beradi); Part 2: 1 daq tayyorgarlik, A 1.5, B 1.5 daq (sherik checklist bilan); Part 3 — 2 daq; 1 daq feedback (S-B1).
Writing (IELTS Task 2 uslubi): discussion — body paragraf
2 daq savol tahlili; 2 daq reja; 6 daq yozish (70–90 so'z); 2 daq juftlikda peer-b1 bilan tekshirish.
Exit ticket
1) I'm late, ___? / Let's start, ___? (aren't I / shall we) 2) "Bitimni yakunlamoq"? (close a deal) 3) ↘ "You live in Tashkent, don't you?" — savolmi yoki tasdiqlash? (tasdiqlash)
Uyga vazifa
MAJBURIY (~45 daq): flashcard, 10 ta tag, tarjima, og'zaki normativ. IXTIYORIY: Topic 11–13, jadval, STRONG, ZAXIRA.

intro: Tag = yordamchi fe'l + olmosh: "He is a teacher, isn't he?" "They went home, didn't they?"
Tasdiq gap → inkor tag; inkor gap → tasdiq tag. Yordamchi fe'l gapdagi bilan bir xil; maxsus holatlar — jadval va izohlarda.
formulas: He is a teacher, isn't he?
He isn't a teacher, is he?
S + V(s), don't/doesn't + S? / S + V2, didn't + S?
He plays football, doesn't he? / They went to school, didn't they?
U futbol o'ynaydi, to'g'rimi? / Ular maktabga borishdi, shundaymi?
S + modal + V, modal + not + S?
He can swim, can't he? / She will be there, won't she?
U suza oladi, to'g'rimi? / U o'sha yerda bo'ladi, shundaymi?
I am → aren't I? / Let's → shall we? / buyruq → will you?
I am your friend, aren't I? / Let's go home, shall we? / Open the door, will you?
Men do'stingman, shunday emasmi? / Uyga boraylik, xo'pmi? / Eshikni och, xo'pmi?
presentation: You run a business, don't you?
Yes, I do. I run a small online shop.
We should reduce costs, shouldn't we?
Yes, we should. The rent is too high.
Let's set a target for next month, shall we?
Good idea — 100 new customers.
Nobody has raised capital yet, have they?
No, they haven't. Investors are careful.
I'm the youngest in the company, aren't I?
Yes, you are — by five years.
notes: Tag'da ega — faqat olmosh: "Ali is here, isn't he?" (isn't Ali — xato).
have — asosiy fe'l bo'lsa: "You have a car, don't you?" (haven't you — Britaniya variantida ham to'g'ri, kamroq).
this/that → it; these/those → they: "This is yours, isn't it?"
there is/are → isn't/aren't there: "There's a warehouse here, isn't there?" (isn't it — xato).
Ohang: pastga tushsa — tasdiqlash (javob kutilmaydi); ko'tarilsa — haqiqiy savol.
Tag — og'zaki nutq vositasi; IELTS Writing (essay) da ishlatilmaydi.
CCQ: You're tired, aren't you? (↘) — Am I asking or checking? (checking)
CCQ: Nobody called, did they? — Why a positive tag? (nobody — inkor ma'no)
CCQ: You'll meet the deadline, won't you? (↗) — Am I sure? (No)
mistakes: He is a teacher, is he?
He is a teacher, isn't he?
They went home, didn't go they?
I am late, am not I?

class_ex.title: Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Business
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda. Part 1 — savol-javob; Part 2 — 1 daq tayyorgarlik (kalit so'zlar), 1–2 daq gapiring; Part 3 — fikr + sabab.
items: Part 1: You live in Tashkent, don't you? What do you like about your area?
Part 1: You'd like to run your own business one day, wouldn't you? Why?
Part 1: Do you often shop at small local shops?
Part 1: What job would you like to do in the future?
Part 2 card: Describe a small business in your area that you like. You should say: what it sells / who runs it / why people go there — and explain what makes it successful.
Part 3: Why do some young people want to start their own business?
Part 3: What skills does a good business owner need?
answers: Yes, I do. I like my area because it's quiet and green.
Yes, I would. I want to be my own boss and run a small online shop.
Yes, quite often. The small shop near my house is cheap and friendly.
I'd like to be a marketing manager because I enjoy working with people.

I'd like to talk about a small bakery near my house. It sells fresh bread, samsa and cakes. It's run by a family: the father bakes, and his two daughters serve customers. People go there because the bread is always hot and the prices are fair. You can't find better samsa in our area, can you? I think the bakery is successful because the owners know every customer by name, so customer loyalty is very high. A good small business doesn't need a big budget, does it? It needs quality and friendly service.
Many young people want to be independent. Also, the internet makes it easy to set up an online business with a small budget.
A good business owner needs strong decision-making skills and should take calculated risks. They also need to communicate well.
class_ex.note: ICQ: How long do you prepare? (1 minute) — Full sentences? (No, key words) — How long do you speak? (1–2 minutes). CCQ: "You live in Tashkent, don't you?" ↘ — Real question? (No, checking). Kuchsizlar uchun: I'd like to talk about… / It's run by… Sherik peer-b1 bilan tekshiradi (L01). Tag — og'zaki nutq vositasi (essayda emas).

to make people buy more

class_ex.instr: Ustoz 6 gapni o'qiydi: ↗ (savol) yoki ↘ (tasdiqlash)? (1 — namuna: ↘). Keyin juftlikda ikki ohangda ayting.

class_ex.title: ZAXIRA: Muzokara
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: ikki hamkor 6 ta tag'li gap bilan kelishadi (A1 — namuna).
items: A1: price
B1: in advance
A2: deadline
B2: delivery
A3: sign
B3: seal the deal
answers: The price is 10,000 dollars, isn't it?
Yes, it is. But you'll pay in advance, won't you?
Half in advance. The deadline is June, isn't it?
Right. Delivery is free, isn't it?
Yes. We can sign today, can't we?
Let's seal the deal, shall we?

class_ex.title: Writing (IELTS Task 2): discussion — body paragraf
class_ex.instr: Some people prefer to work for a large company, while others prefer to run their own small business. Discuss both views and give your opinion. — Sinfda bitta body paragraf: bir nuqtai nazar, 70–90 so'z, 3+ CORE so'z.
items: 1) Tur — discussion; kalit so'zlar: large company / own small business.
2) Bir tomon; reja: fikr → sabab → misol → natija.
3) On the one hand, … / This is because … / For example, … / As a result, …
4) Tekshiring: 70–90 so'z, CORE 3+, tag yo'q.
class_ex.answers: Namuna (74 so'z): On the one hand, many people prefer to work for a large company because it offers a stable salary and clear rules. This is because big firms usually have high revenue and strong cash flow, so workers are paid on time. For example, an engineer at a large bank does not have to find customers. As a result, employees can focus on their tasks and meet deadlines without the stress of running a business.
class_ex.note: Tekshirish: W-B1 rubrika (L01), sinfda juftlik peer-b1 varag'i bilan; ustoz 2 ta ishni doskada ko'rsatadi. Question tag essayda ishlatilmaydi — bu rasmiy yozma nutq.

reading.title: Alisher Usmanov — he took calculated risks, didn't he?
text: Alisher Usmanov was born in 1953 in Chust, a small town in Namangan region. He didn't come from a business family, did he? No — his father was a prosecutor. As a teenager Alisher did fencing seriously. He trained hard, didn't he? Yes — and sport taught him discipline.
Around 1990 he started a small business making plastic bags. He took calculated risks, didn't he? He did: he bought shares in steel and mining companies, and in the 2000s they became worth billions.

Usmanov was also an early investor in technology. He invested in Facebook in 2009, when many people thought social media was a bubble. Good investors have to think outside the box, don't they? He also owned part of Arsenal football club for many years.

In Uzbekistan many people know him for his charity work: he has funded schools, hospitals and the repair of old buildings. He was the president of the International Fencing Federation for many years — sport never left his life, did it?

intro: SOME- (someone, something, somewhere) — tasdiq gapda: "Someone is at the door." Savolda some- — taklifda yoki 'ha' javobi kutilsa (Would you like something?).
ANY- — savol va inkorda (odatiy savolda any-): "Does anyone know? I don't know anything." Tasdiqda "har qanday": "Anybody can join."
NO- (no one, nobody, nothing, nowhere) — inkor ma'no, FE'L TASDIQ: "Nobody knows the answer." (doesn't know — xato).
EVERY- (everyone, everything, everywhere) — hamma, birlik fe'l: "Everybody loves holidays."
formulas: Anybody can join the club. / Does anyone know?
Har kim klubga qo'shilishi mumkin. / Biror kishi biladimi?
Something is wrong. / Do you have anything to say? / Nothing matters. / Everything is ready.
Nimadir noto'g'ri. / Aytadigan gaping bormi? / Hech narsa muhim emas. / Hamma narsa tayyor.
I left my notes somewhere. / There's nowhere to sit.
Konspektlarimni qayerdadir qoldirdim. / O'tiradigan joy yo'q.
presentation: Has anyone conducted an experiment before?
Yes, someone in our class did one in chemistry.
Is there anything interesting in the new research?
Yes, something surprising: the results suggest sleep improves memory.
Does everyone believe the theory?
No, nobody believes it without evidence.
Did anybody find a mistake in the data?
No one found anything.
Is everything ready for the experiment?
Almost everything. We need something to measure pressure.
notes: Ikki inkor yo'q: "I don't know anything" YOKI "I know nothing" ("I don't know nothing" — xato).
Egalik: someone's phone; tag: Everyone is here, aren't they? (they bilan).
else: someone else (boshqa birov), anything else, nowhere else.
Science lug'ati: observation → hypothesis → experiment → data → analysis → conclusion; WRITING (Distance learning) uchun: "Anyone can join…", "Nobody checks…".
CCQ: Is there anything in the fridge? — Do I know if there is food? (No)
CCQ: Would you like something? — Do I expect 'yes'? (Yes)
CCQ: Nobody knows. — Is it a negative idea? (Yes) Do we add not? (No)
mistakes: I don't know anything. / I know nothing.
I didn't see anybody. / I saw nobody.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Distance learning: pros and cons
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ noaniq olmosh (anyone, everyone, no one/nobody, something, anything) — fe'l birlikda.
items: Part 1: Have you ever taken an online lesson or course?
Part 1: Do you prefer studying alone or with other people?
Part 3: Who benefits most from distance learning?
Part 3: Why do some students find it difficult to study online?
Part 3: Can every subject be taught online — for example, science experiments?
Part 3: What do students miss when nobody is in the classroom with them?
Part 3: Will online learning replace schools in the future?
answers: Yes, I have. Last summer I took an online maths course, because nobody near my house teaches it in the evening. Everything was on Zoom.
I prefer studying with other people. When I study alone, nobody checks my work and I check my phone. With friends, everyone helps, and someone always explains the difficult parts.

I think people who live far from big cities benefit most. For example, a student in a small village near Karshi can join a course with a teacher in Tashkent, and nobody has to travel for hours. Working adults also benefit, because anyone with an internet connection can study in the evening after work.

Well, the main problem is self-discipline. At home, nobody watches you, so it is easy to open Instagram during the lesson. For example, my cousin often turns off his camera and plays games. Also, if the internet connection is weak, something always goes wrong and students miss important parts.

I don't think so. Some subjects, like languages or history, work well online. But science is different, because everyone needs to use the equipment in a laboratory. Watching an experiment on a screen is not the same as doing it yourself, so nothing can fully replace a real lab.

They miss face-to-face contact. In a real classroom, someone always asks a question you also wanted to ask, and the teacher can see if anyone looks confused. Online, students also miss breaks with friends. For example, at my school everyone talks and laughs between lessons, and that makes studying more fun.

I'd say no, not completely. Online lessons are flexible and cheap, so more people will use them. However, school is not only about lessons. Children learn to work in teams and make friends, and nobody learns that alone in front of a screen. So overall, I think schools will mix both types.
class_ex.note: ICQ: Necha gapda javob berasiz? (3–4) — Misol kerakmi? (Ha). Gap boshlanmalari: Well, I think… / The main advantage is that… / On the other hand, … / For example, … / So overall, … Baholash — S-B1-P3 (pastdagi jadval). Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 4-qator ("Pros and cons of distance learning."); savollar va namunalar — Jony Academy, original.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Distance learning: pros and cons
class_ex.instr: Nowadays many students study online from home instead of going to classes. What are the advantages and disadvantages of distance learning? Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval + kirish (35–45 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi (Writing 2)
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: advantages/disadvantages — afzalliklar VA kamchiliklar; fikr so'ralmagan, xulosada qisqa fikr mumkin
2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: study online, from home, instead of going to classes, advantages, disadvantages, distance learning

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: afzalliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + fikr, agar savol so'rasa)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of distance learning is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, distance learning also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: noaniq olmoshlar + birlik fe'l 2+ marta (Anyone can join… / Nobody checks… / Everyone has…)
answers: Namuna kirish (41 so'z): These days, a lot of young people take lessons on their laptops at home instead of travelling to a classroom. This way of studying has clear benefits, but it also has some serious drawbacks. This essay will look at both sides.

Namuna AD jadval: Afzalliklar — 1) flexible: anyone with an internet connection can join from home 2) recorded lessons: if someone misses a class, everything is online; Kamchiliklar — 1) self-discipline: nobody checks students at home 2) no face-to-face contact: teacher may not notice a confused student; no real experiment without a laboratory

Namuna insho (190 so'z) — kirish: These days, a lot of young people take lessons on their laptops at home instead of travelling to a classroom. This way of studying has clear benefits, but it also has some serious drawbacks. This essay will look at both sides.

Namuna insho — body 1: One major advantage of distance learning is that it is very flexible. Anyone with an internet connection can join a lesson from home. For example, a student in a small village does not need to travel to Tashkent. Another benefit is recorded lessons: if someone misses a class, everything is still available online.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, distance learning also has some drawbacks. Firstly, it needs a lot of self-discipline, because nobody checks what students are doing at home. For example, many teenagers play games during an online lesson, which is a serious distraction. Secondly, there is no face-to-face contact. If anyone is confused, the teacher may not notice it on a small screen. Also, nobody can do a real experiment without a laboratory.
Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, distance learning is flexible, but it needs self-discipline and cannot replace practical lessons. In my view, it works best together with real classes.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — Anyone can, someone misses, everything is, nobody checks, anyone is, nobody can (fe'l birlikda); bog'lovchilar — For example, Another benefit, On the other hand, Firstly, because, Secondly, In conclusion; mavzu so'zlari — flexible, internet connection, recorded lessons, self-discipline, face-to-face, distraction, experiment, laboratory
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 4-qator ("Pros and cons of distance learning."); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). PEER-AD (juftlik, Ha/Yo'q): 1) savol o'z so'zlari bilan? 2) afzallik va kamchilik alohida xatboshida? 3) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol? 4) 4+ bog'lovchi? 5) dars grammatikasi 2+? 6) 150+ so'z (sinfda kirish 35–45)? Namuna insho o'quvchiga uy inshosi tekshirilgandan keyin ko'rsatiladi.

reading.title: Al-Farabi — the Second Teacher
text: A. Abu Nasr al-Farabi was born around 870 in Farab (Otrar), a town on the Syr Darya. Nobody knows much about his childhood, but everyone agrees on one thing: he was one of the greatest minds of the Islamic Golden Age. In the Muslim world he is called "the Second Teacher" — the first was Aristotle.

B. Farabi probably studied in Central Asia first and then travelled to Baghdad, where anyone with talent could find teachers and books. There he studied logic and wrote commentaries on Aristotle. Later, Ibn Sina wrote that he had read Aristotle's Metaphysics forty times without understanding it, until a short book by Farabi made everything clear.

C. Farabi believed that nothing in science works without logic. In his book on the classification of the sciences, he tried to organise everything that was known at the time: language, logic, mathematics, music and physics. He also wrote about an ideal city, where everyone works together and people help each other to be happy.

D. He was also a musician: he wrote "The Great Book of Music", and some stories say he invented a musical instrument. Farabi died in Damascus around 950. Today a large university in Almaty has his name, and anyone who studies philosophy meets his ideas.

kahoot.q: ___ is at the door. Can you open it, please?
kahoot.explain: Tasdiq gap, noma'lum odam: someone (kimdir).

kahoot.q: I don't know ___ about nuclear physics.
kahoot.explain: Inkor gap (don't) → any-: anything. "don't know nothing" — ikki inkor, xato.

kahoot.q: Nobody ___ the answer.
kahoot.explain: nobody — inkor ma'no, fe'l tasdiq va birlik: Nobody knows.

kahoot.q: Everyone ___ ready for the experiment.
kahoot.explain: everyone — birlik fe'l oladi: Everyone is ready.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: I don't know nothing about DNA.
I don't know anything about DNA.
kahoot.explain: Ingliz tilida ikki inkor yo'q: I don't know anything / I know nothing.

kahoot.q: Would you like ___ to drink?
kahoot.explain: Taklifda (Would you like…?) some- ishlatiladi: something to drink.

kahoot.q: I left my notes ___ in the lab, but I can't remember where.
kahoot.explain: Tasdiq gap, noma'lum joy: somewhere (qayerdadir).

kahoot.q: "Hech kim javobni bilmaydi."
options: No one doesn't know the answer.
kahoot.explain: no one + tasdiq fe'l: No one knows. (doesn't qo'shilmaydi).

kahoot.q: NO- olmoshlari (nobody, nothing) bilan fe'l qanday bo'ladi?
kahoot.explain: no- ning o'zi inkor, fe'l tasdiq: Nothing matters. Nobody knows.

kahoot.q: Someone ___ called you twice.
kahoot.explain: someone — birlik: has called.

kahoot.q: There's ___ to sit. All the chairs are taken.
kahoot.explain: O'tirish uchun joy yo'q: nowhere (fe'l tasdiq: There's nowhere).

kahoot.q: ___ can join the science club — it's open to all.
kahoot.explain: Tasdiqda anybody = "har kim": Anybody can join.

kahoot.q: A scientist ___ an experiment in the lab.
kahoot.explain: conduct an experiment — tajriba o'tkazmoq.

kahoot.q: After analysing the data, we can ___ a conclusion.
kahoot.explain: draw a conclusion — xulosa chiqarmoq.

kahoot.q: An idea that scientists check with an experiment is a ___.
kahoot.explain: hypothesis — gipoteza, taxmin (sinab ko'riladigan g'oya).

kahoot.q: Facts that show something is true are called ___.
kahoot.explain: evidence — dalil.

kahoot.q: A fake pill given to some people in medical tests is a ___.
kahoot.explain: placebo — platsebo, soxta dori.

kahoot.q: When water gets hot, it turns into gas — it ___.
kahoot.explain: evaporate — bug'lanmoq. evaluate — baholamoq.

kahoot.q: A rainbow is a natural ___.
kahoot.explain: natural phenomenon — tabiiy hodisa.

kahoot.q: "plausible" nimani anglatadi?
kahoot.explain: plausible — ishonarli, mantiqiy (a plausible explanation).

listening.audios: Jony Academy original skripti — ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi (~2 daq). Kitob AUDIO 31–40 — ixtiyoriy, uyda.
intro: IELTS Listening Part 3 — multiple choice. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
You will hear a teacher and two students, Aziz and Lola, choosing a project for a school science fair.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, kalit so'zlarni belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: TEACHER: So, you need a project for the science fair. Has anyone got an idea?
AZIZ: Yes — a model volcano! We mix soda and vinegar, and it erupts.
LOLA: It's a bit messy, though.
TEACHER: That's not the problem. Everyone makes a volcano, so nobody will learn anything new. [Q1]
LOLA: What about plants? We could play music to them and see if they grow faster.
TEACHER: Someone did that last year.
AZIZ: Then let's test how the colour of light affects plant growth. Nobody has tried this before in our school. [Q2]
TEACHER: Good. Now form a hypothesis.
LOLA: Plants under blue light will grow faster than plants under red light.
TEACHER: Fine. Change only one variable — the colour. What do you need?
AZIZ: Three new lamps?
TEACHER: That's too expensive. We need something cheap.
LOLA: We already have seeds, so we can just buy coloured plastic sheets for the pots. [Q3]
TEACHER: Perfect. And how long will it take?
LOLA: Two weeks?
TEACHER: Nothing much happens in two weeks. Give it three. [Q4]
AZIZ: OK. Is there anything we can measure?
TEACHER: The height of each plant, every morning.
AZIZ: I can measure them every day.
TEACHER: It's better if everyone in the class takes a turn — then nobody gets bored. [Q5] Aziz, you'll analyse the data, and we'll draw a conclusion together.

3 What will the students buy? A) coloured plastic sheets B) new lamps C) seeds
4 How long will the experiment take? A) two weeks B) three weeks C) a month
5 Who will collect the data? A) Aziz B) Lola C) everyone in the class

class_ex.instr: Some people think governments should spend money on art galleries and museums; others think this money should be spent on hospitals and schools. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. — Sinfda bitta body paragraf, 70–90 so'z.
items: 1) Tur — discussion; bu paragraf — san'at uchun fikr.
2) Kalit so'zlar: governments, spend money, museums / hospitals and schools.
3) Reja: fikr → sabab → misol.
4) On the one hand, … / This is because … / For example, … / Therefore, …
class_ex.answers: Namuna (82 so'z): On the one hand, some people believe that governments should spend money on art galleries and museums. This is because every painting and artwork tells young people about their history. For example, Behzod's miniatures have survived for about five hundred years; people must have protected them very carefully. Without state money, many masterpieces could have disappeared. Moreover, a free gallery gives every family the chance to enjoy art, not only rich people. Therefore, spending on culture is not a waste of money.

reading.title: Kamoliddin Behzod — the miniature master of Herat
text: Kamoliddin Behzod was born in Herat in the middle of the 15th century, when Herat was the capital of the Timurid state and a great centre of culture. He lost his parents as a child, but he must have shown real talent early, because the poet and statesman Alisher Navoi became his patron. Behzod trained in the royal workshop, where he might have studied the work of older masters.

Behzod became one of the greatest masters of miniature painting in the East. His paintings are small — often the size of a book page — but they can't have been painted quickly: one picture may show dozens of people, each with a different face and emotion. He must have used a very fine brush for the smallest details. He often showed ordinary people at work — builders, servants, beggars — and not only kings.

In 1507 the Uzbek ruler Shaybani Khan took Herat. Later Behzod moved to Tabriz, where he became head of the royal library and its workshop. His students carried his style to other cities, including Bukhara.

Behzod died around 1535. Many works linked to his name are now kept in libraries and museums abroad, for example in London and Cairo. Some people say more of them should have stayed in Central Asia, but in the 16th century nobody thought about museums. Today the National Institute of Fine Arts and Design in Tashkent is named after him.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 2 — Matching. Write the correct letter A–F next to Paintings 1–5. One letter is not used.
You will hear a museum guide talking about five old miniature paintings.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): A–F bayonotlarni o'qing, kalit so'zlar tagiga chizing.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: GUIDE: Good morning and welcome to the miniature room. Nobody knows exactly how these five paintings were made, so a lot of what I say is a guess.

GUIDE: Painting one shows a garden party. Some visitors think it was painted in a hurry, but look at the tiny leaves — the artist can't have finished it quickly. The colours look as if they were mixed by candlelight: he must have worked at night. [Q1]
GUIDE: Painting two is a portrait of a young prince. There's a short poem in the corner, written for his birthday, so it might have been a gift from his teacher. [Q2]

GUIDE: Painting three shows a building site with forty workers. Experts first thought one master painted it alone. But the faces are in two different styles. He can't have done it by himself — his apprentices must have helped. [Q3]
GUIDE: Painting four is a hunting scene. It's a masterpiece, but we don't know who made it, because there's no name on it. The artist should have signed it! [Q4]

GUIDE: And finally, painting five — a horse in a storm. It looks as if it was painted in one afternoon — sorry, let me correct that — the sketch was quick, but the colours were added over many weeks. The line across it isn't part of the design: the paper was torn and repaired much later. [Q5]

tasks.title: Paintings 1–5 — matching (A–F)
tasks.instr: What does the guide say about each painting?
box: A — Several people worked on it.
B — It was damaged and later fixed.
C — It was completed in a very short time.
D — The painter was probably working when it was dark.
E — The painter did not put his name on it.
F — It was probably a present for someone.
items: Painting 1 — a garden party
Painting 2 — a young prince
Painting 3 — a building site
Painting 4 — a hunting scene
Painting 5 — a horse in a storm
tasks.note: Bitta harf ortiqcha; gid o'zini tuzatgan joyga e'tibor bering.

lessons.title: Adverbs of Degree
lessons.grammar_topic: DARAJA RAVISHLARI (very / too / enough / so…that / quite / rather / fairly / almost / absolutely / completely / utterly)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 6 – Adverbs of degree (11 qatorli jadval); HEALTH (65 so'z); Reading — Oksana Chusovitina (Jony Academy matni, moslashtirilgan); kitob Topic 26–28 uyga (ixtiyoriy); kitob AUDIO 51–55 (ixtiyoriy); SPEAKING/WRITING mavzusi — rahbar rejasi (IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 6-qator): "The advantages and disadvantages of using social media"
objectives: Daraja ravishlarini kuch bo'yicha joylashtira olish (fairly < quite < rather < very < absolutely).
too + adj + to V / adj + enough + to V / so + adj + that qoliplarini farqlab, gapda to'g'ri ishlata olish.
Kuchli (extreme) sifatlar bilan absolutely/completely, oddiy sifatlar bilan very ishlata olish.
Listening (IELTS Part 1): sport markaziga a'zolik suhbatidan formadagi 6 bo'shliqni (ism, yosh, vaqt, narx) to'ldira olish.

SPEAKING (IELTS Part 3): Social media: advantages and disadvantages — 4–5 savolga 3–4 gapli javob (javob → sabab → misol), daraja ravishlari (too / enough / so … that / quite / extremely / absolutely) bilan; WRITING: Social media: advantages and disadvantages — AD jadval sinfda, 150–200 so'zli insho uyda (W-B1-AD).
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 6 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.
CORE 20 varag'i — dars sahifasining Lug'at tabidan (PDF).
Kahoot: bu dars boshida o'ynalmaydi (Progress test 1); shu darsning Kahooti L07 boshida — 'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi (L06).
Progress test 1 (pt1) varaqlari + ustoz kaliti. Listening: skript ustozda (yashirin transcript), ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi; audio fayl kerak emas.
Writing/Speaking rubrikasi — shu darsdagi W-B1-AD va S-B1-P3 jadvallari (WRITING mashqidan keyin); juftlik tekshiruvi — PEER-AD (WRITING mashqi izohida).
timeline: Warm-up: tired → exhausted
Ustoz: "I'm tired. I'm very tired. I'm too tired to teach. I'm absolutely exhausted!" — o'quvchilar shkala tuzadi. "too" nima uchun boshqacha? (salbiy natija).
PROGRESS TEST 1 (pt1) — 1–5-darslar

Listening 6 · Reading 7 · Grammar 6 · Vocabulary 4 · Writing 12 — 40 ball; o'tish 28/40. Material va kalit — pt1 varag'i (listening skriptini ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi). Vocabulary bo'limida L05 Art CORE so'zlari (2+) — yozma normativ o'rniga. Tahlil — L07 da.
YANGI MAVZU: Adverbs of degree (very / too / enough / so…that)

10 daq taqdimot: jadval (kitob yoki grammar.formulas) + presentation 1, 3, 4, 6, 9-savol-javoblar juftlikda; fairly (nisbatan) < quite (ancha) < rather (ancha, ko'pincha salbiy) < very < absolutely. CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq amaliyot: 'Shkala' (og'zaki, 1 — namuna).
Lug'at: Health — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

10 so'z: well-being, fitness, balanced diet, lifestyle, allergy, injury, diagnosis, treatment, recovery, symptom — so'z → ma'no → dars grammatikasida 1 gap. Qolgan CORE va STRONG — flashcard (uyda), SUPER — ixtiyoriy.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 11 qator)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. Me'yor — normativ[2].
Sinf mashqlari: very / too / enough

very / too / enough — 6 daq (yakka, 1 — namuna; juftlikda tekshirish). ZAXIRA: so … that (4 daq), Kuchaytiruvchini tanlang (4 daq), Xatoni toping. Vaqt yetmasa: avval 'Xatoni toping', keyin 'Kuchaytiruvchini tanlang' tashlanadi — kuchlilarga yoki uyga.
Listening (IELTS Part 1): form completion
2 daq tayyorgarlik; 1-tinglash; 1 daq juftlikda solishtirish; 2-tinglash; 3 daq javoblar — ustoz dalil gapni skriptdan o'qiydi.
Reading: T/F/NG + summary completion
2 daq gist: 'Why is Oksana's career unusual?' (eight Olympic Games); 5 daq T/F/NG; 3 daq summary completion. 'ZAXIRA: Daraja ravishlarini toping' — kuchlilarga yoki uyga.
SPEAKING — Social media: advantages and disadvantages

1 daq Part 1 lead-in (2 savol, juftlikda) → 6 daq Part 3 juftlikda: A savol beradi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashadi; har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol (+ qarama-qarshi fikr) → 2 daq 2 o'quvchi sinf oldida bitta Part 3 savoliga javob beradi, ustoz S-B1-P3 bilan baholaydi → 1 daq feedback (1 kuchli tomon + 1 tuzatish + 1 foydali ibora).
WRITING — Social media: advantages and disadvantages
1 daq savol va 4 xatboshi rejasi (proyektorda) → 3 daq juftlikda AD jadval (2 + 2 g'oya, misol bilan, SPEAKING dan). Insho — uyda, MAJBURIY.
Uyga vazifa

MAJBURIY (~45 daq): HEALTH CORE 20 flashcard + 5 tarjima gapi + WRITING — Social media inshosi + SPEAKING ovozli 2 javob. IXTIYORIY: ovozli normativ, Speaking Part 2 (Health), Topic 26–28, jadval yoddan, ZAXIRA mashqlar.

intro: VERY — oddiy kuchaytirish: very tired. TOO — haddan tashqari, salbiy natija: too hot to go outside. ENOUGH — sifatdan keyin: warm enough to swim.
SO + adj + THAT + natija: He was so happy that he cried. (such + ot + that: such a good doctor that…)
FAIRLY — nisbatan (eng kuchsiz): fairly well; QUITE — ancha: quite interesting; RATHER — ancha, kutilganidan ko'p (ko'pincha salbiy): rather cold. ALMOST — deyarli: almost fell asleep.
Kuchli sifatlar (amazing, exhausted, freezing, furious) bilan very EMAS: absolutely amazing, completely empty, utterly disappointed.
formulas: It is too hot to go outside.
adj/adv + enough (+ to V) / enough + ot
He is fit enough to run a marathon. / We have enough vitamins.
U marafon yugurish uchun yetarlicha chiniqqan. / Vitaminlarimiz yetarli.
He was so happy that he cried.
U shunday baxtli ediki, yig'lab yubordi.
The movie was quite interesting. / It's rather cold. / She speaks fairly well. / I almost fell asleep.
Kino ancha qiziqarli edi. / Havo ancha sovuq. / U nisbatan yaxshi gapiradi. / Deyarli uxlab qoldim.
The view is absolutely amazing. / The house is completely empty. / He was utterly disappointed.
Manzara mutlaqo ajoyib. / Uy butunlay bo'sh. / Uning hafsalasi butunlay pir bo'ldi.
presentation: How are you feeling?
I'm quite tired, but not too tired to train.
Is she fit enough for the competition?
Yes, she's absolutely ready.
Was the doctor's advice useful?
It was so useful that I changed my whole diet.
Is it too late to start exercising at 40?
No, it's never too late.
How was the check-up?
Fairly quick — almost painless.
Is the gym warm enough in winter?
It's rather cold in the morning, but fine later.
Was he very ill?
He was completely exhausted after the flu.
Is junk food really that bad?
It's so bad that doctors call it a health risk.
Do you sleep enough?
Almost — six hours. Not quite enough.
Was Chusovitina's story surprising?
It was absolutely amazing — eight Olympic Games!
notes: enough: sifat/ravishdan KEYIN (good enough), otdan OLDIN (enough time).
too ≠ very: "very hot" (juda issiq, OK) — "too hot" (haddan tashqari, muammo).
Kuchli sifatlar: absolutely + amazing / exhausted / freezing / delicious / furious / terrified; very + oddiy sifat (tired, cold, good).
too / enough + for + kishi + to V (ega o'zi bajarmasa): The fracture was too serious for her to train.
CCQ: I'm too tired to teach. — Can I teach? (No) Is it a problem? (Yes)
CCQ: He's old enough to drive. — Can he drive? (Yes) Is he too young? (No)
CCQ: I was so tired that I slept. — Why did I sleep? (Because I was very tired) Which part is the result? (I slept)
CCQ: After the marathon I was absolutely exhausted. — Was I a little tired? (No, extremely tired)
mistakes: It's too hot today — I love it!
It's very hot today — I love it!
He is enough tall to play.
He is tall enough to play.
She was so tired for she slept.
She was so tired that she slept.
I almost never don't eat sugar.

how: CORE 20 — sog'liq va turmush tarzi (sinfda 10 tasi); STRONG — kasalliklar va jarohatlar; SUPER — davolash va sog'lom odat iboralari.
Har so'zga daraja ravishi bilan gap: "Sleep is absolutely essential." / "This diet is too strict to follow."
core: Sleep is absolutely essential for well-being.
Her fitness is so good that she can train for hours.
Uning jismoniy tayyorgarligi shunday yaxshiki, soatlab mashq qila oladi.
Hygiene is quite simple: wash your hands.
Good nutrition is very important for athletes.
Yaxshi oziqlanish sportchilar uchun juda muhim.
A balanced diet is fairly easy to plan.
Her lifestyle is so busy that she never rests.
Uning turmush tarzi shunchalik bandki, u hech qachon dam olmaydi.
His immunity was strong enough to fight the virus.
Uning immuniteti virusga qarshi kurashish uchun yetarlicha kuchli edi.
The vaccine was so effective that the disease almost disappeared.
Vaksina shunday samarali ediki, kasallik deyarli yo'qoldi.
Antibiotics are used far too often.
My allergy is rather bad in spring.
Prevention is almost always cheaper than treatment.
Oldini olish deyarli har doim davolashdan arzon.
The treatment was too expensive for many families.
Davolash ko'p oilalar uchun juda qimmat edi.
Her recovery was absolutely amazing — six weeks.
Uning sog'ayishi mutlaqo hayratlanarli edi — olti hafta.
The injury was so bad that she couldn't walk.
Jarohat shunday og'ir ediki, u yura olmadi.
Chronic diseases are very common after 50.
Surunkali kasalliklar 50 dan keyin juda keng tarqalgan.
His blood pressure is rather high.
Everyone should know enough first aid to help.
Har kim yordam berish uchun yetarlicha birinchi yordamni bilishi kerak.
strong: The fracture was too serious for her to train.
Sinish jiddiy bo'lgani uchun u mashq qila olmadi.
A sprain is quite painful but heals fast.
Cho'zilish ancha og'riqli, lekin tez bitadi.
The wound was deep enough to need stitches.
Yara tikish kerak bo'ladigan darajada chuqur edi.
Diabetes is very common in cities.
A stroke is always an emergency.
Obesity is a rather new problem here.
Semizlik bu yerda ancha yangi muammo.
Her asthma is too bad for her to stay in dusty rooms.
Astmasi og'ir bo'lgani uchun u changli xonalarda qola olmaydi.
Depression is so common that everyone should know the symptoms.
Depressiya shunchalik keng tarqalganki, hamma alomatlarini bilishi kerak.
Rehabilitation was quite slow after the operation.
Operatsiyadan keyin reabilitatsiya ancha sekin bo'ldi.
Dehydration is very dangerous in summer.
Malnutrition is almost gone in the region.
His cholesterol was far too high.
Uning xolesterini haddan tashqari yuqori edi.
The X-ray was quite clear: no fracture.
Rentgen ancha aniq edi: sinish yo'q.
The blood test was almost normal.
Athletes must stay hydrated — it's absolutely vital.
Sportchilar suv ichib turishi shart — bu mutlaqo hayotiy.
super: It's quite hard to eat healthily at university.
I almost completely avoid junk food now.
Endi zararli ovqatdan deyarli butunlay qochaman.
Doctors say we should limit sugar intake — it's far too high.
Shifokorlar shakar iste'molini cheklashimizni aytadi — u haddan tashqari yuqori.
Taking vitamins isn't enough without real food.
Haqiqiy ovqatsiz vitamin ichishning o'zi yetarli emas.
Regular exercise is absolutely the best medicine.
Muntazam mashq — mutlaqo eng yaxshi dori.
A cardio workout of 20 minutes is enough for beginners.
20 daqiqalik kardio yangi boshlovchilar uchun yetarli.
She has maintained a healthy weight for 30 years.
U 30 yildan beri sog'lom vaznni saqlab kelmoqda.
Get fresh air — you look rather pale.
Toza havoga chiq — ancha rangpar ko'rinasan.
Heart attacks are quite rare in young people.
Yurak xuruji yoshlarda ancha kam uchraydi.
Cancer treatment has become far more effective.
Too much medication can be dangerous.
Haddan tashqari ko'p dori xavfli bo'lishi mumkin.
The burn was too painful to ignore.
Kuyish e'tiborsiz qoldirib bo'lmas darajada og'riqli edi.
A sore throat is very common in winter.
Tomoq og'rig'i qishda juda keng tarqalgan.
His fever was high enough to call a doctor.
Uning isitmasi shifokor chaqirish uchun yetarlicha yuqori edi.
The flu was so bad that the school closed.
Gripp shunday yomon ediki, maktab yopildi.
Chusovitina is the only gymnast who has competed at eight Olympic Games.
Chusovitina — sakkizta Olimpiada o'yinlarida qatnashgan yagona gimnastikachi.
Most gymnasts retire quite young because the sport is very hard on the body.
Ko'pchilik gimnastikachilar ancha yosh sportni tark etadi, chunki bu sport tanaga juda og'ir.
normativ: Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan o'lchanadigan me'yor; bajarsa jurnalga '+' va coin, bajarmasa keyingi darsgacha qayta topshiradi.
Og'zaki: CORE 20 + tarjima, 1.5 daqiqa (ilovada, L07 gacha) — 1 coin.
Yozma (L07 boshida): 20 so'z, 4 daqiqa; 17/20+ — 2 coin. STRONG/SUPER — +2 / +3 coin.

class_ex.title: Progress Test 1 — 1–5-darslar: ustoz uchun o'tkazish tartibi va ball jadvali
class_ex.instr: Test 6-darsda Warm-up (4 daq) dan keyin yoziladi: 4-daqiqadan 39-daqiqagacha, 35 daqiqa, yakka, qog'ozda. Jami 40 ball: Listening 5 · Reading 5 · Grammar 10 · Vocabulary 8 · Writing 12. Qamrov — faqat 1–5-darslar (12 zamon, used to / be used to, question tags, indefinite pronouns, modal + have + V3; Learning, Technology, Business, Science, Art CORE lug'ati). Natija tahlili — 7-darsda ('PROGRESS TEST 1 tahlili', 8 daq).
items: 1. Darsdan 1 kun oldin: o'quvchi varag'ini har o'quvchiga bittadan chop eting — unda 1–5-bo'limlar (Listening formasi, Reading matni va savollari, Grammar, Vocabulary, Writing savoli va reja) bor. Listening skripti, kalitlar, W-B1 rubrikasi, namuna paragraf, zaxira writing mavzusi va ball varag'i FAQAT ustozda, alohida varaqda.

2. Proyektor: test davomida faqat taymer (35:00) va bo'lim vaqtlari chiqariladi: Listening 0–6 · Reading 6–13 · Grammar 13–19 · Vocabulary 19–23 · Writing 23–35. Savollar, skript va kalit proyektorga CHIQARILMAYDI. Telefonlar qutiga yig'iladi, lug'at va daftarlar sumkaga.
3. Tarqatish (Warm-up oxirida, 1 daqiqa): varaqni yuzini pastga qilib tarqating; o'quvchi ism-familiya, guruh va sanani yozadi. 'Start' deganda hamma varaqni ochadi va taymer yoqiladi.

4. 0–6-daqiqa — LISTENING (hamma birga, BIRINCHI bo'lib): 30 soniya — o'quvchilar formani o'qiydi; ustoz 'Listening skripti' ni ikki ovozda (RECEPTIONIST — oddiy, STUDENT — sal balandroq) o'rtacha tezlikda o'qiydi (~1 daq 10 s); 10 soniya pauza; ikkinchi marta o'qiydi; 30 soniya — javoblarni tekshirish. Skript o'quvchiga ko'rsatilmaydi; so'zlar alohida takrorlanmaydi va harf-harf aytilmaydi (skriptdagi R-A-K-H-I-M-O-V-A dan tashqari).

5. 6–35-daqiqa — qolgan bo'limlar o'z tezligida. 13-, 19-, 23-daqiqalarda keyingi bo'limni ovoz chiqarib eslating ('Now start Grammar', 'Now Vocabulary', 'Now start Writing — 12 minutes'); 33-daqiqada '2 minutes left' deng. Savollarga javob tushuntirilmaydi — faqat topshiriq shartini qayta o'qib berasiz.
6. 35-daqiqada varaqlar yig'iladi. Shu darsda kalit KO'RSATILMAYDI — dars YANGI MAVZU bilan davom etadi.

7. Tekshirish (7-darsgacha): Listening, Reading, Grammar, Vocabulary — har to'g'ri javob 1 ball. Listening: 1-savolda (familiya) imlo aniq bo'lishi shart; boshqa javoblarda bitta harf xatosi — 0.5; ikki so'zdan ortiq (masalan, 'quarter to ten') — 0. Reading: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN yoki T / F / NG — to'liq ball; YES / NO — 0. Grammar: faqat harf yoki to'g'ri shakl — 1 ball; ikki variant belgilangan — 0. Vocabulary: bitta harf imlo xatosi — 0.5; boxdan tashqari so'z — 0. Writing — W-B1 rubrikasi (4 mezon × 0–3 = 12). Kalitdagi muqobil javoblar ham to'liq ball.

8. Natija tizimga bo'limlar kesimida kiritiladi: L, R, G, V, W alohida + jami; foiz = jami × 2.5. Yarim ball yaxlitlanmaydi (27.5 — 28 dan kam). Keyingi qadam quyidagi jadval (answers) bo'yicha belgilanadi.

9. 7-dars — 'PROGRESS TEST 1 tahlili' (8 daq): tekshirilgan varaqlar qaytariladi; ustoz har bo'limdan eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 bandni doskada ko'rsatadi, o'quvchilar o'z varag'ida tuzatadi (4 daq); writing bo'yicha 2 ta umumiy xato va namuna paragrafdan 1 ta yaxshi gap (2 daq); QAYTA ISHLASH o'quvchilarga individual vazifa, O'TMADI o'quvchilarga qayta topshirish sanasi e'lon qilinadi (2 daq). Tahlildan keyin varaqlar ustozga qaytariladi.

10. Qayta topshirish (O'TMADI, 7 kun ichida, dars vaqtidan tashqari, 22 daqiqa): shu faylning 'Qayta topshirish varag'i' (Grammar 10 + Vocabulary 8, boshqa tartibda, 10 daq) + 'Zaxira Writing mavzusi' (12 daq). Listening va Reading qayta yozilmaydi — ularning birinchi balli saqlanadi; yangi jami = eski L + R + yangi G + V + W.
answers: 34–40 ball (≥85%) — O'TDI, 3 coin → 7-darsdan odatdagidek davom etadi.
28–33 ball (70–84%) — O'TDI, 2 coin → davom etadi; eng past bo'limi bo'yicha uyga 1 ta qo'shimcha mashq (shu darsning ZAXIRA mashqlaridan).

20–27 ball (50–69%) — QAYTA ISHLASH, coin yo'q → xato qilingan bo'limlar bo'yicha individual uy vazifasi (har xato band uchun shu darsning 'Xatoni toping' / lug'at mashqidan 2 ta o'xshash gap) + 7-darsdagi tahlil bosqichida 5 savollik og'zaki qayta tekshiruv: ustoz o'quvchi xato qilgan bandlardan 5 tasini og'zaki so'raydi (grammatika — to'g'ri shaklni aytadi, lug'at — so'z va misol gap), 4/5+ — 'tuzatildi', 3/5 va kam — keyingi darsda yana 5 savol; natija jurnalga yoziladi.

0–19 ball (<50%) — O'TMADI, coin yo'q → shu kuni ota-onaga xabar (sabab va qayta topshirish sanasi bilan); 7 kun ichida qayta topshirish: Grammar va Vocabulary bo'limlari boshqa tartibda ('Qayta topshirish varag'i') + zaxira writing mavzusi. Yangi jami ≥28 — O'TDI (coin berilmaydi); yana <28 — rahbar bilan suhbat va 2 ta qo'shimcha mashg'ulot.
WRITING QOIDASI: Writing bo'limidan 12 dan 4 dan kam (0–3) olgan o'quvchi umumiy natijadan qat'i nazar writing'ni qayta yozadi — zaxira mavzu, 12 daqiqa, 7 kun ichida (O'TDI bo'lsa ham).
Misol 1: L 4 · R 4 · G 8 · V 7 · W 9 = 32 (80%) → O'TDI, 2 coin.
Misol 2: L 3 · R 2 · G 6 · V 5 · W 8 = 24 (60%) → QAYTA ISHLASH: Reading va Grammar bo'yicha individual vazifa + 7-darsda 5 savollik og'zaki qayta tekshiruv.
Misol 3: L 5 · R 4 · G 9 · V 8 · W 3 = 29 (72.5%) → O'TDI (2 coin), lekin W 3 < 4 → writing zaxira mavzuda qayta yoziladi.
Misol 4: L 2 · R 2 · G 4 · V 3 · W 5 = 16 (40%) → O'TMADI: ota-onaga xabar, 7 kun ichida G + V (boshqa tartib) + zaxira writing; L 2 va R 2 saqlanadi.

items: 1. RECEPTIONIST: Good morning, City Art Gallery. How can I help you?
2. STUDENT: Hello. I'd like to book tickets for the Art and Technology exhibition. It opens this Saturday, doesn't it?
3. RECEPTIONIST: Yes, it does. How many tickets do you need?
4. STUDENT: Four. I'm coming with three classmates from my English course.
5. RECEPTIONIST: Can I have your surname, please?
6. STUDENT: Rakhimova. That's R-A-K-H-I-M-O-V-A.
7. RECEPTIONIST: Thank you. An adult ticket is sixty thousand som, but students pay forty-five thousand.
8. STUDENT: Great, we all have student cards.

9. RECEPTIONIST: With a student ticket, you can also visit one special room. The first one shows paintings made by artificial intelligence. The second is a virtual reality room, where you can walk inside a famous painting.
10. STUDENT: We have already seen a lot of AI pictures online, so the virtual reality room, please.
11. RECEPTIONIST: Good choice. Someone from our team will meet your group at the main entrance, not at the ticket office.
