class_ex.title: 2. Reading — TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN (5 × 1 = 5 ball, 7 daq)
class_ex.instr: Read the text "The Painting Under the Painting". Do the statements agree with the information in the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. (Matnni o'qing. TRUE — matnda shunday yozilgan; FALSE — matnda aksi yozilgan; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot yo'q.)
box: For many years, visitors to a small city museum used to walk past a dark portrait of an old man without looking at it twice. Nobody thought it was special. Then, in 2023, a team of young researchers from a local university decided to study it with X-ray cameras. They had been looking for a simple project for their students, but they found something much bigger.

Under the portrait, there was another picture: a bright landscape with mountains and a river. The scientists believe the artist must have painted the landscape first and then covered it a few years later. Why would anyone hide a finished artwork? One researcher thinks the painter might have needed a new canvas and had no money to buy one. Another says he may have simply disliked the first painting.

The students were not used to working with such expensive equipment, so at first they made several mistakes with the data. However, they repeated every experiment three times to check the accuracy of their results.

Today the museum is showing both images side by side: the real portrait and a digital copy of the hidden landscape. By next summer, more than ten thousand people will have visited the exhibition. The team is now planning to examine everything else in the museum's collection.
items: 1. Before 2023, most visitors paid little attention to the portrait of the old man.
2. The researchers started the project because they wanted to find a hidden painting.
3. The mountains in the hidden landscape are near the museum's city.
4. The researchers agree about why the landscape was covered.
5. Students can visit the exhibition for free.
why: "used to walk past … without looking at it twice. Nobody thought it was special."
"They had been looking for a simple project for their students" — yashirin rasmni qidirmagan, tasodifan topgan.
Landshaftda tog' va daryo bor, lekin ular qayerdaligi aytilmagan.
"One researcher thinks … Another says …" — fikrlari har xil (might have / may have).
Ko'rgazma narxi yoki chegirma haqida hech narsa yo'q.
class_ex.note: Original matn, 217 so'z; muzey va qahramonlar to'qima. Matnda 1–5-darslar grammatikasi: used to, had been looking, nobody / anyone / everything, must / might / may have + V3, were not used to working, will have visited. Har javob — 1 ball.

why: 1-dars: 'be quiet' — hozir, ayni paytda davom etayotgan ish → Present Continuous.
1-dars: 'By the end of this year' + 'for five years' — kelajakdagi nuqtagacha davom etgan jarayon → Future Perfect Continuous.
2-dars: o'tgan odat, hozir yo'q → used to + V1 (watch). be used to dan keyin V-ing kelardi.
2-dars: be used to (o'rganib qolgan) + V-ing → making.
3-dars: tasdiq gap, Past Simple (went) → inkor tag didn't it.
3-dars: No one — inkor ma'noli → tasdiq tag; no one/everyone uchun tagda 'they' → fe'l ham 'were' bo'ladi → were they.
4-dars: hammasi unutgan → nobody (fe'l tasdiq shaklda: remembers). anybody tasdiq gapda 'hech kim' ma'nosini bermaydi.
4-dars: everyone + birlik fe'l → has (to present).
5-dars: imkonsiz, ishonch bilan inkor taxmin → can't have + V3.
5-dars: o'tmishdagi afsus (qilmagan ishim) → should have + V3.

class_ex.title: 5. Writing — IELTS Task 2 uslubida bitta paragraf (12 ball, W-B1 rubrikasi, 12 daq)
class_ex.instr: Write ONE paragraph (80–100 words) to answer the question. Give your opinion, explain it and give an example. (Savolga BITTA paragraf yozing, 80–100 so'z: fikringiz, sababi va misol. Oxirida so'z sonini yozing.)
items: 1. Question: Some people think that students learn more from technology than from teachers. Do you agree or disagree?
2. Plan: Topic sentence (your opinion) → Reason (because …) → Example (For example, …) → Concluding sentence (Therefore / In conclusion, …).

3. Use: at least 3 linking words (because, however, for example, therefore) and 3 words from Lessons 1–5 (e.g. research, critical thinking, study habits, artificial intelligence, user-friendly, digital transformation).
4. Use at least 2 structures from Lessons 1–5 (e.g. used to / be used to, a perfect tense, should have / could have + V3). Write the number of words at the end.
answers: 1. NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, W-B1 ≈ 11–12 ball, 99 so'z): In my opinion, students learn more when technology and teachers work together, but teachers are still more important. Technology is useful because it gives us quick access to information. For example, I used to spend hours in the library, but now I can find research online in minutes. However, an app cannot explain why my answer is wrong or teach me critical thinking. Last year I tried to learn maths with videos and kept making the same mistakes, so I should have asked my teacher earlier. Therefore, technology is a helpful tool, but it cannot replace a good teacher.

2. Namunada tuzilma: pozitsiya (In my opinion … teachers are still more important) → sabab (because it gives us quick access) → misol (For example, I used to …) → qarshi fikr (However, an app cannot …) → shaxsiy misol (should have asked) → xulosa (Therefore …). Bog'lovchilar: but, because, for example, however, so, therefore.
3. Namunada lug'at: research, critical thinking (L01), technology (L02 mavzusi); grammatika: used to + V1 (L02), should have + V3 (L05), Present Simple / Past Simple (L01).

4. Baholash: W-B1 rubrikasi (keyingi jadval) — 4 mezon × 0–3 = 12. 54 so'zdan kam (talabning 2/3 qismi) — Task Response ko'pi bilan 1; 20 so'zdan kam yoki mavzudan tashqari — Task Response 0. Bitta paragraf bo'lgani uchun Coherence mezonida 'kirish – asosiy qism – xulosa' = topic sentence – sabab/misol – concluding sentence deb baholanadi. Writing 0–3 → qayta yozadi (zaxira mavzu).

class_ex.instr: Write ONE paragraph (80–100 words) to answer the question. Give your opinion, explain it and give an example. (Savolga BITTA paragraf yozing, 80–100 so'z: fikringiz, sababi va misol. Oxirida so'z sonini yozing.) — O'TMADI yoki Writing 0–3 olgan o'quvchilar uchun, 12 daqiqa.
items: 1. Question: Some people say that art lessons are a waste of time for students who want to work in business or science. Do you agree or disagree?
2. Plan: Topic sentence (your opinion) → Reason (because …) → Example (For example, …) → Concluding sentence.
3. Use at least 3 linking words, 3 words from Lessons 1–5 (e.g. creativity, imagination, entrepreneur, experiment, design) and 2 structures from Lessons 1–5.
answers: 1. NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, 98 so'z): I disagree with the idea that art lessons are a waste of time for future business people and scientists. Firstly, drawing and painting develop creativity and imagination, which every entrepreneur needs to find ideas for a product. Secondly, art teaches students to look at details, and this skill is important when you conduct an experiment. For example, my uncle, who runs a business, has used his design skills to create his own brand logo. He could have paid a designer, but he did it himself. In conclusion, art lessons are useful for everyone, not only for future artists.

2. Namunada: pozitsiya (I disagree) → 1-sabab (Firstly … creativity and imagination) → 2-sabab (Secondly … conduct an experiment) → misol (For example, my uncle … has used) → could have + V3 → xulosa (In conclusion). Lug'at: creativity, imagination, painting, design (L05), entrepreneur, runs a business (L03), conduct an experiment (L04). class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Social media: advantages and disadvantages
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ daraja ravishi (too / enough / so … that / quite / extremely / absolutely).
items: Part 1: Which social media apps do you use most?
Part 1: How much time do you spend on social media every day?
Part 3: Why is social media so popular with teenagers?
Part 3: How can social media help students or small businesses?
Part 3: Can using social media too much be harmful to people's health — for example, sleep or mood?
Part 3: Why is it so easy to believe fake news online?
Part 3: Should there be an age limit for using social media?
answers: I use Telegram and Instagram most. Telegram is absolutely essential for my school chats, and Instagram is quite fun because I follow football pages and my friends.
About two hours, which is rather too much. On school days I'm so busy that I only check it in the evening, but at weekends I spend longer online.

I think the main reason is that it's extremely easy to stay in touch with friends. Teenagers want to know what their classmates are doing. For example, in my class we have a Telegram group, and if you're not in it, you miss absolutely everything. Also, short videos are so entertaining that it's hard to stop watching.

It can help them quite a lot. Students can find free lessons and ask teachers questions in online groups. For small businesses it's even more useful, because advertising is too expensive for many of them. For example, my aunt sells homemade cakes in Chilonzor, and she gets almost all her orders through Instagram.

Yes, definitely. If people scroll late at night, they don't get enough sleep, and the next day they feel completely exhausted. It can also affect their well-being, because they compare their lives with other people's perfect photos. For example, my cousin felt rather unhappy until she started to use her phone less.

I think it's because fake news is often so shocking that people share it immediately, without checking. Also, many users aren't careful enough — they trust a post if lots of people like it. For example, last year a false story about school holidays spread on Telegram, and almost everyone in my mahalla believed it.

In my view, yes, there should be. Children under thirteen are too young to understand the risks, such as talking to strangers. On the other hand, a strict ban is rather hard to control, because children can easily lie about their age. So overall, I'd say parents should check their children's accounts.
class_ex.note: ICQ: Necha gapda javob berasiz? (3–4) — Misol kerakmi? (Ha). Gap boshlanmalari: Well, I think… / The main advantage is that… / On the other hand, … / For example, … / So overall, … Health CORE so'zlari (well-being, lifestyle, symptom) tabiiy tushsa — qo'shimcha plyus. Baholash — S-B1-P3 (pastdagi jadval). Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 6-qator ("The advantages and disadvantages of using social media"); savollar va namunalar — Jony Academy, original.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Social media: advantages and disadvantages
class_ex.instr: Social media has become part of everyday life for millions of people. What are the advantages and disadvantages of using social media? Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval; uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: advantages/disadvantages (afzalliklar va kamchiliklar; fikr so'ralmagan — ikkala tomonni teng yoriting)
2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: social media, everyday life, millions of people, advantages, disadvantages

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: afzalliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + fikr, agar savol so'rasa)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of … is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, … also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: daraja ravishlari (too / enough / so … that / very / extremely / fairly) 2+ marta
answers: Namuna kirish (28 so'z): Millions of people, both young and old, use apps like Telegram and Instagram every day. Social media brings some clear benefits, but it also has several serious drawbacks.

Namuna AD jadval: Afzalliklar — 1) aloqa juda oson va arzon (chet eldagi qarindoshlar bilan bepul video qo'ng'iroq); 2) o'qish va biznes uchun foydali (bepul onlayn darslar; Samarqanddagi tort do'koni reklamasiz mijoz topadi); Kamchiliklar — 1) kechasi uzoq onlayn o'tirish → uyqu yetmaydi (sinfdoshlar yarim tungacha video ko'radi, darsda uxlab qoladi); 2) yolg'on yangiliklar juda tez tarqaladi, odamlar tekshirmay ishonadi (non narxi haqidagi yolg'on xabar bir kechada minglab odamga yetadi).

Namuna insho (187 so'z) — kirish: Millions of people, both young and old, use apps like Telegram and Instagram every day. Social media brings some clear benefits, but it also has several serious drawbacks.

Namuna insho — body 1: One major advantage of social media is that it makes communication extremely easy and cheap. For example, families with relatives working abroad can see them on video calls for free. Another benefit is that it is very useful for learning and business. Students can watch free lessons online. Small businesses, such as a cake shop in Samarkand, can find customers without expensive adverts.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, social media has some drawbacks. Firstly, many teenagers stay online too late, so they do not get enough sleep. For example, some of my classmates watch videos until after midnight and fall asleep in lessons. Secondly, fake news spreads so quickly that people believe it without checking. For instance, a false message about bread prices can reach thousands of people overnight.

Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, social media is a fairly useful tool for communication, learning and business, but it can also harm our sleep and spread false stories, so we should use it wisely.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — extremely easy, very useful, too late, enough sleep, so quickly that, fairly useful; bog'lovchilar — For example, Another benefit is, On the other hand, Firstly, Secondly, For instance, so, but, In conclusion; mavzu so'zlari — social media, communication, video calls, online, customers, adverts, stay online, fake news, false message, false stories.
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 6-qator ("The advantages and disadvantages of using social media"); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). PEER-AD (juftlik, Ha/Yo'q): 1) savol o'z so'zlari bilan? 2) afzallik va kamchilik alohida xatboshida? 3) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol? 4) 4+ bog'lovchi? 5) dars grammatikasi 2+? 6) 150+ so'z (test darsi: sinfda faqat AD jadval, insho uyda)? Test darsi: sinfda faqat AD jadval (3 daq), insho — uyda MAJBURIY. Namuna insho o'quvchiga uy inshosi tekshirilgandan keyin ko'rsatiladi.

answers: A healthy habit I have is walking to school every morning. I started it about two years ago, when a doctor told me that my fitness was not good enough. reading.title: Oksana Chusovitina — the gymnast who is never too old
text: Oksana Chusovitina was born in 1975 in Bukhara. Gymnasts usually retire at about 20, because the sport is so hard on the body that almost nobody can continue longer. Oksana has competed at eight Olympic Games — from Barcelona 1992 to Tokyo 2020 (held in 2021) — and that is absolutely unique in the history of the sport.

She won an Olympic gold medal in 1992, when she was only 17. Then she married, had a son, and kept training. In 2002 her son Alisher was diagnosed with leukaemia, a form of cancer. The treatment in Germany was far too expensive for the family, so Oksana made a decision: she would compete for prize money in every competition she could. She competed for Germany for several years, and Alisher recovered completely.

At the London Olympics in 2012 she was 37 — old enough to be the mother of the other gymnasts. In Tokyo, at 46, she was still fit enough to compete on the vault. Doctors say that a long career in sport needs quite simple things: a balanced diet, enough sleep, regular exercise and very little junk food. Gymnastics is very tiring for the body, but her motivation was strong enough to keep her in the sport for three decades.

In 2013 she started competing for Uzbekistan again. In Tokyo, the other gymnasts and judges stood up and applauded when she finished. For many young gymnasts, her story shows that it is never too late to follow a dream.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 1 — form completion. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear a phone call between a receptionist at a sports centre and a teenager who wants to become a member.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (ism, raqam, vaqt, ot) belgilang.
Ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi: 1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: RECEPTIONIST: Good afternoon, Green Park Sports Centre. How can I help?
AZIZ: Hi. I'd like to become a member. I want to improve my fitness and my lifestyle.
RECEPTIONIST: Great. Your name, please?
AZIZ: Aziz Karimov. That's K-A-R-I-M-O-V. [Q1]
RECEPTIONIST: And how old are you?
AZIZ: I'm fifteen — sorry, sixteen. My birthday was last week. [Q2]
RECEPTIONIST: OK. The weights room is only for adults, so you're not old enough for that, but you can join our young members' programme.
RECEPTIONIST: Any health problems? An injury or an allergy?
AZIZ: No allergy, but I've got asthma. [Q3] It isn't very bad, but running outside in winter is too hard for me.
RECEPTIONIST: No problem. Our trainers plan safe workouts and help with injury prevention. When would you like to train? We open at six in the morning.
AZIZ: Six is too early for me! I'm so busy with school that I can only come in the evening. Maybe half past five? Actually, no — seven o'clock is better, after my English class. [Q4]
RECEPTIONIST: Seven is fine. The monthly fee for young members is 250,000 som.
AZIZ: Hmm, that's quite expensive.
RECEPTIONIST: With a student card, it's only 200,000. [Q5]
AZIZ: Great, I've got one.

RECEPTIONIST: Your trainer is Mr Rustamov — oh, sorry, he's on holiday this month. It'll be Ms Nodira Saidova. S-A-I-D-O-V-A. [Q6] She's absolutely brilliant with beginners and gives advice on a balanced diet too.
AZIZ: Am I fit enough to start now?
RECEPTIONIST: Of course. Everyone is fit enough to start slowly. See you on Monday!
[Ustoz uchun] Chalg'itgichlar: fifteen → sixteen (Q2); half past five → seven (Q4); 250,000 → 200,000 (Q5); Mr Rustamov → Ms Saidova (Q6).

intro: HOWEVER / NEVERTHELESS / STILL — "biroq, shunga qaramay": yangi gap boshida, vergul bilan.
ON THE OTHER HAND / IN CONTRAST — ikki tomon yoki ikki narsa farqi, yangi gap boshida.
WHEREAS / WHILE — bitta gap ichida ikki farqli fakt.
YET — "ammo", but dan rasmiyroq: "…, yet …".
formulas: The test was difficult. However, I passed it.
Test qiyin edi. Biroq men undan o'tdim.
Gap 1. Nevertheless, gap 2. / Gap 1. Still, gap 2.
He was tired. Nevertheless, he continued working. / It was raining. Still, they went for a walk.
U charchagan edi. Shunga qaramay, ishlashda davom etdi. / Yomg'ir yog'ayotgan edi. Shunga qaramay, sayrga chiqishdi.
Gap 1. On the other hand, gap 2.
Living in a city is convenient. On the other hand, it can be noisy.
Shaharda yashash qulay. Boshqa tomondan, shovqinli bo'lishi mumkin.
She is very shy. In contrast, her brother is outgoing.
U juda tortinchoq. Aksincha, ukasi kirishimli.
She enjoys classical music, whereas he prefers rock. / Some people like coffee, while others prefer tea.
Qiz klassik musiqani yoqtiradi, yigit esa rokni afzal ko'radi. / Ba'zilar qahvani yoqtiradi, boshqalar esa choyni.
She is smart, yet she often makes mistakes.
U aqlli, ammo tez-tez xato qiladi.
presentation: Is travelling abroad expensive?
Yes. However, it is worth every penny.
Do you prefer the mountains or the sea?
I love the mountains, whereas my sister prefers the beach.
Was the hotel good?
The room was small. Nevertheless, the staff were wonderful.
Is Samarkand better than Bukhara?
Samarkand is grander. On the other hand, Bukhara is quieter.
Did the trip go well?
The flight was delayed, yet we arrived on time.
Is package tourism good for Uzbekistan?
Package tourists stay briefly. In contrast, backpackers stay much longer.
Why did Babur leave Fergana?
He lost his kingdom. Still, he never gave up.
Do tourists like Uzbek food?
Most love it, while some find it too heavy.
Is the visa process difficult?
It used to be. However, now it takes five minutes online.
Is it worth visiting Khiva in summer?
It's very hot. Nevertheless, the old city is unforgettable.
notes: However — gapning boshida (However, …) yoki o'rtasida (…, however, …); "but" bilan bir gapda ishlatilmaydi.
whereas/while — faqat ikki fakt farqi, sabab emas.
Writing Task 2: har paragrafda kamida bitta contrast bog'lovchi: "On the one hand, … On the other hand, …"
CCQ: Tashkent is big, whereas Bukhara is small. — Two different things? (Yes) One sentence? (Yes)
CCQ: It rained. However, we went out. — Surprising? (Yes) Did the rain stop us? (No)
CCQ: It was cold, yet we swam. — Comma after 'yet'? (No)
mistakes: She likes tea, however he likes coffee.
She likes tea. However, he likes coffee. / She likes tea, whereas he likes coffee.
However — yangi gap; bitta gapda whereas.
She likes coffee, whereas he likes tea.
It was cold, yet, we went out.
It was cold, yet we went out.

items: Part 1: Do you like travelling?
Part 1: Do you prefer the mountains or the sea?
Part 1: How do people usually travel in your city?
Part 1: Where did you go last summer?
Part 2 card: Describe a trip that was different from what you expected. You should say: where you went / what you expected / what actually happened — and explain how you felt about it.
Part 3: Is it better to travel alone or with a group?
Part 3: How has tourism changed Uzbekistan?
answers: Yes, I do. I don't travel often. However, every trip teaches me something new.
I prefer the mountains, whereas my parents love the sea. The mountains are cooler in summer.
Most people use the metro or buses. Taxis are faster. On the other hand, they cost much more.
Last summer I went to Chimgan with my family. It was a short trip, yet it was really relaxing.

I'd like to talk about a trip to Khiva with my classmates last spring. Before the trip, I expected a boring, dusty town with a few old buildings. However, the reality was completely different. The old city, Itchan Kala, felt like a living museum, and craftsmen carved wooden doors in front of us. The weather was very hot. Nevertheless, we walked for hours because every street was interesting. My friends loved the souvenirs, whereas I enjoyed the evening view from the city walls. I felt surprised and happy, and now Khiva is my favourite destination.
Travelling alone gives you freedom. On the other hand, a group is safer and cheaper, so beginners should travel with friends.
Tourism has brought new hotels and jobs to Samarkand and Bukhara. However, some old areas have become crowded, whereas small towns still get few visitors.

class_ex.title: Writing (IELTS Task 2): discussion — Writing 3
class_ex.instr: Some people think that tourists should only visit famous places such as Samarkand and Bukhara, while others believe that small towns and villages are more interesting to explore. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write 180–200 words. — Sinfda: reja + kirish paragrafi (40–50 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 180–200 so'z.
items: 1) Savol turi: discussion + opinion.
2) Kalit so'zlar: famous places, small towns and villages, both views, your opinion.
3) Reja: Body 1 — mashhur joylar (fikr + sabab + misol), Body 2 — kichik shahar va qishloqlar (fikr + sabab + misol); Xulosa — fikr.
4) Boshlanmalar: 'Some people…, whereas others…', 'On the other hand, …', 'In my opinion, …'
answers: Namuna kirish (44 so'z): Every year, thousands of tourists come to Uzbekistan, but they choose different routes. Some believe that famous cities like Samarkand and Bukhara are enough, whereas others think that small towns and villages are more exciting. In my opinion, a good trip should include both.

Namuna reja: Body 1 — mashhur joylar: Registon va Ark kabi tarixiy yodgorliklar, gidli sayr, qulay mehmonxona va transport; however: odam ko'p, narx baland, sayohat 'rasmga tushish'ga aylanadi; Body 2 — kichik shahar va qishloqlar: Nurota, Boysun, Chimyon atrofidagi qishloqlar — mahalliy oilalar, uy taomi, hunarmandlar, tabiat; on the other hand: yo'l yomon, mehmonxona kam, inglizcha biladiganlar kam; Xulosa — fikr (In contrast bilan): ikkalasini birlashtirish — 2 kun Samarqand, 1 kun yaqin qishloq.
class_ex.note: Tekshirish: W-B1 rubrika (L01), sinfda juftlik peer-b1 varag'i bilan; ustoz 2 ta ishni doskada ko'rsatadi.

reading.title: Babur — the king who lost everything, yet wrote it all down
text: A. Zahiriddin Muhammad Babur was born in 1483 in Andijan. When his father died in 1494, the young Babur became the ruler of Fergana; he was only about twelve. However, his uncles and neighbours wanted his land, and by his early twenties he had lost Fergana, won Samarkand twice and lost it twice. Many people would have given up. Babur, nevertheless, kept moving.

B. In 1504 he crossed the mountains with a small group of followers and took Kabul. It was a small, poor city, whereas Samarkand had been the jewel of Asia. Still, Kabul became his home for more than twenty years. He planted gardens, wrote poems and studied the land.
C. Then, in 1526, he led an expedition to India and defeated a much larger army at Panipat. He became the first Mughal emperor, and his descendants ruled India for about 300 years.

D. Today Babur is also famous for his memoir, the "Baburnama". Kings usually praised themselves. In contrast, Babur wrote about his mistakes, his fears and his homesickness with great honesty. He described the cities, fruits, animals and rivers he saw, so the book is like a travel guide to Central Asia and India in the 16th century. He wrote it in Chagatai Turkic, the language of Navoi, yet it has been translated into many languages.

E. He died in Agra in 1530, only four years after his victory. He was rich and powerful. On the other hand, he was homesick to the end. In the Baburnama he writes that no melons compared to those of Fergana.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 2 — sentence completion. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear a tour guide talking about a two-day trip to Samarkand and Bukhara.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (vaqt, raqam, ot) belgilang.

transcript: GUIDE: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Silk Way Travel. I'm Dilnoza, your guide on our two-day tour of Samarkand and Bukhara. Here is the itinerary.
GUIDE: We meet at Tashkent railway station on Saturday at seven o'clock — sorry, at a quarter past seven [Q1].
GUIDE: We travel by high-speed train. It takes about two hours [Q2], whereas the bus takes about five. The train is more expensive. However, it's much more comfortable.

GUIDE: In Samarkand, our accommodation is a small family guesthouse [Q3] near the Registan. It isn't a big international hotel. On the other hand, the rooms are clean and the owners are very friendly.

GUIDE: The price of the tour is two hundred and fifty dollars — no, I'm sorry, that was last year's price. This season it's two hundred and forty dollars [Q4] per person. That includes the train tickets, the guided tours and all the sightseeing.
GUIDE: Breakfast and lunch are included, while dinner [Q5] isn't, so you can try local restaurants in the evening.
GUIDE: Although it's autumn, the afternoons in Bukhara are still hot. The evenings can be cool, though, so please bring a light jacket [Q6].
GUIDE: Finally, travel insurance isn't included, but we strongly recommend it.

intro: HERE / THERE — shu yerda / u yerda.
EVERYWHERE — hamma joyda; SOMEWHERE — qayerdadir (tasdiq); ANYWHERE — biror joyda (savol/inkor); NOWHERE — hech qayerda (inkor ma'no, fe'l tasdiq).
NEARBY — yaqin atrofda: "There is a bank nearby." Predlogsiz: abroad, upstairs, downstairs, indoors, home.
O'rin: fe'ldan keyin (go there), ob'ektdan keyin (put it here), odatda vaqt ravishidan oldin: "We went there yesterday."
formulas: She is here now. / He is there waiting for you.
U hozir shu yerda. / U u yerda seni kutyapti.
They looked everywhere for the keys.
I left my phone somewhere in the house. / Can you find this book anywhere?
Telefonimni uyning qayeridadir qoldirdim. / Bu kitobni biror joydan topa olasanmi?
S + V + nearby / there is … nearby
go home / live abroad / go upstairs / stay indoors
Jaloliddin lived abroad for years and never went home.
Jaloliddin yillar davomida chet elda yashadi va hech qachon vataniga qaytmadi.
presentation: Where did the battle take place?
It took place here, near the river.
Is there a museum nearby?
Yes, the history museum is nearby.
Where are the ruins of the old fortress?
They are somewhere in the hills.
Did the Mongols go everywhere?
Almost everywhere — from China to Europe.

He went abroad — to India, then to Iran.

Somewhere unknown — nobody knows where his grave is.
notes: Joy + vaqt: joy oldin — We stayed there all day.
"Here comes…" / "There goes…" — urg'u uchun inversiya: "Here comes the teacher!"
B1: -where + sifat / to + V1: somewhere quiet, nowhere to go (Is there anywhere quiet? — NOT Is there quiet anywhere?).

CCQ: There was nowhere to hide. — Could he hide? (No)
CCQ: I left my phone somewhere. — Do I know where it is? (No)
CCQ: Is there a bank nearby? — Is it far? (No)

reading.title: Jaloliddin Manguberdi — the prince who had nowhere to go
text: Jaloliddin Manguberdi was born in 1199 in Khorezm, the son of the Khorezmshah Muhammad II. His father ruled over a huge empire, from the Caspian Sea almost to India. Then, in 1219, Genghis Khan invaded. City after city fell; Bukhara, Samarkand and Urgench were destroyed. The Shah fled somewhere to the west and died on a small island in the Caspian. His son did not flee.

The Mongols were everywhere, but Jaloliddin gathered soldiers wherever he could and fought them here and there for eleven years. His most famous battle took place in 1221 on the banks of the Indus river, in today's Pakistan. His army was surrounded; there was nowhere to retreat. Jaloliddin rode his horse off a cliff into the river and swam across with his weapons. According to old chronicles, Genghis Khan was watching from the bank and told his sons that every father should wish for a son like this.

He carried on fighting abroad — in India, Iran, Georgia and Iraq — always looking for allies, but he found none anywhere. In 1231 he was killed in the mountains of Kurdistan. Nobody knows where his grave is.

For centuries his story lived mainly in chronicles. Today his monument stands in Urgench, and many visitors go there to see it. An order of the Republic of Uzbekistan is named after him, and people in Uzbekistan remember him as the man who never surrendered.

GUIDE: First, the coins. Many visitors look for them upstairs, but they are actually downstairs, next to the café. [Q1] Some of these ancient coins came from abroad, with traders on the Silk Road.

lessons.title: Like, As if, As though, Such as
lessons.grammar_topic: LIKE / AS / AS IF / AS THOUGH / FOR (kitob) + qo'shimcha: SUCH AS / THE SAME AS / JUST AS / UNLIKE / INSTEAD OF
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 9 – like, as if, as though, for (8 qator); GENETICS; Reading — Usain Bolt (Jony Academy matni (moslashtirilgan)); Topic 46–48, AUDIO 71–80 — ixtiyoriy; SPEAKING/WRITING mavzusi — rahbar rejasi (IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 9-qator): "Living in a big city vs. living in a small town"
objectives: like (o'xshatish) va as (haqiqiy vazifa): 6 gapdan 5 tasida to'g'ri tanlash.
as if / as though: real (Present) va noreal (Past Simple, were); for — nisbatan.
such as / the same … as / unlike / instead of + V-ing ni to'g'ri ishlatish.
Listening (IELTS Part 3, MCQ): 5 savoldan 4 tasiga to'g'ri javob.

Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 8 qator)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. 1 daqiqada: 2 marta — warm-up, 3 — normativ, 4 — a'lo (2 coin).

Reading: T/F/NG + sentence completion

To'liq insho — uyda (Writing 4).
Exit ticket

1) He acts as if he ___ (be) the boss, but he isn't. (were) 2) Inglizchasi: irsiyat; belgi (heredity; trait). 3) Part 3 da chalg'itgich nima? (avval aytilib, keyin tuzatilgan javob). Qog'ozda topshiriladi.
Uyga vazifa

MAJBURIY (~50 daq): CORE 20 flashcard, WRITING — Big city vs small town (Writing 4, 150–200 so'z), SPEAKING ovozli 2 javob, 5 tarjima gapi, og'zaki normativ. IXTIYORIY: Speaking Part 2 (Family and genes), Topic 46–48, STRONG 20 + jadval yoddan, ZAXIRA mashqlar.

intro: LIKE + ot — o'xshatish: She dances like a professional (u professional emas). AS + ot — haqiqiy vazifa: She works as a teacher (u o'qituvchi).
AS IF / AS THOUGH + gap — "xuddi …dek": real — Present (He looks as if he is tired); noreal — Past Simple, were (He talks as if he knew everything).
FOR — nisbatan: tall for his age. Qo'shimcha (kitobda yo'q): such as, the same as, just as, unlike, instead of + V-ing.
formulas: S + V + as if / as though + gap (Present — real; Past Simple, were — noreal)
He talks as if he knew everything.
U xuddi hamma narsani biladigandek gapiradi (aslida bilmaydi).
He is tall for his age.
I love fruits such as apples and bananas.
Olma va banan kabi mevalarni yaxshi ko'raman.
the same as + ot; just as + gap/ot
This jacket is the same as mine. / She sings just as her mother did.
Bu kurtka meniki bilan bir xil. / U xuddi onasi kuylagandek kuylaydi.
Unlike his brother, he is very shy. / I'll have tea instead of coffee.
Akasidan farqli o'laroq, u juda tortinchoq. / Qahva o'rniga choy ichaman.
presentation: Why does he run like that?
He runs as if he had wings — but it's genetics and training.
Does she work as a scientist?
Yes, she works as a geneticist in a lab.
Why do identical twins look so similar?
They have the same DNA as each other, unlike ordinary brothers and sisters.
Why is he so fast?
He is very tall for a sprinter, and he looks as though he was born to run.
Is a clone like a twin?
A clone is genetically the same as the original, like a twin born later.
notes: as if: Present — real ehtimol (He looks as if he is tired); Past Simple — noreallikni ta'kidlaydi (og'zakida Present ham uchraydi); Past Perfect — o'tgan noreal (He looked as if he had seen a ghost); rasmiy — as if he were, og'zaki — as if he was.
the same as — aynan bir xil (the same DNA as his twin); o'xshatish uchun like (The genome is like a book). look + sifat — like'siz: She looks tired.
CCQ: He works as a doctor. — Is he a doctor? (Yes)
CCQ: He talks like a doctor. — Is he a doctor? (No / not necessarily)
CCQ: She acts as if she were the boss. — Is she the boss? (No)
CCQ: He is tall for his age. — Is he taller than most children of his age? (Yes) Is he tall for an adult? (Not necessarily)
mistakes: She works like a teacher. (haqiqiy ish)
look + sifat — like'siz (like + ot: looks like her mum).

how: CORE — asosiy atamalar; STRONG — jarayon va texnologiya; SUPER — tibbiyot va sport. Har so'zga taqqoslash gapi: "DNA works like a code."
core: A gene is like a recipe for one protein.
Gen — bitta oqsil uchun retsept kabi.
DNA works like a code with four letters.
DNK to'rt harfli kod kabi ishlaydi.
Humans have 46 chromosomes, unlike dogs, which have 78.
Odamda 46 xromosoma bor, itlarda esa, farqli o'laroq, 78.
Heredity explains why you look like your parents.
Traits such as eye colour are inherited.
Ko'z rangi kabi xususiyatlar irsiy o'tadi.
Some traits, such as height, depend on many genes.
Bo'y kabi ba'zi xususiyatlar ko'p genlarga bog'liq.
A mutation is like a typing mistake in the code.
The human genome is like a book of 3 billion letters.
Inson genomi 3 milliard harfli kitobga o'xshaydi.
The genetic code is almost the same in all living things.
Genetik kod barcha tirik mavjudotlarda deyarli bir xil.
The gene for brown eyes is usually dominant, unlike the gene for blue eyes.
Qo'ng'ir ko'z geni, ko'k ko'z genidan farqli o'laroq, odatda dominant bo'ladi.
A recessive trait appears only if both parents pass it on.
Retsessiv belgi faqat ikkala ota-ona bersagina ko'rinadi.
Offspring look like their parents but are not exactly the same as them.
Nasl ota-onaga o'xshaydi, lekin ular bilan aynan bir xil emas.
We share a common ancestor with chimpanzees.
Biz shimpanzelar bilan umumiy ajdodga egamiz.
Evolution works like a very slow experiment.
Evolyutsiya juda sekin tajriba kabi ishlaydi.
Natural selection acts like a filter.
Every organism, such as a plant or a fish, has DNA.
O'simlik yoki baliq kabi har bir organizmda DNK bor.
A cell is like a small factory.
A clone is genetically the same as the original.
Klon genetik jihatdan asl nusxa bilan bir xil.
Genetic disorders such as haemophilia are inherited.
Gemofiliya kabi genetik kasalliklar irsiy o'tadi.
Genetic engineering works as if scientists were editing a text.
Gen muhandisligi xuddi olimlar matnni tahrirlayotgandek ishlaydi.
strong: An allele is one version of a gene, like one spelling of a word.
Allel — genning bir varianti, so'zning bir imlosi kabi.
Your genotype is the code; your phenotype is what we see.
Genotip — kod; fenotip — biz ko'radigan narsa.
Identical twins have the same genotype, but their phenotypes can differ.
Bir tuxumli egizaklarning genotipi bir xil, lekin fenotipi farq qilishi mumkin.
The nucleus works like the office of the cell.
Cloning sounds like science fiction, but Dolly the sheep was real.
Klonlash ilmiy fantastikaga o'xshaydi, lekin qo'y Dolli haqiqiy edi.
Heritable traits pass from parents to offspring, just as a family name does.
Irsiy belgilar, xuddi familiya kabi, ota-onadan naslga o'tadi.
GMO crops such as corn are common.
Makkajo'xori kabi GMO ekinlar keng tarqalgan.
A mule is a hybrid — a mix of a horse and a donkey.
Xachir — duragay, ya'ni ot va eshakning aralashmasi.
Farmers crossbreed plants instead of waiting for nature.
Fermerlar tabiatni kutish o'rniga o'simliklarni chatishtiradi.
Reproduction passes genes to the next generation.
An embryo is like a plan of the future body.
Fertilization is like two halves of a code joining.
Urug'lanish — kodning ikki yarmi qo'shilishi kabi.
Stem cells can become any cell, unlike normal cells.
Ildiz hujayralar, oddiy hujayralardan farqli o'laroq, har qanday hujayraga aylanishi mumkin.
Scientists read the DNA sequence like a text.
Olimlar DNK ketma-ketligini matn kabi o'qiydi.
Genetic testing works as if you were reading your own manual.
Genetik tekshiruv xuddi o'z qo'llanmangni o'qiyotgandek ishlaydi.
Gene therapy repairs genes instead of treating symptoms.
Gen terapiyasi alomatlarni davolash o'rniga genlarni tuzatadi.
Variation in a population is like colours in a garden.
Biotechnology uses cells as if they were factories.
Biotexnologiya hujayralarni xuddi zavod kabi ishlatadi.
Proteins such as haemoglobin carry oxygen.
super: Enzymes work like scissors that cut DNA.
Fermentlar DNKni kesadigan qaychi kabi ishlaydi.
DNA replication is like photocopying a book.
A carrier has the gene but, unlike a patient, no symptoms.
Tashuvchida gen bor, lekin bemordan farqli o'laroq, alomat yo'q.
Mutant plants such as seedless grapes are useful.
Urug'siz uzum kabi mutant o'simliklar foydali.
Newborn screening works as a safety check.
Chaqaloq skriningi xavfsizlik tekshiruvi sifatida ishlaydi.
Genetic modification is like editing, not creating.
Genetik o'zgartirish yaratishga emas, tahrirlashga o'xshaydi.
Adaptation changes a species just as training changes a body.
Moslashish turni xuddi mashq tanani o'zgartirgandek o'zgartiradi.
Species such as tigers are disappearing.
Sprinters have fast-twitch fibres, unlike marathon runners.
Sprinterlarda, marafonchilardan farqli o'laroq, tez qisqaruvchi tolalar bor.
Talent is like a seed — it needs training to grow.
Iste'dod urug' kabi — o'sish uchun mashq kerak.
The nature-vs-nurture debate is as old as science.
Tabiat-tarbiya bahsi fanning o'zi kabi qadimiy.
Identical twins are like living clones.
Bir tuxumli egizaklar tirik klonlar kabi.
Children resemble their parents in traits such as voice.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Living in a big city vs living in a small town
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ like / as / such as / unlike / as if.
items: Part 1: Do you live in a big city or a small town?
Part 1: What do you like most about the place where you live?
Part 3: Why do so many young people move from small towns to big cities such as Tashkent?
Part 3: What are the main problems of living in a big city?
Part 3: What can a small town offer that a big city cannot?
Part 3: Do neighbours in small towns help each other more than people in big cities?
Part 3: How could small towns become more attractive for young people?
answers: I live in Tashkent, so I live in a big city. Unlike my cousins in a small town near Samarkand, I take the metro to school every day.
I like the parks most, such as Babur Park near my house. In the evening it feels as if the whole neighbourhood comes there to walk and talk.

Well, I think the main reason is job opportunities. Big cities such as Tashkent have universities, IT companies and banks, unlike small towns, where good jobs are rare. For example, my neighbour from Jizzakh moved here and now works as a programmer. So young people go where the future is.

I'd say the main problems are traffic and the cost of living. In the morning the roads are so crowded that it feels as if the whole city is driving at the same time. For example, my father's commute takes an hour. Also, rent in Tashkent is very expensive, so many families spend half their salary on a flat.

A small town offers peace and a strong community. Life there is quiet, unlike the noisy streets of a capital. For example, in my grandmother's town in the Fergana Valley, people know each other, and the air is clean. On the other hand, there are fewer facilities, such as cinemas or good hospitals.

Yes, I think they usually do. In a small town the mahalla works like a big family. For example, when my uncle built his house, all the neighbours came to help him, as if it were their own home. In a big city, people are busy and often don't even know who lives next door.

In my view, the government should create jobs there, for example small factories or IT centres. Young people also need facilities such as sports centres, cafes and fast internet. If a small town had all this, life there would feel just as interesting as in Tashkent, and young people would not have to leave.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Living in a big city vs living in a small town
class_ex.instr: Some people prefer to live in a big city, while others would rather live in a small town. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of both places and give your own opinion. Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval + kirish (35–45 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi (Writing 4)
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: ikki variant taqqoslash (katta shahar va kichik shahar) — ikkala joyning afzallik va kamchiliklari + o'z fikringiz

2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: big city, small town, advantages and disadvantages, both places, your own opinion; mavzu so'zlari: job opportunities, cost of living, peaceful, crowded, facilities, community, commute

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: katta shahar — afzalliklar va kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kichik shahar — afzalliklar va kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + o'z tanlovingiz va sababi)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of … is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, … also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: like / as / such as / unlike / as if 2+ marta (Unlike a small town, … / such as theatres and universities / it feels as if everyone knows you / works as a …)
answers: Namuna kirish (43 so'z): Many young people dream of moving to a large city, but others are happy with the calm life of a small town. Both places have clear benefits and drawbacks. This essay will discuss them and explain why I would choose a big city.

Namuna AD jadval: KATTA SHAHAR — Afzalliklar: 1) ish imkoniyatlari (IT kompaniyalar, banklar) 2) universitet, kasalxona, teatr kabi qulayliklar; Kamchiliklar: 1) yashash narxi qimmat (ijara) 2) tirbandlik, ishga yo'l ~1 soat. KICHIK SHAHAR — Afzalliklar: 1) tinch va arzon 2) qo'shnilar bir-birini taniydi, mahalla ahil; Kamchiliklar: 1) ish kam 2) qulayliklar kam — yoshlar o'qish/ish uchun ketadi.

Namuna insho (188 so'z) — kirish: Many young people dream of moving to a large city, but others are happy with the calm life of a small town. Both places have clear benefits and drawbacks. This essay will discuss them and explain why I would choose a big city.

Namuna insho — body 1: On the one hand, a big city such as Tashkent offers many job opportunities and facilities, including universities, hospitals and theatres. For example, my cousin moved from a village and now works as a designer in an IT company. However, city life also has drawbacks: the cost of living is high, the streets are crowded, and the commute can take an hour.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, life in a small town is peaceful and cheap. Unlike city people, neighbours in a small town know each other, so the whole street feels like one big family. Nevertheless, there are fewer jobs and facilities, and many young people have to leave to find work or study.
Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, both places have strengths and weaknesses. Personally, I would choose a big city, because at my age education and a career matter more to me than a quiet life.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — such as Tashkent, works as a designer, Unlike city people, feels like one big family (4 marta); bog'lovchilar — On the one hand, For example, However, On the other hand, so, Nevertheless, In conclusion, because; mavzu so'zlari — job opportunities, facilities, cost of living, crowded, commute, peaceful, community.
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 9-qator ("Living in a big city vs. living in a small town"); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). reading.title: Usain Bolt — born to run, or made to run?
text: Usain Bolt was born in 1986 in a small village in Jamaica. As a boy he played cricket and football, just as many Jamaican children do, and he ran like the wind — but he didn't like training. Some people thought he behaved as if success would come by itself.

It didn't, but hard work helped. At the Beijing Olympics in 2008 Bolt ran 100 metres in 9.69 seconds, and in Berlin in 2009 he set a world record of 9.58 seconds. He won eight Olympic gold medals and became one of the most famous sprinters in history. Unlike most sprinters, who are shorter and more compact, Bolt is 1.95 m tall.

Scientists are very interested in athletes like him. Genetics is part of the answer: top sprinters usually have a large number of fast-twitch muscle fibres, a trait that is partly inherited, and many of them share a variant of a gene called ACTN3. This variant is common in Jamaica, as if the whole island were selected for running. But genes are not everything. Bolt trained hard for many years and worked with the same coach for about thirteen years.

Was he born to run or made to run? Most scientists answer: both. They often say that nature loads the gun and nurture pulls the trigger. Bolt retired in 2017. Many young runners train as though they could become the next Bolt, but few have both the genes and the discipline.

tasks.note: NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q; FALSE — matn teskarisini aytadi.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 3 — multiple choice (A, B or C).
You will hear two students, Anna and Ben, planning a biology presentation about a study of twins.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, kalit so'zlarni belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: ANNA: Ben, shall we start our biology presentation with the twin study from the article?
BEN: Yes. They followed two hundred pairs of twins — sorry, three hundred pairs — for ten years.
ANNA: What did it show? Something about food and height?
BEN: No, that was an older study. This one showed that traits such as eye colour and height are mostly inherited, but personality depends a lot on the people around you. [Q1]
ANNA: Right. Identical twins have the same DNA as each other, so they look like each other. But they don't always act the same.
BEN: Which example shall we use? The two brothers who became doctors?
ANNA: I prefer the sisters, Mia and Lucy. Mia is quiet, unlike her sister, and Lucy acts as if she were much older. [Q2]
BEN: OK. What was the hardest part for you?
ANNA: The statistics. And you?
BEN: The numbers were fine. The vocabulary was the most difficult — words like genome and heredity. [Q3]
ANNA: Should we show photos of the twins?
BEN: We can't. The families asked to keep them private. [Q4] Let's draw a diagram instead of using photos.
ANNA: And how long is the talk? Ten minutes?
BEN: The teacher said eight — no, wait, twelve minutes, with questions. [Q5]

tasks.title: Multiple choice — A, B or C
tasks.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
items: 1 What did the study mainly show? A) Height depends mostly on food. B) Body traits are mostly inherited, but personality also depends on other people. C) Twins have the same personality.
2 Which example do they choose? A) two sisters B) two brothers who became doctors C) twins from different countries
3 What did Ben find most difficult? A) the statistics B) finding the article C) the vocabulary
4 Why will they not show photos? A) The photos are poor. B) The families want privacy. C) The teacher does not allow it.
5 How long will the talk be? A) twelve minutes B) ten minutes C) eight minutes

kahoot.explain: O'xshatish (u gepard emas): like + ot.

kahoot.q: He talks as if he ___ everything about DNA. (But he doesn't.)
kahoot.explain: Noreal → Past Simple: knew (og'zakida knows ham uchraydi, noreallikni knew ko'rsatadi).

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: He went out instead of study for the biology test.
She reads about genes instead of watching TV.
Unlike his sister, he has blue eyes.
My uncle works as a nurse.
kahoot.explain: instead of + V-ing: instead of studying.

kahoot.q: I love fruits ___ apples and bananas.
kahoot.explain: Misol keltirish: such as.

kahoot.q: Your eyes are the same ___ your mother's.
kahoot.explain: the same as + ot.

kahoot.q: ___ his brother, he is very shy.
kahoot.explain: unlike — …dan farqli o'laroq.

kahoot.q: "U o'qituvchi sifatida ishlaydi."
options: She works as if a teacher.
She works such as a teacher.
kahoot.explain: sifatida = as; like — o'xshab.

kahoot.q: LIKE va AS farqi qaysi?
kahoot.explain: like — o'xshatish; as — haqiqiy vazifa.

kahoot.q: He behaves as though he ___ a king. (He isn't.)
kahoot.explain: Noreal: as though + were.

kahoot.q: I'll have tea instead of ___ coffee.
kahoot.explain: instead of + V-ing.

kahoot.q: She sings just ___ her mother did.
kahoot.explain: just as + gap.

kahoot.q: Children ___ traits such as eye colour from their parents.
kahoot.explain: inherit — irsiy olmoq.

kahoot.q: A change in a gene is a ___.
kahoot.explain: mutation — gendagi o'zgarish.

kahoot.q: The young of an animal or a plant are its ___.
kahoot.explain: offspring — nasl; ancestor — ajdod.

kahoot.q: An exact genetic copy of an organism made in a lab is a ___.
kahoot.explain: clone — aniq genetik nusxa.

kahoot.q: The smallest living unit of any organism is a ___.
kahoot.explain: cell — hujayra.

kahoot.q: Which is the opposite of a "dominant" gene?
kahoot.explain: dominant — ustun; recessive — retsessiv.

kahoot.q: "natural selection" nimani anglatadi?
kahoot.explain: Darvin nazariyasi atamasi.

kahoot.q: Eye colour and height are genetic ___.
kahoot.explain: trait — belgi.

lessons.title: Mixed Conditionals
lessons.grammar_topic: ARALASH SHART GAPLAR (If + Past Perfect, would + V1 / If + Past Simple, would have + V3)
lessons.test_after: PROGRESS TEST 2 (pt2) — keyingi dars (11-dars) boshida, 35 daqiqa, 40 ball; qamrov: 6–10-darslar (adverbs of degree / contrast / place, like / as if, mixed conditionals; Health, Travel, History, Genetics, VR); o'tish: ≥70% (28/40)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 10 – Conditional mixed (2 qatorli jadval); VIRTUAL REALITY (41 so'z); Reading — Jony Academy matni (moslashtirilgan); AUDIO 81–90, Topic 51–53 — ixtiyoriy.
objectives: Mixed 1 va Mixed 2 ni qo'llash: gap to'ldirishda 5 tadan 4+ to'g'ri.
Type 2 / 3 va Mixed 1 / 2 ni vaqt ko'rsatkichlari (now / yesterday) bo'yicha farqlash: 6 tadan 5+.
VR CORE 10 so'zni ta'rifiga moslash va mixed conditional gapda ishlatish.
Listening Part 4: ma'ruzadan 6 ta aniq ma'lumotni chalg'itgichlarga aldanmay yozish.
Speaking Part 2 da 2+ mixed conditional; Task 2 body paragrafi (70–90 so'z).
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 10 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.
CORE 20 varag'i — dars sahifasining Lug'at tabidan (PDF).
Kahoot: dars boshida — 'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi (L09); shu darsning Kahooti uyda o'ynaladi (11-dars — test darsi).
Listening: skript ustozda (yashirin transcript), ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi; audio fayl kerak emas.
Writing/Speaking rubrikasi — L01 dagi W-B1 va S-B1 jadvallari; juftlik varag'i peer-b1.
timeline: Warm-up: If I had studied IT…

Ustoz: "If I had studied IT at university, I would be a programmer now." — shart o'tganda, natija hozir. Teskarisi: "If I were rich, I would have bought a VR headset yesterday." 2–3 o'quvchi o'zi haqida 1 gap aytadi.
TAKROR: Kahoot — L09 (Like / as / as if)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi — L09 savollari (shu darsniki emas). 20 savol × 15 s; izohni faqat yarmidan ko'pi xato qilgan savollarga bering.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — L09 Genetics CORE 20
Ustoz 20 so'zni o'zbekcha aytadi, o'quvchi inglizcha yozadi (4 daq); 1 daq juftlikda tekshirish, kalit — L09 Lug'at tabi. 17/20+ — bajarildi (2 coin).
Uy vazifasini tekshirish

L09 MAJBURIY: WRITING — Living in a big city vs living in a small town (Writing 4) inshosi yig'ib olinadi (ustoz W-B1-AD bilan tekshiradi; jadval — L09 dars sahifasida); SPEAKING ovozli javoblari — ilova natijasi; tarjimadan 2 gap doskada tuzatiladi.
YANGI MAVZU: Mixed conditionals (Mixed 1 / Mixed 2)

10 daq: doskada vaqt chizig'i O'TMISH | HOZIR. Mixed 1: If + had + V3 → would + V1 (now); Mixed 2: If + Past Simple (doimiy holat) → would have + V3 (yesterday); Type 2/3 bilan solishtirish (formulas 3–4); presentation 1–5 juftlikda. CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq: 1-majburiy mashq 'Mixed 1'.
Lug'at: Virtual reality — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

Sinfda: virtual reality, augmented reality, simulation, headset, immersive, avatar, interactive, graphics, realistic, virtual tour — ma'no + 1 gap; 'VR lug'ati' match (2 daq). Qolgani — flashcard uyda.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 2 qator + Type 2/3)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. Kitobsiz — grammar.formulas 1–4.
Sinf mashqlari: Mixed 2 (8 daq) + Qaysi tur? (8 daq)
Mixed 2 — yakka + juftlikda tekshirish; Qaysi tur? — juftlikda, vaqt chizig'i bilan; 2 daq javoblar. ZAXIRA: Xatoni toping. Vaqt yetmasa — uyga.
Listening (IELTS Part 4): note completion — VR in schools
2 daq tayyorgarlik; 1-tinglash; 1 daq juftlikda solishtirish; 2-tinglash; 3 daq javoblar — dalil gap skriptdan (Q1, Q5 tuzatishlari); 2 daq 2 ta target gapni og'zaki tiklash.
Reading: T/F/NG + sentence completion
3 daq gist: 'Why did Zuckerberg buy Oculus?' (to build the next big platform); 5 daq T/F/NG; 4 daq sentence completion. ZAXIRA — qolgan 2 topshiriq.
Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Decisions and technology
Part 1 juftlikda 3 daq; Part 2: 1 daq tayyorgarlik, A 1.5, B 1.5 daq (sherik peer-b1 belgilaydi); Part 3 — 2 daq; ustoz 1 daq feedback (S-B1).
Writing (IELTS Task 2 uslubi): opinion — to what extent
2 daq savol tahlili; 2 daq reja; 6 daq body paragraf; 2 daq juftlikda peer-b1.
Exit ticket
1) If I had learned to code at 12, I ___ (work) in IT now. (would work) 2) The device you wear on your head for VR? (headset) 3) 'Two hundred and fifty dollars' — note'da qanday? (250)
Uyga vazifa
MAJBURIY: test tayyorgarligi, CORE flashcard, 8 aralash shart, tarjima, og'zaki normativ. IXTIYORIY: Topic 51–53, STRONG, jadval yoddan. Keyingi dars — PROGRESS TEST 2.

intro: MIXED 1 (o'tgan → hozir): "If I had studied harder (o'tgan), I would be successful now (hozir)."
MIXED 2 (hozir → o'tgan): "If he were more careful (doimiy xarakter), he wouldn't have made that mistake (o'tgan)."
Ko'rsatkichlar: now / today / still — hozirgi yarim; yesterday / last year / then — o'tgan yarim.
formulas: If + Past Perfect, S + would + V1 (now)
If I had studied harder, I would be successful now.
If + Past Simple, S + would have + V3 (then)
If he was/were more careful, he wouldn't have made that mistake.
U (umuman) ehtiyotkor odam bo'lganida, o'sha xatoni qilmagan bo'lardi.
If I had a VR headset, I would play every day.
VR shlemim bo'lsa, har kuni o'ynardim.
If + Past Perfect, would have + V3
If I had bought it last year, it would have been cheaper.
O'tgan yili olganimda, arzonroq bo'lgan bo'lardi.
If + … , S + wouldn't + V1 / Would + S + V1 if …?
If Aziz hadn't left university, would he be a businessman today?
Aziz universitetni tashlamaganida, bugun tadbirkor bo'larmidi?
If I had learned to code, I could work in VR now.
Dasturlashni o'rganganimda, hozir VR sohasida ishlay olardim.
presentation: If you had started coding at 12, what would you be now?
If I had started at 12, I would be a developer now.
If VR were cheaper, would you have bought a headset last year?
Yes, if it were cheaper, I would have bought one.
If you weren't so busy, would you have joined the VR club?
Yes, if I weren't so busy, I would have joined.
If the school had bought headsets, would lessons be different now?
Yes, lessons would be immersive now.
If I had listened to my teacher, would I be at university?
Yes, you would be there now.
notes: Mixed 1 eng ko'p uchraydi: o'tgan qaror → hozirgi hayot: "If I hadn't come to Jony Academy, I wouldn't speak English now."
Mixed 2 — doimiy xarakter/holat (were, had, lived) → o'tgan voqea.
"were" hamma shaxs uchun rasmiy; "was" og'zaki.
CCQ: If I had studied harder, I would be successful now. — Did I study hard? (No) Am I successful now? (No)
CCQ: If he were more careful, he wouldn't have crashed. — Is he careful in general? (No) Did he crash? (Yes)
CCQ: If she weren't afraid of heights, she would have tried the VR game. — Is she afraid of heights? (Yes) Did she try the game? (No)
mistakes: If I had studied harder, I would have been successful now.
If he would be careful, he wouldn't have made it.
If I studied IT, I would be a programmer now. (o'tgan qaror)
If I had studied IT, I would be a programmer now.
If I had a car, I would have drove.
If she was more careful, she wouldn't make it yesterday.

class_ex.title: Mixed 1
class_ex.instr: O'tgan shart → hozirgi natija. Yakka; 1 — namuna.
items: If I ___ (learn) to code at school, I ___ (work) in IT now.
If she ___ (not / miss) the exam, she ___ (be) at university today.
If they ___ (invest) in VR in 2014, they ___ (be) rich now.
If he ___ (listen) to the doctor, he ___ (feel) better now.
If we ___ (buy) headsets last year, our lessons ___ (be) immersive now.

class_ex.title: Mixed 2
class_ex.instr: Hozirgi holat → o'tgan natija. Yakka + juftlikda tekshirish; 1 — namuna.
items: If he ___ (be) more careful, he ___ (not / make) that mistake.
If I ___ (not / get) motion sickness, I ___ (finish) the game.
If she ___ (live) in Tashkent, she ___ (come) to the VR event.
If VR ___ (be) cheaper, schools ___ (buy) it years ago.
If he ___ (not / be) so shy, he ___ (present) his prototype.

class_ex.title: Qaysi tur?
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Type 2 / Type 3 / Mixed 1 / Mixed 2 — vaqt ko'rsatkichi bilan asoslang. 1 — namuna (Type 2).
items: If I had a headset, I would play now.
If I had bought it last year, it would have been cheaper.
If I had bought it, I would be an expert now.
If I were richer, I would have bought it yesterday.
If he hadn't left university, he would be a teacher now.
If she weren't afraid of heights, she would have tried the simulation yesterday.

class_ex.title: Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Decisions and technology
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 savol-javob; Part 2 kartochka, 1–2 daqiqa; Part 3 fikr + sabab.
items: Part 1: Have you ever tried virtual reality (VR)?
Part 1: Do you play computer games? Why / why not?
Part 1: What technology would you like to have?
Part 1: Do you prefer real games or online games?
Part 2 card: Describe an important decision you made. You should say: what it was / when you made it / who helped you — and explain how your life would be different now if you hadn't made it.
Part 3: Will VR replace school trips in the future?
Part 3: Is technology making young people less active?
answers: Yes, I tried a VR headset at a shopping centre last year. It was so immersive!
Yes, I play football games on my phone at weekends. If I had more free time, I would play more.
I'd like to have a good laptop. If I had bought one last year, I would be learning programming now.
I prefer real games, especially football with my friends. Online games make my eyes tired.

I'd like to talk about my decision to join an English course two years ago. I made it in the summer after ninth grade, when I realised that English was important for my future. My older sister helped me most — she found the course and paid for the first month. At first it was hard, because I had to study after school every day. If I hadn't joined the course, I wouldn't be able to watch videos in English now. And if I hadn't met my classmates there, I wouldn't have such good friends today.
I don't think so. VR is cheaper and safer, but real trips teach students to communicate and to see things with their own eyes.
In some ways, yes. If schools had built more sports grounds years ago, young people would be more active now.
class_ex.note: ICQ: How long do you prepare? (1 minute) — Full sentences? (No, key words) — How long do you speak? (1–2 minutes). CCQ: If I hadn't made that decision, I wouldn't be here now. — Did I make it? (Yes) Am I here now? (Yes). Kuchsizlar uchun: If I hadn't …, I wouldn't … now. Sherik peer-b1 bilan tekshiradi (L01).

class_ex.title: VR lug'ati
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: ta'rifga qutidagi so'zni moslang (2 so'z ortiqcha). 1 — namuna (headset).
items: the device you wear on your head for VR
makes you feel you are inside the virtual world
a copy of a real situation for training
your character in a virtual world
feeling sick because of movement in VR
a shared virtual universe

If the school bought headsets last year, our lessons would be immersive now.
If I weren't afraid of heights, I would have try the VR skydiving game.

answers: If the school had bought headsets last year, …
…I would have tried the VR skydiving game.
…the game would have sold well last month.

class_ex.title: Writing (IELTS Task 2): opinion — to what extent
class_ex.instr: Some people think virtual reality will replace real travel and school trips in the future. To what extent do you agree or disagree? — Sinfda 1 body paragraf (70–90 so'z): 1+ mixed conditional, 3+ VR CORE so'z.
items: 1) Savol turi: opinion (to what extent).
2) Kalit so'zlar: replace, real travel, school trips, in the future.
3) Reja: fikr + sabab (haqiqiy tajriba, muloqot) + misol (sinf sayohati).
4) Boshlanmalar: In my opinion, … / One reason is that … / For example, … / If our class hadn't …, we wouldn't … now.
class_ex.answers: Namuna: In my opinion, virtual reality will not fully replace real school trips. One reason is that a virtual tour, however realistic and immersive, cannot give students real experience. For example, last spring my class visited Samarkand. If we hadn't gone there, we wouldn't remember Registan Square so clearly now. We also talked to local people and practised our English with tourists. If the trip had been only a headset lesson, we wouldn't be such good friends now. Therefore, VR is a useful extra tool, not a replacement.

reading.title: Mark Zuckerberg — a big bet on virtual reality
text: Mark Zuckerberg was born in 1984 in New York State. He started writing computer programs while he was still at school, and in 2004, at Harvard, he built a website for Harvard students from his dormitory. It was called "The Facebook". If he had stayed at Harvard, he would probably be a computer science professor now. Instead, he dropped out, moved to California and opened the site to the world. By 2012 it had a billion users.

In 2014 Zuckerberg made a decision that surprised everybody: he paid about two billion dollars for Oculus, a small company that made VR headsets. He believed that the next big computer platform was coming, and he wanted his company to build it. Critics laughed. Headsets were heavy, the graphics were poor, and many users got motion sickness. If the headsets had been lighter, more people would have bought them in those first years. If the technology had been ready, VR would be everywhere now. It wasn't.

In 2021 he went further: he renamed the whole company Meta and promised a "metaverse" — a shared virtual world where people would work, study and meet as avatars. The company has spent tens of billions of dollars on it. If he weren't so sure about the future, he would have stopped years ago. Some investors wish he had.

Today Meta's headsets are among the most popular in the world, and many people use them for games, simulations and virtual tours. Still, if VR headsets were as light as glasses, far more people would use them every day. Was the bet right? Nobody knows yet. If the metaverse becomes real, Zuckerberg will be remembered as a visionary. If it doesn't, people will say that if he had put that money into AI earlier, Meta would be far ahead now. Either way, he once said that the biggest risk is not taking any risk.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 4 — note completion. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear part of a short lecture about using virtual reality (VR) in schools.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (raqam, yil, ot) belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: LECTURER: Good morning. Today's talk is about virtual reality, or VR, in schools, and what we have learned from the first projects.
LECTURER: Schools first tried VR headsets in normal lessons in 2016 — sorry, let me correct that: the first large school projects actually started in 2015. [Q1]
LECTURER: A headset cost about three hundred dollars in the shops, but schools paid less: two hundred and fifty dollars per headset. [Q2]
LECTURER: If the headsets had been cheaper, many more schools would use them now.

LECTURER: However, price was not the main problem. The main problem was teacher training. [Q3] If teachers had been trained properly, most projects would be much bigger today. And if more teachers were confident with technology, many projects would have started earlier.

LECTURER: Which subject improved most? Many people expect history, because of the virtual tours of ancient cities. In fact, the biggest change was in science, [Q4] where students could explore the human body in 3D simulations.
LECTURER: Lessons also became more interactive. In one school, test results went up by eighteen per cent — no, sorry, by fifteen per cent [Q5] — after one year.
LECTURER: There is one negative point: some students get motion sickness, so teachers now use a headset for no more than twenty minutes at a time. [Q6]
LECTURER: If I were a head teacher, I would have started with one small class first.

The main problem: (3) ______

kahoot.q: If he were more careful, he ___ that mistake yesterday.

kahoot.q: If I ___ IT at university, I would be a programmer now.

options: If she would have more time, she would have finished the game.
If she had more time, she would have finished the game.
If I had charged the controller, it would work now.

kahoot.explain: Type 2 (hozirgi noreal): If + Past Simple, would + V1.

kahoot.q: If I had bought it last year, it ___ cheaper.
kahoot.explain: Type 3 (o'tgan noreal): If + Past Perfect, would have + V3.

options: If I had studied more, I would be successful now.
If I studied more, I would have been successful now.
If I had studied more, I would have been successful now.
If I would study more, I would be successful now.

options: If + Past Simple, would have + V3
kahoot.explain: Mixed 1: If I had studied harder (o'tgan), I would be successful now (hozir).

kahoot.q: If I had a car, I would have ___ you to the VR centre yesterday.
kahoot.explain: would have + V3: drive → drove → driven.

kahoot.q: If Aziz hadn't left university, ___ he be a businessman today?
kahoot.explain: Mixed 1 savol: Would + S + V1 … today?

kahoot.q: If I weren't afraid of heights, I ___ the VR skydiving game last week.
kahoot.explain: Hozirgi xarakter (qo'rqaman) → o'tgan natija (last week): would have + V3.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap ARALASH (mixed) shart gap?
options: If she hadn't missed the bus, she would be here now.
If she misses the bus, she will be late.
If she missed the bus, she would be late.
If she had missed the bus, she would have been late.
kahoot.explain: hadn't missed (o'tgan) + would be here now (hozir) — Mixed 1. Qolganlari Type 1, 2, 3.

kahoot.q: You wear a VR ___ on your head to see the virtual world.
kahoot.explain: headset — VR shlem, boshga kiyiladigan qurilma.

kahoot.q: A game that makes you feel you are really inside it is ___.
kahoot.explain: immersive — butunlay sho'ng'itadigan (ichida bo'lgandek his qildiradigan).

kahoot.q: Your character in a virtual world is your ___.
kahoot.explain: avatar — virtual dunyodagi qahramoningiz.

kahoot.q: Some people feel dizzy when they use VR. This is motion ___.
kahoot.explain: motion sickness — harakat kasalligi (bosh aylanishi).

kahoot.q: Programs and apps are ___; the physical parts of a device are hardware.
kahoot.explain: software — dasturiy ta'minot; hardware — apparat qismi.

kahoot.q: Young doctors can practise operations with surgery ___.
kahoot.explain: surgery simulation — jarrohlik simulyatsiyasi.

kahoot.q: "eye strain" nimani anglatadi?
kahoot.explain: eye strain — ko'z charchog'i (ekranga uzoq qarashdan).

intro: EACH — har biri ALOHIDA (2 va undan ko'p): "Each student has a book."
EVERY — hammasi UMUMIY (3 va undan ko'p): "Every child needs love."
EITHER — ikkitadan istalgan BIRI: "Either road leads to the city." Inkor bilan: "I don't like either team" = "I like neither team". Ikkalasi birga — both + ko'plik: "Both roads lead…"
NEITHER — ikkitadan hech biri: "Neither option is good." (fe'l tasdiq!).

B1: each / either / neither of + the/them + ko'plik ot: "Neither of the teams was ready." Rasmiy yozuvda fe'l birlik; og'zakida ko'plik (were) ham uchraydi — testda birlik. EMAS: "every of the players".

class_ex.title: Reading — 5 ball (5 × 1), 7 daqiqa: The Silk Road: Then and Now
class_ex.type: Original matn (7-dars Travel + 8-dars History); TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
class_ex.instr: Read the text. Do the statements agree with the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. (Matnni o'qing. TRUE — matnga mos, FALSE — matnga zid, NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q.)
box: The Silk Road: Then and Now

For more than a thousand years, the Silk Road connected China with the Mediterranean. It was not really one road; it was a network of routes across deserts and mountains. Merchants travelled in caravans of camels, carrying silk, spices and paper. The journey was absolutely exhausting. Summers in the desert were too hot for travelling during the day, so caravans often moved at night. Nevertheless, trade continued for centuries, because the profits were very high.

Along the routes there were caravanserais - large buildings where travellers could rest, feed their animals and do business. They were usually built about one day's journey apart. Some were fairly simple, whereas others in big cities such as Bukhara had rooms for hundreds of people.

Today, travel along the old route is completely different. A modern tourist can go from Tashkent to Samarkand by fast train in just over two hours, whereas a caravan needed several days. However, many visitors say that the old cities still feel rather magical. Some caravanserais have become hotels, restaurants or museums. On the other hand, a few are almost ruined, and local historians worry that there is not enough money to protect them.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan original matn.)
items: 1. The Silk Road was a single road from China to the Mediterranean.
2. In summer, caravans often travelled in the dark because of the heat.
3. Silk was the most expensive product that the merchants carried.
4. Travellers could buy and sell goods at caravanserais.
5. Local historians have asked the government for money to protect the old caravanserais.
answers: 1. FALSE — 'It was not really one road; it was a network of routes'.
2. TRUE — 'too hot for travelling during the day, so caravans often moved at night'.
3. NOT GIVEN — mahsulotlar sanalgan (silk, spices, paper), lekin narxi solishtirilmagan.
4. TRUE — 'travellers could rest, feed their animals and do business'.
5. NOT GIVEN — tarixchilar faqat 'worry' (xavotirda); hukumatdan so'ragani aytilmagan.

class_ex.title: Grammar — 10 ball (10 × 1), 6 daqiqa
class_ex.type: MCQ (4 variant, bitta to'g'ri javob); har darsdan 2 ta: 1–2 — 6-dars, 3–4 — 7, 5–6 — 8, 7–8 — 9, 9–10 — 10
class_ex.instr: Choose the correct answer A, B, C or D. (To'g'ri javobni tanlang: A, B, C yoki D — faqat bittasi to'g'ri.)
items: 1. My little brother is only six. He isn't ___ to come on the long mountain hike with us. A) old enough B) enough old C) too old D) very old
2. After walking twenty kilometres in the heat, we were all ___ exhausted. A) very B) absolutely C) fairly D) enough
3. The hotel was rather old. ___, the rooms were clean and the staff were very friendly. A) Whereas B) Nevertheless C) Although D) While
4. My sister loves beach holidays, ___ I prefer sightseeing in old cities. A) however B) whereas C) nevertheless D) in contrast
5. I've looked for my passport in every room, but I can't find it ___. A) nowhere B) somewhere C) anywhere D) everywhere
6. After ten years ___, the old historian finally came ___ to Samarkand. A) in abroad / to home B) abroad / home C) abroad / to home D) in abroad / home
7. During the war, my great-grandfather worked ___ a nurse in a field hospital. A) like B) as C) as if D) such as
8. Why does he talk ___ he knew everything about genes? He started biology only a month ago! A) as B) such as C) as if D) the same as
9. If my parents hadn't given me a VR headset for my birthday, I ___ interested in 3D design now. A) wouldn't have been B) won't be C) wouldn't be D) didn't be
10. If Aziz ___ so forgetful, he wouldn't have left his controller on the bus yesterday. A) isn't B) weren't C) wouldn't be D) won't be
answers: 1. A) old enough — 6-dars: sifat + enough + to V (enough sifatdan keyin).
2. B) absolutely — 6-dars: kuchli sifat (exhausted) bilan very/fairly emas, absolutely.
3. B) Nevertheless — 7-dars: yangi gap boshida, vergul bilan; whereas/while/although vergul bilan yolg'iz turmaydi.
4. B) whereas — 7-dars: bitta gap ichida farq; however/nevertheless/in contrast vergul bilan ikki gapni ulamaydi.
5. C) anywhere — 8-dars: inkor gapda anywhere (can't … nowhere — ikki inkor).
6. B) abroad / home — 8-dars: abroad va home predlogsiz (live abroad, come home).
7. B) as — 9-dars: as + ot = haqiqiy vazifa (u haqiqatan hamshira bo'lgan).
8. C) as if — 9-dars: as if + Past Simple = noreal (aslida hamma narsani bilmaydi).
9. C) wouldn't be — 10-dars: Mixed 1 — o'tgan shart (hadn't given), hozirgi natija (now).
10. B) weren't — 10-dars: Mixed 2 — doimiy xarakter (If + Past Simple), o'tgan natija (would have + V3).

class_ex.title: Writing — 12 ball (W-B1: 4 mezon × 0–3), 12 daqiqa
class_ex.type: IELTS Task 2 uslubidagi savol — BITTA paragraf, 80–100 so'z
class_ex.instr: Read the question. Write ONE paragraph of 80–100 words. Give your opinion, two reasons and an example. Use linking words (however, in contrast, for example, therefore). (Savolni o'qing. 80–100 so'zlik BITTA paragraf yozing: fikringiz, ikkita sabab va misol; bog'lovchilardan foydalaning.)
items: 1. Is it better to travel to other countries or to explore your own country? Give reasons for your answer.

2. Checklist (o'quvchi uchun): birinchi gapda fikringiz; 2 ta sabab + 1 ta misol; kamida 3 xil bog'lovchi (however, in contrast, for example, therefore, because); 6–10-darslar grammatikasidan kamida 2 ta (however / whereas, too / enough / absolutely, abroad / home, as if, mixed conditional); Travel yoki History lug'atidan kamida 3 so'z; 80–100 so'z.
answers: NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, W-B1 ≈ 11–12 ball, 96 so'z): In my opinion, it is better to explore your own country first. Travelling abroad is exciting; however, it is often too expensive for young people, because flights, accommodation and travel insurance cost a lot. In contrast, a trip inside Uzbekistan is fairly cheap, and you can learn a lot about your own cultural heritage. For example, last spring I visited Khiva with my class, and the ancient walls were absolutely amazing. If I hadn't gone on that trip, I wouldn't know so much about our history now. Therefore, young people should start their journeys at home.

Baholash: W-B1 jadvali (keyingi bo'lim). Namunadagi elementlar: pozitsiya — 1-gap; bog'lovchilar — however, in contrast, for example, therefore; daraja ravishlari — too expensive, fairly cheap, absolutely amazing; mixed conditional — If I hadn't gone…, I wouldn't know… now; CORE — accommodation, travel insurance, cultural heritage, journey, ancient.

class_ex.type: Faqat ustoz uchun — asosiy testda berilmaydi; O'TMADI yoki Writing < 4 bo'lgan o'quvchilar uchun
class_ex.instr: Write ONE paragraph of 80–100 words. Give your opinion, two reasons and an example. (80–100 so'zlik BITTA paragraf: fikringiz, ikkita sabab va misol.)
items: 1. Some people think that virtual tours can replace real travel. Do you agree or disagree? Give reasons for your answer.
2. Checklist: asosiy mavzudagi talablar bilan bir xil; Virtual reality (10-dars) yoki Travel (7-dars) lug'atidan kamida 3 so'z.
answers: NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, 99 so'z): I disagree that virtual tours can replace real travel. A virtual tour is cheap and interactive, and the graphics in modern headsets are quite realistic. However, you cannot taste the local food or talk to the locals in a virtual world. For example, I once took a virtual tour of Bukhara, but it felt completely different when I walked there and bought a souvenir at the market. If I had only seen the city on a screen, I wouldn't remember it so well now. Therefore, VR is useful for planning, but not as a replacement for a real journey.
Baholash: W-B1 jadvali (4 mezon × 0–3 = 12). Qayta topshirishda 4+ ball — writing talabi bajarildi.
