class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Working from home: pros and cons
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ each / every / either / neither (+ birlik fe'l).
items: Part 1: Do you know anyone who works from home?
Part 1: Where do you usually do your homework — at home or somewhere else?
Part 3: Why do many companies now let their workers work from home?
Part 3: What are the benefits of working from home for parents with small children?
Part 3: What problems can people have if they work from home every day?
Part 3: Can every job be done from home? Which jobs cannot?
Part 3: For a young worker, is either option better — working in an office or working at home?
answers: Yes, my uncle does. He is a web designer in Tashkent, and he works from home every day. Each morning he starts at nine, just like in an office.
Usually at home, in my room. Sometimes I go to the library in our mahalla, but either place is fine for me if it is quiet.

I think the main reason is money. If every worker stays at home, the company doesn't need a big office, so it saves on rent and electricity. For example, many IT companies in Tashkent now rent smaller offices. Also, each worker saves time because there is no commute.

The main advantage is that parents can stay close to their children. They can take each child to kindergarten in the morning and cook lunch at home. For example, my aunt has flexible hours, so she sees her son every afternoon. On the other hand, small children can be a big distraction.

Well, I think the biggest problem is isolation. When you work alone every day, you don't see your colleagues, and you can feel lonely. Another problem is distraction, for example, noisy neighbours, TV or housework. So not every person can stay productive at home.

No, not every job can be done from home. Doctors, bus drivers and builders have to be at work, because each of them works with people or machines. For example, a doctor in a Samarkand hospital cannot check every patient online. But office jobs, like accounting, are easier to do at home.

In my view, the office is better for a young worker. Neither option is perfect, but in an office you can learn from experienced colleagues every day. For example, my cousin learned most of his skills from his boss in his first job. Later, when you have experience, working at home is fine.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Working from home: pros and cons
class_ex.instr: More and more people now work from home instead of going to an office every day. What are the advantages and disadvantages of working from home? Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval; uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: advantages / disadvantages (afzalliklar va kamchiliklar; fikr so'ralmagan — xulosada qisqa umumiy baho yetarli)
2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: more and more people / work from home / instead of going to an office / advantages and disadvantages

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: afzalliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + fikr, agar savol so'rasa)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of … is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, … also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: each / every + birlik ot + birlik fe'l; either / neither (of) … + birlik fe'l — 2+ marta
answers: Namuna kirish (35 so'z): Nowadays, more and more people in Uzbekistan do their jobs at home instead of travelling to an office every morning. This way of working has some clear benefits, but it also has a few drawbacks.

Namuna AD jadval: Afzalliklar — 1) commute yo'q: vaqt va pul tejaladi (Toshkent metrosida har kuni 1 soat); 2) flexible hours: ota-ona bolani maktabga olib boradi — work-life balance; Kamchiliklar — 1) distraction: televizor, uy ishlari, shovqinli qo'shnilar — productivity tushadi; 2) isolation: colleagues bilan uchrashmaydi, yosh xodim yolg'izlik his qiladi.

Namuna insho (183 so'z) — kirish: Nowadays, more and more people in Uzbekistan do their jobs at home instead of travelling to an office every morning. This way of working has some clear benefits, but it also has a few drawbacks.

Namuna insho — body 1: One major advantage of working from home is that people save time and money. There is no long commute, so a worker in Tashkent does not spend an hour on the metro each day. Another benefit is flexible hours. For example, parents can start early and still take every child to school, which improves their work-life balance.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, working from home also has some drawbacks. Firstly, a home is full of distractions, such as television, housework or noisy neighbours, so productivity can fall. Secondly, people may suffer from isolation because they do not meet their colleagues. For instance, a young designer working alone every day may feel lonely.

Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, working from home saves time and gives people freedom, but it can also cause distraction and loneliness. Neither option is perfect for every person, so a mix of office and home days may be best.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — every morning, each day, every child, every day, Neither option is…, every person; bog'lovchilar — Nowadays, but, so, Another benefit, For example, which, On the other hand, Firstly, Secondly, because, For instance, In conclusion; mavzu so'zlari — commute, flexible hours, work-life balance, distractions, productivity, isolation, colleagues, drawbacks, benefits.
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 11-qator ("Pros and cons of working from home."); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Test darsi: sinfda faqat AD jadval (4 daq), to'liq insho — uyda. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). PEER-AD (juftlik, Ha/Yo'q): 1) savol o'z so'zlari bilan? 2) afzallik va kamchilik alohida xatboshida? 3) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol? 4) 4+ bog'lovchi? 5) dars grammatikasi 2+? 6) 150+ so'z (sinfda kirish 35–45)? reading.title: Rustam Kasimdzhanov — the Uzbek who became FIDE World Chess Champion
text: Rustam Kasimdzhanov was born in 1979 in Tashkent. Every young chess player dreams of the grandmaster title, but each year only a small number of players get it. Kasimdzhanov became a grandmaster in 1997, at the age of 17.

In 2004 the FIDE World Chess Championship was held in Tripoli, Libya, as a knockout tournament: 128 players started, and after each round half of them went home. Few people expected the underdog from Uzbekistan to go far. But he beat every opponent, including some of the strongest players in the world, and in the final he faced Michael Adams of England. Each of the six classical games was hard; neither player could get a clear lead, and the match went to tiebreaks. Kasimdzhanov won and became FIDE World Champion.

He never won the title again, but many top players know his name. He has worked as a second (an assistant) for top players such as Viswanathan Anand and Fabiano Caruana, helping them prepare openings for their world championship matches. He believes that there is no easy way in chess: every player must work hard, day after day.

Uzbek chess has grown fast since then. In 2022 a very young Uzbek team won the Chess Olympiad. For many young chess players in Uzbekistan, his victory in 2004 showed that each of them could reach the top too.

transcript: ASSISTANT: Good morning, Chilonzor Youth Football Club. How can I help you?
MALIKA: Hi. I'd like to join the club, please.
ASSISTANT: Great. Can I have your full name?
MALIKA: Malika Tursunova. That's T-U-R-S-U-N-O-V-A. [Q1]
ASSISTANT: The girls train on Saturdays, and you can choose one extra day. Either Tuesday or Thursday is fine.
MALIKA: Tuesday, please — oh, wait, I have a piano lesson then. Thursday. [Q2]
ASSISTANT: OK. Each member pays 150,000 som a month — sorry, that was last year's price. It's 180,000 now. [Q3]
MALIKA: Do I need to buy anything?
ASSISTANT: Every player needs a kit. The shirt and shorts are free, but you must bring your own boots. [Q4] Some girls also bring gloves or a cap, but neither is necessary.
MALIKA: When is the first match?
ASSISTANT: Our first match in the city tournament is on the 14th of October — no, sorry, the 15th. [Q5] Our opponents are strong, but each girl gets a chance to play.
MALIKA: Who is the coach?
ASSISTANT: Mr Aliev — oh no, he works with the boys. Your coach is Ms Nazarova, N-A-Z-A-R-O-V-A. [Q6] She was a team captain for many years.
MALIKA: Do I need to qualify for the team?
ASSISTANT: Not for training. Before every match the coach chooses the players. Neither of our teams lost a game last season!
MALIKA: Great! See you on Thursday.

intro: ANY — istalgan (3+ dan qaysi biri bo'lsa ham): "Any student can answer." Ko'pincha birlik ot bilan, lekin ko'plik va sanalmas ot bilan ham: "Any students can apply.", "Any help is welcome."
BOTH — ikkalasi (2): "Both players are ready." both of them / both the boys / both … and …
ALL — hammasi (3+): "All students have passed."; all + sanalmas: "All information is useful."
NONE — hech biri (3+): "None of the books is available." (rasmiy — birlik; og'zaki — are; ikkalasi ham to'g'ri). Yolg'iz ham: "There were none left."
Juftlar: either/any, neither/none, both/all — 2 va 3+.
formulas: Any + birlik ot (ko'pincha) / ko'plik yoki sanalmas ot
Any student can answer the question. / Any students can apply.
Istalgan talaba bu savolga javob bera oladi. / Istalgan talabalar ariza topshirishi mumkin.
All + ko'plik ot + ko'plik fe'l / All + sanalmas + birlik
All students have passed the exam. / All information is useful.
Barcha talabalar imtihondan o'tdi. / Barcha ma'lumot foydali.
None of + ko'plik ot + birlik (rasmiy) / ko'plik (og'zaki) fe'l
None of the books is available.
both / either / neither (2) — all / any / none (3+)
Neither parent works. / None of the parents work.
Ota-onaning hech biri ishlamaydi. / Ota-onalarning hech biri ishlamaydi.
both of / all of / none of / any of + olmosh/the + ot
Both of them agree. / All of the money was donated. / None of us knew.
Ikkalasi ham rozi. / Hamma pul ehson qilindi. / Hech birimiz bilmasdik.
presentation: Are both problems serious?
Yes, both poverty and unemployment are serious.

notes: both … and: "Both poverty and hunger are problems." neither … nor / either … or — 13-dars.
all day / all night / all the time — vaqt iboralari.
none of + guruh: None of my friends came. no one / nobody — of bilan kelmaydi (No one of my friends — xato).
none of + ko'plik ot: rasmiy (IELTS Writing) — birlik fe'l (None of the solutions is quick.), og'zaki — ko'plik (None of them are ready.); ikkalasi ham to'g'ri — 13-darsda ham shu qoida.
CCQ: Both players are ready. — How many players? (Two) Is one of them not ready? (No)
CCQ: None of the five students came. — Did any student come? (No) Can we say 'neither' here? (No — 3+)
CCQ: Any volunteer can join. — Is it only one special volunteer? (No — whichever volunteer)
CCQ: All the money was donated. — Is any money left? (No) Money — countable? (No, so 'was')

all of + the / olmosh + ot; 'all of students' — xato.

class_ex.title: Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Your city
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda. Part 1 — savol-javob; Part 2 — 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik, 1–2 daqiqa gapiring; Part 3 — muhokama. Har javobda 1+ any / both / all / none.
items: Part 1: What do you like about your city?
Part 1: Is there enough public transport?
Part 1: Are there any parks near your home?
Part 1: Do both young and old people like living there?
Part 2 card: Describe a problem in your town or city and how it could be solved. You should say: what the problem is / who it affects / why it happens — and explain what could be done.
Part 3: Whose job is it to solve city problems — the government's or the people's?
Part 3: Can young people help their community?
answers: I like the old streets and the markets. All of my friends live nearby, so we meet almost every day.
Not really. There are buses, but none of them come on time in the morning, so many people use taxis.
Yes, there are two small parks. Both of them are nice, but they are always full at weekends.
Mostly, yes. Young people like the cafés, and old people like the quiet mahalla. But not all of them like the traffic.

I'd like to talk about traffic in my city. In the morning, all of the main roads are full of cars, and buses are often late. The problem affects everyone: students, workers and old people. Both of my parents spend more than an hour in traffic every day. It happens because the city is growing fast and many families now have two cars, but public transport has not grown as quickly. I think the government could build more metro lines and bus lanes. Also, any big company could let some workers start later. None of these solutions is quick, but together they could make a big difference.
I think both of them are responsible. The government has the money for big projects, but people can also help, for example by keeping the streets clean.
Yes, all of them can do something. They can volunteer, clean parks or raise awareness online. Any small action helps the community.

class_ex.title: Writing (IELTS Task 2): problem–solution
class_ex.instr: In many cities, young people cannot find jobs after they finish school. What are the causes of this problem, and what solutions can you suggest? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 180 words. — Sinfda: reja + kirish (40–50 so'z); uyda to'liq insho (Writing 5).
items: 1) Savol turi: problem–solution — ikkala qismga javob bering (causes + solutions).
2) Kalit so'zlar: young people, cannot find jobs, causes, solutions.
3) Reja: kirish → Body 1: 2 sabab + misol → Body 2: 2 yechim + misol → xulosa.
4) Gap boshlanmalari: One cause is that … / Another reason is … / One solution would be to …
answers: Namuna kirish (46 so'z): In many cities today, a large number of young people cannot find work after they leave school. This unemployment is a serious problem for both families and society. In this essay, I will explain the main causes and suggest some solutions that could help all school leavers.
Reja: Body 1 (sabablar) — none of the school subjects teaches practical job skills; almost all companies want workers with experience, so any first job is hard to get.
Body 2 (yechimlar) — schools and companies could offer internships to all final-year students; the government could support young people who start small businesses.
Xulosa — the problem is serious, but both schools and the government can help if they work together.

reading.title: Malala Yousafzai — all girls have the right to learn
text: A. Malala Yousafzai was born in 1997 in the Swat Valley in Pakistan. Her father ran a school, and both of her parents believed that all children — boys and girls — should study. But in early 2009 the Taliban, who controlled much of the valley, banned girls from going to school. Thousands of girls had to stay at home, and none of them knew when they could go back to class.

B. Malala was only 11, and any girl who spoke out was in danger. Yet she started writing a blog for the BBC about life without school. Later, both her name and her face became known. In October 2012, a gunman stopped her school bus and shot her. She was badly hurt and was taken to a hospital in England, where she slowly recovered.

C. After her recovery she did not stop. On her 16th birthday she spoke at the United Nations and told the world that one child, one teacher, one book and one pen can change the world. In 2014, at the age of 17, she won the Nobel Peace Prize. Her organisation, the Malala Fund, works in several countries, and all of its projects have one goal: 12 years of free, safe education for every girl.

D. In 2020 Malala graduated from Oxford University. She has visited many countries, and both students and presidents listen to her. She often says that her story is not unique — it is the story of many girls. None of them, she believes, should be silent.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 3 — matching. Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to questions 1–5.
You will hear two students, Nodira and Timur, discussing the results of their survey about problems in their city.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): 1–5 va A–F ni o'qing, kalit so'zlarni (all, none, both, any, more) belgilang. Bitta variant ortiqcha.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: NODIRA: Timur, have you counted the answers to our survey? We asked two groups — sixty students and forty adults — about problems in our city.
TIMUR: Yes. Let's start with traffic. All of the people we asked said it's serious. Not one person disagreed. [Q1]
NODIRA: No surprise. What about rubbish in the streets?
TIMUR: At first I thought the adults were angry about it… Actually, no — both groups said the situation is getting better now that the city has put new bins in every street. [Q2]
NODIRA: Good. And unemployment?
TIMUR: The students are worried about jobs after school, but the adults mentioned it much more often. Many of them have children who can't find work, and some said unemployment leads to poverty. [Q3]
NODIRA: And parks? I think the adults complained about that.
TIMUR: I expected that too, but no. None of the adults mentioned parks. Only the students wrote that there's nowhere to play football. [Q4]
NODIRA: Last one — noise.
TIMUR: Both groups find it annoying, especially at night. But they said any solution — like new windows or moving the bus station — would cost a lot of money. [Q5]
NODIRA: So what's our conclusion for the community project?
TIMUR: Our society needs more awareness. People want change, but none of these problems can be solved by the government alone.

intro: THE NUMBER OF + ko'plik ot + BIRLIK fe'l (son bitta): "The number of students is increasing."
A NUMBER OF + ko'plik ot + KO'PLIK fe'l (= many): "A number of students are late."
NONE / SOME / ALL / MOST OF + ko'plik ot → ko'plik fe'l (none of: rasmiy Writing'da birlik, og'zaki ko'plik — ikkalasi to'g'ri); + sanalmas ot → birlik: "Some of the water is cold."
EITHER … OR / NEITHER … NOR — fe'l OXIRGI egaga mos: "Either John or his friends are coming." / "Neither the students nor the teacher is here."
GERUND ega → birlik: "Swimming is fun." ONE OF THE + ko'plik → birlik: "One of the students is absent."
formulas: The number of + ko'plik ot + birlik fe'l
The number of students is increasing.
A number of + ko'plik ot + ko'plik fe'l
A number of students are late.
+ ko'plik ot + ko'plik fe'l (none of — rasmiy: birlik ham)
None of them are here. (rasmiy: is) / Some of the habits are bad.
Ularning hech biri bu yerda emas. / Ba'zi odatlar yomon.
Either John or his friends are coming. / Neither my friends nor I am ready.
Jon yoki uning do'stlari kelyapti. / Do'stlarim ham, men ham tayyor emasman.
Swimming is fun. / Reading every day builds knowledge.
Suzish qiziqarli. / Har kuni o'qish bilimni oshiradi.
One of the + ko'plik ot + birlik fe'l
One of the students is absent.
presentation: Is the number of readers growing?
Yes, the number of readers is growing every year.
Why are so many students late today?
A number of them are late because of the rain.
What is one of your bad habits?
One of my bad habits is checking my phone too often.
Does journaling help?
Journaling helps a lot — writing every day is powerful.
Who is coming — your mentor or your parents?
Either my mentor or my parents are coming.
Are all of your goals written down?
All of my goals are written in a notebook.
Is all of the advice in this book useful?
Some of the advice is useful, but not all of it.
Do laziness or fear ever stop you?
Neither fear nor laziness stops me now.
What is one of the keys to success?
One of the keys to success is self-discipline.
Is the information about time management free?
Yes, the information is free online.
notes: Sanalmas otlar birlik: information, advice, knowledge, progress, feedback, homework — "The advice is good."
Collective nouns (team, family): Britaniyada ko'plik fe'l ham mumkin (the team are).
there is / there are — keyingi otga qarab: "There is a mentor" / "There are a number of mentors".
CCQ: The number of students is growing. — One number or many students? (one number)
CCQ: A number of students are late. — Is it one student? (No, several)
CCQ: Either my mentor or my parents are coming. — Which subject is closer to the verb? (my parents → are)
CCQ: One of my habits is journaling. — One habit or many? (one → is)

The number of students is increasing.
A number of students is late.
A number of students are late.
One of the students are absent.
One of the students is absent.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Online shopping: benefits and drawbacks
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ ega–kesim mosligi holati (The number of … is / A number of people are / Shopping online is / One of the … is / Everyone who … has).
items: Part 1: How often do you buy things online?
Part 1: What was the last thing you bought online?
Part 3: Why do a number of people prefer shopping online to going to the bazaar?
Part 3: What kinds of products are better to buy in a real shop? Why?
Part 3: What problems can people have when they buy things online?
Part 3: How can buyers protect themselves from fake products and online scams?
Part 3: Has online shopping changed the way young people spend money?
answers: Not very often, maybe once or twice a month. Buying clothes online is risky for me, but a number of my friends order snacks and phone cases online every week.
It was a pair of wireless headphones last week. One of the reasons I bought them online was the price: they were about twenty percent cheaper than in a shop.

I think the main reason is time. Shopping online saves a lot of time, because you don't need to travel across the city or stand in long queues. For example, my mother works until seven, so ordering food and household things online is much easier for her. Also, a number of websites offer free delivery.

Well, I'd say clothes, shoes and fresh food. Trying on clothes is important, because sizes are often different on websites. For example, at Chorsu bazaar you can touch the fruit and choose the best ones yourself. So for these things, a real shop or market is a safer choice.

The main problem is quality. Sometimes the product in the photo looks great, but the real one is cheap and badly made. Another problem is late delivery. For example, one of my classmates ordered a jacket for the winter, and it arrived in March! Also, returning things is not always easy.

First of all, buyers should read customer reviews carefully. Everyone who shops online has to check the seller's rating. Another good idea is paying only on the official website, never by sending money to a stranger's card. For example, if a price is fifty percent lower than in other shops, it is probably a fake.

Yes, I think it has. The number of young people who shop on their phones is growing every year, and buying things with one click is very easy. On the other hand, this leads to impulse buying. For example, my cousin often buys cheap things he doesn't need just because there is a discount.
class_ex.note: ICQ: Necha gapda javob berasiz? (3–4) — Misol kerakmi? (Ha). class_ex.title: WRITING — Online shopping: benefits and drawbacks
class_ex.instr: Online shopping is becoming more popular than shopping in traditional stores. What are the benefits and drawbacks of shopping online? Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval + kirish (35–45 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi (Writing 6)
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: advantages/disadvantages (benefits and drawbacks) — ikkala tomon alohida xatboshida; savol fikr so'ramaydi, xulosada qisqa fikr bildirsa bo'ladi.
2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: online shopping, more popular, traditional stores, benefits, drawbacks.

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: afzalliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + fikr, agar savol so'rasa)

4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of online shopping is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, online shopping also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, … Mavzu so'zlari: delivery, discount, compare prices, customer reviews, return, fake products, impulse buying.
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: ega–kesim mosligi 2+ marta (The number of online shoppers is growing / A number of websites offer / Comparing prices takes … / One of the main drawbacks is …)
answers: Namuna kirish (42 so'z): Nowadays, the number of people who buy things on the internet is growing quickly. In Uzbekistan, many shoppers now prefer ordering on their phones to visiting traditional shops and bazaars. This essay will discuss the main benefits and drawbacks of shopping online.

Namuna AD jadval: Afzalliklar — 1) qulaylik: istalgan vaqtda buyurtma, eshikkacha tez delivery (misol: kechgacha ishlaydigan ona oziq-ovqatni onlayn buyuradi); 2) narxlarni solishtirish va discount (misol: bitta telefon turli saytlarda turli narxda); Kamchiliklar — 1) mahsulotni ushlab yoki kiyib ko'rib bo'lmaydi — o'lcham xato, return qiyin (misol: noto'g'ri o'lchamdagi kiyim); 2) fake products va firibgarlik — customer reviews ni o'qish shart (misol: boshqa do'konlardan 50% arzon narx — shubhali).

Namuna insho (187 so'z) — kirish: Nowadays, the number of people who buy things on the internet is growing quickly. In Uzbekistan, many shoppers now prefer ordering on their phones to visiting traditional shops and bazaars. This essay will discuss the main benefits and drawbacks of shopping online.

Namuna insho — body 1: One major advantage of online shopping is convenience. Customers can order almost anything at any time, and delivery to their door is usually fast. Another benefit is that comparing prices takes only a few minutes. For example, a number of websites offer different prices for the same phone, so buyers can choose the best discount.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, online shopping also has some drawbacks. One of the main drawbacks is that buyers cannot touch or try the product before they pay. As a result, clothes are often the wrong size, and returning them is not always easy. Moreover, there are many fake products online, so everyone who uses a new website has to read customer reviews first.
Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, shopping online saves time and money, but fake products and wrong sizes are real risks. In my view, it is best for simple, everyday things.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — the number of people … is growing; comparing prices takes; a number of websites offer; One of the main drawbacks is; returning them is; everyone who uses … has; shopping online saves; bog'lovchilar — Nowadays, Another benefit, For example, On the other hand, As a result, Moreover, In conclusion; mavzu so'zlari — delivery, comparing prices, discount, returning, fake products, customer reviews, online shopping, traditional shops.

reading.title: Abdulla Avloni — a teacher of character
text: A. Abdulla Avloni was born in 1878 in Tashkent, in a family of craftsmen. Reading was his passion from childhood. As a young man he started teaching, and in 1904 he opened his own school — a new-method school, where children learned by understanding, not by repeating. At that time the number of new-method schools in Tashkent was still small, and a number of parents were afraid of them.

B. Avloni believed that education is not only knowledge. One of his most famous books is "Turkiy Guliston yoxud Axloq" (The Turkic Garden, or Ethics), a textbook from 1913 about good and bad qualities of character, such as patience, courage and honesty. In this book he wrote that upbringing was a matter of life or death for the nation. A number of his ideas — daily habits, self-control, learning from mistakes — are close to what modern books on personal development teach.

C. He was also a playwright. He started one of the first Uzbek theatre groups, because he believed that a play could teach people as well as a lesson could. After 1917 he worked as a diplomat in Afghanistan and later taught in Tashkent again.
D. Avloni died in 1934. Neither fame nor money was his main goal; teaching was. Today many teachers see him as a role model, and none of his ideas about character has lost its value.

tasks.instr: Do the statements agree with the information in the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

"Turkiy Guliston yoxud Axloq" was translated into Russian.

Avloni worked in Afghanistan after 1917.
answers: FALSE (a number of parents were afraid)
tasks.note: NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q; FALSE — matn teskarisini aytadi. Faqat matnga tayaning, o'z bilimingizga emas.

listening.audios: Jony Academy original skripti — ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi. Kitob AUDIO 106–110 — ixtiyoriy, uyda.
intro: IELTS Listening Part 2 — multiple choice. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
You will hear a study coach talking to students about habits.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, kalit so'zlarni belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: COACH: Good morning, everyone. I'm Timur Rahimov, a study coach, and today I want to talk about habits.

COACH: Last year we asked six hundred students about their routines. The number of students who sleep less than seven hours is growing every year, and a number of students have no fixed time for homework.

COACH: So what is my main advice? Many people expect me to say 'study for more hours'. But no — the most important thing is to go to bed at the same time every night. [Q1] Sleep is your first priority.

COACH: Which habit is the hardest to build? You might think it's getting up early. But in our research, putting the phone away while studying was the most difficult [Q2] — and it is the best thing for your focus.
COACH: Students who read for twenty minutes a day remembered forty per cent more new words — sorry, thirty per cent more. [Q3] Reading every day is a small habit with big results.
COACH: Each of us has the same twenty-four hours. That's why we made a free app called StepUp. It doesn't teach English or maths — it simply helps you track your habits. [Q4]

COACH: Finally, neither motivation nor willpower lasts for ever, so change one habit at a time. Many books say three weeks is enough, but I'd say try it for two months [Q5] before you add the next one.

tasks.title: Multiple choice — A, B or C
tasks.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
items: 1 What is the coach's main piece of advice? A) study for more hours B) go to bed at the same time every night C) get up early
2 According to the research, which habit was the hardest for students? A) getting up early B) reading every day C) putting the phone away while studying
3 Students who read 20 minutes a day remembered … more new words. A) 20% B) 30% C) 40%
4 What is the StepUp app for? A) learning English B) practising maths C) tracking habits
5 How long does the coach suggest trying one habit before adding the next? A) three weeks B) two months C) one year

intro: -ING CLAUSE — ega o'zi bajaradi, asosiy gap bilan bir vaqtda yoki sabab: "Walking down the street, she saw an old friend." (= While she was walking…) "Feeling tired, I went to bed." (= Because I felt tired…)
-ING EGA SIFATIDA — gerund: "Studying late at night is tiring." (+ birlik fe'l).
-ED CLAUSE — egaga nisbatan bajarilgan (passiv): "Shocked by the news, he couldn't say a word." (= Because he was shocked…) "Built in 2015, the model is old."
Otdan keyin: "The student sitting there is Ali." (= who is sitting) / "The data collected by sensors is huge." (= which was collected).
Ega bir xil bo'lishi shart: "Walking home, the rain started" — xato (yomg'ir yurmaydi).

I'd like to talk about a translation app on my phone. Recommended by my cousin, it was the first AI tool I installed last year. class_ex.answers: Namuna (84 so'z): I disagree with the idea that young people no longer need university. Trained on huge datasets, AI can do many routine tasks, such as simple translation or data entry. However, working with AI still needs people who understand it. reading.title: Sam Altman and the rise of ChatGPT
text: Sam Altman was born in 1985 in Chicago. Given his first computer at the age of eight, he soon learned to program. Studying at Stanford University, he started a company called Loopt at 19 — and, wanting to work on it full-time, he dropped out. Later he ran Y Combinator, a well-known startup accelerator.

In 2015 Altman, Elon Musk and several others founded OpenAI as a non-profit research lab. Its goal was to make artificial intelligence safe and useful for everyone. Trained on huge amounts of text from the internet, OpenAI's language models became better every year. Then, in November 2022, the company released ChatGPT. Used by an estimated 100 million people in about two months, it became one of the fastest-growing apps in history. Students in Tashkent, doctors in London and farmers in India were all typing prompts into the same chatbot.
In November 2023 something strange happened: Altman was fired by OpenAI's board. Shocked by the decision, most of the company's employees threatened to leave. A few days later he was back as CEO.

Altman believes that AI will change the way people work and learn. Worried about risks such as job displacement and deepfakes, he asked US lawmakers in 2023 to regulate AI — including products like his own. Not everyone trusts him; critics say that a company growing this fast cannot control itself. But one thing is clear: talking to a machine, we no longer feel surprised.

tasks.title: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: Do the statements agree with the information in the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
items: Altman finished his degree at Stanford.
OpenAI started as a non-profit in 2015.
Altman's parents bought him his first computer.
About 100 million people used ChatGPT in its first two months.
Altman never returned to OpenAI after he was fired.
The board explained its decision to the employees.
tasks.note: NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q; FALSE — matn teskarisini aytadi.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 4 — sentence completion. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear a short lecture about how AI assistants are trained and how people use them.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (raqam, ot, ibora) belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: LECTURER: Good afternoon. Today's short talk is about AI assistants, such as chatbots: how they are trained and how people use them.
LECTURER: Let's start with training. Trained on millions of texts from books and websites, the model learns patterns in language. [Q1]
LECTURER: Before training, engineers clean the dataset carefully, because bad data gives poor results.
LECTURER: Training a big model takes time. Using thousands of computers, engineers train it for about six weeks — sorry, I mean eight weeks for the biggest models. [Q2]
LECTURER: After that, the model is tested. Asked thousands of questions, it gets a score for accuracy. [Q3]
LECTURER: So, how do people use AI assistants? Many people think they are mainly for writing essays. In fact, the most common use is finding information. [Q4]
LECTURER: Using voice commands, users can also set alarms or send messages without touching the phone. [Q5]

LECTURER: Finally, some apps are made for education. Designed for students, one popular maths app explains each problem step by step, but it never gives the final answer. [Q6] Teachers like this, because students still have to think.
LECTURER: Remember: an AI assistant makes predictions — it doesn't really understand. So always check its answers.

tasks.title: Questions 1–6: Sentence completion
tasks.instr: Complete the sentences. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. (Gaplarni to'ldiring.)
items: Trained on millions of texts, the model learns (1) ________ in language.
The biggest models need about (2) ________ weeks of training.
After training, the model gets a score for its (3) ________.
The most common use of AI assistants is (4) ________.
With voice (5) ________, users can send messages without touching the phone.
The maths app designed for students never gives the (6) ________.

kahoot.q: ___ down the street, she saw an old friend.
kahoot.explain: Ega (she) o'zi yuradi, bir vaqtda → V-ing: Walking down the street = While she was walking.

kahoot.q: ___ by the news, he couldn't say a word.
kahoot.explain: Uni xabar hayratga soldi (passiv) → V3: Shocked by the news.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: Waiting for the bus, my phone battery died.
Waiting for the bus, I checked my messages.
Feeling tired, I went to bed.
Built in 2015, the model is old.
kahoot.explain: Batareya avtobus kutmaydi! Ikkala qismning egasi bir xil bo'lishi shart.

kahoot.q: The data ___ by sensors is huge.
kahoot.explain: Ma'lumot to'planadi (passiv): the data (which was) collected by sensors.

kahoot.q: Studying late at night ___ tiring.
kahoot.explain: Gerund ega (Studying...) — birlik fe'l: is.

kahoot.q: The robot ___ the room is new.
kahoot.explain: Robot o'zi tozalaydi (faol) → the robot (which is) cleaning the room.

kahoot.q: ___ the answer, he raised his hand.
kahoot.explain: Sabab, ega o'zi biladi → Knowing the answer = Because he knew the answer.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Katta ma'lumotda o'rgatilgan model yaxshiroq ishlaydi."
options: The model trained on big data works better.
The model training on big data works better.
The model trains on big data works better.
The model was trained on big data works better.
kahoot.explain: Model o'rgatilgan (passiv) → otdan keyin V3: the model trained on big data.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: Trained on data, the model makes predictions.
Training on data, the predictions are made.
Train on data, the model makes predictions.
kahoot.explain: Asosiy gapda ega kerak (the model) va model o'rgatiladi → Trained.

kahoot.q: -ed clause qachon ishlatiladi?
kahoot.explain: -ed (V3) clause — passiv: Shocked by the news = Because he was shocked.

kahoot.q: The student ___ there is Ali.
kahoot.explain: Relative clause qisqasi: the student (who is) sitting there → sitting.

kahoot.q: ___ in 2015, the chatbot is now quite old.
kahoot.explain: Chatbotni ishga tushirishgan (passiv) → Launched in 2015.

kahoot.q: A set of step-by-step rules that a computer follows is an ___.
kahoot.explain: algorithm — algoritm: kompyuter bajaradigan qadamma-qadam qoidalar.

kahoot.q: You type a ___ into ChatGPT to tell it what to do.
kahoot.explain: prompt — AI ga beriladigan buyruq/so'rov matni.

kahoot.q: My phone unlocks when it sees my face — this is ___ recognition.
kahoot.explain: facial recognition — yuzni tanish. voice recognition — ovozni tanish.

kahoot.q: A car that can drive without a human is a ___ car.
kahoot.explain: self-driving car — o'zi boshqariladigan (haydovchisiz) mashina.

kahoot.q: AI can show ___ if it is trained on unfair data.
kahoot.explain: bias — noxolislik, bir tomonga og'ish. Adolatsiz ma'lumot → noxolis AI.

kahoot.q: "autonomous" so'zining sinonimi qaysi?
kahoot.explain: autonomous — mustaqil, o'zi ishlaydigan = independent.

kahoot.q: A large collection of data used to train AI is a ___.
kahoot.explain: dataset — ma'lumotlar to'plami; AI shu bilan o'rgatiladi.

kahoot.q: "cybersecurity" nimani anglatadi?
kahoot.explain: cybersecurity — kiberxavfsizlik: tizim va ma'lumotlarni xakerlardan himoya qilish.

lessons.title: Relative Clauses with Who / Which
lessons.grammar_topic: ANIQLOVCHI ERGASH GAPLAR — WHO / WHICH / THAT (ega va to'ldiruvchi vazifasida)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 15 – Relative clauses with who/which (4 qatorli jadval); CRYPTOCURRENCY (48 so'z); Reading — Satoshi Nakamoto (Jony Academy matni, moslashtirilgan); kitob Topic 91–93 uyga (ixtiyoriy); kitob AUDIO 121–125 (ixtiyoriy); SPEAKING/WRITING mavzusi — rahbar rejasi (IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 15-qator): "The benefits and challenges of traveling abroad."
objectives: who (odam) / which (narsa) / that (ikkalasi) bilan ikki gapni bitta gapga birlashtira olish.
Ega va to'ldiruvchi relative clause'ni farqlash; faqat to'ldiruvchi olmoshni tushirish (The phone she bought).
Defining (vergulsiz, muhim ma'lumot) va non-defining (vergulli, qo'shimcha; that ishlatilmaydi) gaplarni to'g'ri tuzish.
Listening (IELTS Part 2): raqamli pul xavfsizligi haqidagi nutqdan eslatmadagi 6 bo'shliqni (raqam, ot) to'ldira olish.

SPEAKING (IELTS Part 3): Travelling abroad: benefits and challenges — 4–5 savolga 3–4 gapli javob (javob → sabab → misol), relative clause (who / which / that) bilan; WRITING: Travelling abroad: benefits and challenges — AD jadval sinfda, 150–200 so'zli insho uyda (W-B1-AD).
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 15 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.
CORE 20 varag'i — dars sahifasining Lug'at tabidan (PDF).
Kahoot: bu dars boshida o'ynalmaydi (Progress test 3); shu darsning Kahooti L16 boshida — 'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi (L15).
Progress test 3 (pt3) varaqlari + ustoz kaliti. Listening: skript ustozda (yashirin transcript), ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi.

Writing/Speaking rubrikasi — shu darsdagi W-B1-AD va S-B1-P3 jadvallari (WRITING mashqidan keyin); juftlik tekshiruvi — PEER-AD (WRITING mashqi izohida). Progress test E bo'limi — W-B1 (test ichidagi jadval).
timeline: Warm-up: odam → who, narsa → which

Ustoz: "A miner is a person. He checks transactions." → "A miner is a person who checks transactions." "Bitcoin is a currency. It has no bank." → "Bitcoin is a currency which has no bank." O'quvchilar qoidani topadi: odam → who, narsa → which.
PROGRESS TEST 3 (pt3) — 11–14-darslar

Listening 6 · Reading 7 · Grammar 6 · Vocabulary 4 · Writing 12 (daqiqa) — L5 · R5 · G10 · V8 · W12 = 40 ball; o'tish 28/40. Vocabulary bo'limida L14 Artificial intelligence CORE so'zlari (2+) — yozma normativ o'rniga. Tahlil — L16 da.
YANGI MAVZU: Relative clauses — who / which / that

10 daq: jadval (kitob yoki grammar.formulas) + presentation 1, 2, 3, 5, 10-savol-javoblar juftlikda. Ega (who/which + fe'l) tushirilmaydi, to'ldiruvchi (which + ega + fe'l) tushadi; non-defining — vergul, that yo'q. CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq amaliyot: 'Tushirsa bo'ladimi?' (1 — namuna).
Lug'at: Cryptocurrency — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

10 so'z: cryptocurrency, blockchain, digital wallet, private key, transaction, exchange, investor, volatility, risk, scam — so'z → ma'no → relative clause bilan 1 gap; 'Kripto lug'ati' (match) 2 daq. Qolgan CORE va STRONG — flashcard (uyda), SUPER — ixtiyoriy.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 4 qator)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. Me'yor — normativ[2].
Sinf mashqlari: who / which / that

who / which / that — 6 daq (yakka, 1 — namuna; juftlikda tekshirish). ZAXIRA: Ikki gapni birlashtiring (5 daq), Xatoni toping (3 daq), Ta'rif o'yini. Vaqt yetmasa: avval 'Ta'rif o'yini', keyin 'Xatoni toping' tashlanadi.
Listening (IELTS Part 2): note completion
2 daq tayyorgarlik; 1-tinglash; 1 daq juftlikda solishtirish; 2-tinglash; 3 daq javoblar — ustoz dalil gapni skriptdan o'qiydi.
Reading: T/F/NG + matching information
2 daq gist: 'Why is Satoshi a mystery?' (Nobody knows who he is.); 5 daq T/F/NG; 3 daq matching information (A–D). 'ZAXIRA: Relative clause toping' — kuchlilarga yoki uyga.
SPEAKING — Travelling abroad: benefits and challenges

1 daq Part 1 lead-in (2 savol, juftlikda) → 6 daq Part 3 juftlikda: A savol beradi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashadi; har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol (+ qarama-qarshi fikr) → 2 daq 2 o'quvchi sinf oldida bitta Part 3 savoliga javob beradi, ustoz S-B1-P3 bilan baholaydi → 1 daq feedback (1 kuchli tomon + 1 tuzatish + 1 foydali ibora).
WRITING — Travelling abroad: benefits and challenges
1 daq savol va 4 xatboshi rejasi (proyektorda) → 3 daq juftlikda AD jadval (2 + 2 g'oya, misol bilan, SPEAKING dan). Insho — uyda, MAJBURIY.
Uyga vazifa

MAJBURIY (~45 daq): CRYPTO CORE 20 flashcard + 5 tarjima gapi + WRITING — Travelling abroad inshosi + SPEAKING ovozli 2 javob. IXTIYORIY: ovozli normativ, Speaking Part 2 — Money, Topic 91–93, jadval yoddan, ZAXIRA mashqlar.

intro: WHO — odam: "The girl who called you is my cousin." (who = ega: who + fe'l).
WHO(M) — odam, to'ldiruvchi: "The boy (who) you met is my friend." (who + ega + fe'l → tushirsa bo'ladi; whom — rasmiy).
WHICH / THAT — narsa: "The car which broke down was expensive." (ega) / "The phone (which) she bought is new." (to'ldiruvchi, tushirsa bo'ladi).
Non-defining: qo'shimcha ma'lumot, vergul bilan, that EMAS: "Bitcoin, which was created in 2009, has no bank."
Ikki ega xatosi: "The phone which she bought it" — "it" ortiqcha.
formulas: The girl who called you is my cousin.
Senga qo'ng'iroq qilgan qiz — mening amakivachcham.
The boy (who) you met is my friend.
The car which broke down was expensive.
The phone (which) she bought is new.
Satoshi, who invented Bitcoin, is unknown.
The exchange (which) I trade on is safe.
presentation: Who is a miner?
A miner is a person who checks transactions and earns coins.
What is a blockchain?
It's a chain of blocks which stores every transaction.
Which coin did you buy?
The coin (that) I bought last year has lost half its value.
Who created Bitcoin?
It was created by someone who calls himself Satoshi Nakamoto.
What is a wallet?
A wallet is an app which keeps your private keys.
Do you know anyone who lost money in crypto?
Yes, a friend who invested in 2021 lost a lot.
What's a scam?
A scam is a project that promises profit but takes your money.
Which exchange do you use?
I use the exchange (which) my brother recommended.
Who is a whale?
A whale is an investor who owns a huge amount of coins.
What is volatility?
It's the thing that makes crypto risky: prices jump every day.
notes: who/which ega bo'lsa — tushirib bo'lmaydi; to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa — tushirsa bo'ladi.
Non-defining clause'da "that" yo'q va tushirib bo'lmaydi: "My father, who is 60, still trades."
whom — faqat to'ldiruvchi, rasmiy: "the investor whom we met" / "to whom".
Crypto lug'ati: blockchain, wallet, private key, mining, exchange, volatility, bull/bear market, scam.
Qavs '(which)/(that)/(who)' — faqat to'ldiruvchi vazifasida: qavsdan keyin ega keladi (The coin (which) I bought…), fe'l EMAS.
CCQ: The man who called me asked for a code. — Who called? (the man) Can we drop who? (No — it is the subject)
CCQ: The coin (which) I bought lost value. — Who bought? (I) Can we drop which? (Yes)
CCQ: Bitcoin, which was created in 2009, has no bank. — Is this extra information? (Yes) Can we use that here? (No)
mistakes: The man which sold me the coin…
The man who sold me the coin…
The app who I use is free.
The app (which/that) I use is free.
The phone which she bought it is new.
The phone which she bought is new.
The girl called you is my cousin.
The girl who called you is my cousin.

how: CORE 20 — kripto asosiy so'zlari (blockchain, wallet, mining…); STRONG — bozor va savdo so'zlari; SUPER — xavf va texnik atamalar.
Har so'zga relative clause: "A miner is a person who…" / "A token is a coin which…"
Moliyaviy savodxonlik — xavflarni tushunish; investitsiya maslahati berilmaydi.
core: A cryptocurrency is money which exists only online.
Kriptovalyuta — faqat onlayn mavjud bo'lgan pul.
A blockchain is a list of blocks that everyone can check.
Blokcheyn — hamma tekshira oladigan bloklar ro'yxati.
Bitcoin, which appeared in 2009, is the best-known cryptocurrency.
2009-yilda paydo bo'lgan Bitkoin — eng mashhur kriptovalyuta.
A token is a coin which is built on another blockchain.
Token — boshqa blokcheyn ustida qurilgan tanga.
The coin (that) I bought has doubled.
Men sotib olgan tanga ikki baravar oshdi.
A digital wallet is an app that stores your keys.
The private key is a password which nobody else should see.
Maxfiy kalit — boshqa hech kim ko'rmasligi kerak bo'lgan parol.
The public key is an address (which) you can share.
A transaction which is written in a block cannot be changed.
Mining is the work that creates new coins.
A miner is a person who checks transactions.
Each block, which holds many transactions, links to the block before it.
Ko'p tranzaksiyani saqlaydigan har bir blok o'zidan oldingi blokka bog'lanadi.
Bitcoin is decentralized, which means no bank controls it.
Bitkoin markazlashmagan, ya'ni uni hech qaysi bank boshqarmaydi.
An exchange is a website which lets you buy and sell coins.
Birja — tanga sotib olish va sotish imkonini beradigan sayt.
Trading is an activity that needs nerves of steel.
Treyding — po'lat asab talab qiladigan faoliyat.
Some investors who bought early became rich, but many lost money.
Erta sotib olgan ba'zi investorlar boyib ketdi, lekin ko'pchilik pul yo'qotdi.
Volatility is the thing that scares beginners.
A coin whose value can fall 50% in a day is a big risk.
Qiymati bir kunda 50% tushishi mumkin bo'lgan tanga — katta xavf.
The risk which people forget is losing the key.
A scam is a project that promises 100% profit a week.
Firibgarlik — haftasiga 100% foyda va'da qiladigan loyiha.
strong: A stablecoin is a coin which is tied to the dollar.
The address (which) you send coins to must be correct.
Tanga jo'natiladigan manzil to'g'ri bo'lishi kerak.
A bank is a centralized system which one company controls.
Bank — bitta kompaniya boshqaradigan markazlashgan tizim.
A trader who panics loses money.
Market cap is the number that shows a coin's total value.
Bozor kapitalizatsiyasi — tanganing umumiy qiymatini ko'rsatadigan raqam.
A bull market is a market which is rising; a bear market is one which is falling.
Ko'tariluvchi bozor — narxlar o'sayotgan bozor; tushuvchi bozor — narxlar tushayotgan bozor.
Liquidity is how easily a coin (that) you own can be sold.
Likvidlik — egalik qilgan tanganing qanchalik oson sotilishi.
Fiat money is money which a government prints.
Fiat pul — hukumat chop etadigan pul.
A smart contract is code that runs automatically.
Staking is a way that lets you earn money by holding coins.
Steyking — tangalarni ushlab turib daromad olish usuli.
The yield that they promised was too good to be true.
Ular va'da qilgan daromad haqiqat bo'lishi uchun juda yaxshi edi.
The exchange which was hacked lost millions of dollars.
Buzib kirilgan birja millionlab dollar yo'qotdi.
Security is the thing that matters most.
Anonymity is a feature which criminals also like.
Transparency means that anyone who wants to can see every transaction.
Shaffoflik — xohlagan har kim har bir tranzaksiyani ko'ra olishi.
Some governments that see crypto as risky want a ban on it.
Kriptoni xavfli deb biladigan ba'zi hukumatlar uni taqiqlashni xohlaydi.
Crypto adoption can grow fast in countries whose currencies are weak.
Valyutasi zaif mamlakatlarda kriptoning qabul qilinishi tez o'sishi mumkin.
The whitepaper is the document that explains a project.
The gas fee is the money (which) you pay for a transaction.
Gas to'lovi — tranzaksiya uchun to'lanadigan pul.
Peer-to-peer is trade between two people who don't use a bank.
Tengdan-tengga — bank ishlatmaydigan ikki odam o'rtasidagi savdo.
super: An airdrop is a gift of coins that a project gives to users.
Erdrop — loyiha foydalanuvchilarga beradigan tanga sovg'asi.
A fork is a change which splits one blockchain into two.
Fork — bitta blokcheynni ikkiga bo'ladigan o'zgarish.
A node is a computer which keeps a copy of the blockchain.
A bubble is a rise in prices which has no real value behind it.
Pufak — ortida real qiymati bo'lmagan narx o'sishi.
The crash of 2022 hit investors who had borrowed money.
2022-yildagi keskin tushish qarz olgan investorlarga zarba berdi.
A whale is an investor whose trades move the market.
Kit — savdolari bozorni harakatga keltiradigan investor.
Satoshi Nakamoto is a pseudonym which hides a real person or a group.
Satoshi Nakamoto — real odam yoki guruhni yashiradigan taxallus.
The identity of the person who created Bitcoin is unknown.
The blockchain is a ledger that nobody can erase.
Blokcheyn — hech kim o'chira olmaydigan hisob daftari.
The supply of Bitcoin, which is limited to 21 million coins, will never grow above that number.
21 million tanga bilan cheklangan Bitkoin taklifi hech qachon bu raqamdan oshmaydi.
Halving is an event that cuts miners' reward in half.
Halving — maynerlar mukofotini ikkiga qisqartiradigan hodisa.
Speculation is buying something (that) you hope to sell higher.
Spekulyatsiya — qimmatroq sotishni umid qilib sotib olish.
Many governments that worry about crypto want stronger regulation.
Kriptodan xavotirlanadigan ko'plab hukumatlar qat'iyroq tartibga solishni xohlaydi.
Legal tender is money which people must accept as payment.
Qonuniy to'lov vositasi — odamlar to'lov sifatida qabul qilishi shart bo'lgan pul.
People who call Bitcoin "digital gold" see it as savings.
Bitkoinni "raqamli oltin" deydiganlar uni jamg'arma deb biladi.
A cold wallet is a device which is not connected to the internet.
Phishing is a trick which uses fake websites.
Miners verify every transaction that enters a block.
Maynerlar blokka kiradigan har bir tranzaksiyani tasdiqlaydi.
Messages which are encrypted cannot be read by others.
Satoshi is a mystery that the internet has never solved.
Satoshi — internet hech qachon yechmagan jumboq.
normativ: Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan o'lchanadigan me'yor; bajarsa jurnalga '+' va coin, bajarmasa keyingi darsgacha qayta topshiradi.
Og'zaki: CORE 20 + tarjima, 1.5 daqiqa (ilovada, L16 gacha) — 1 coin.
Yozma (L16 boshida): 20 so'z, 4 daqiqa; 17/20+ — 2 coin. STRONG/SUPER — +2 / +3 coin.

class_ex.title: Progress Test 3 — 11–14-darslar: ustoz uchun o'tkazish tartibi va ball jadvali

Qamrov — faqat 11–14-darslar: each / every / either / neither, any / both / all / none, ega–kesim mosligi (the number of, a number of, neither … nor, one of the, gerund ega), -ing / -ed clauses; CORE lug'at: Sport, Social issues, Personal development, Artificial intelligence. 15-dars mavzusi (who / which / that, kriptovalyuta) testga KIRMAYDI.
items: 1. Darsdan oldin: o'quvchi varag'ini chop eting — A Listening savollari (1–5), B Reading matni va savollari, C Grammar, D Vocabulary (quti bilan), E Writing savoli. Listening skripti, javob kalitlari, namuna paragraf, zaxira writing mavzusi va qayta topshirish varag'i chop etilmaydi va o'quvchiga ko'rsatilmaydi. Skriptni uyda 1 marta ovoz chiqarib o'qib mashq qiling (taxminan 1 daq 10 s).

2. Warm-up ning oxirgi daqiqasida: telefonlar yig'iladi, o'quvchilar alohida o'tiradi, varaqqa ism va sana yoziladi, 'O'quvchi uchun yo'riqnoma' o'qib beriladi. Proyektorga faqat taymer va joriy bo'lim nomi chiqariladi; bu sahifa proyektorda ochilmaydi, 'Javobni ko'rsat' tugmasi test davomida bosilmaydi.

3. Vaqt: A Listening — 6 daq, B Reading — 7 daq, C Grammar — 6 daq, D Vocabulary — 4 daq, E Writing — 12 daq (jami 35 daq). Har bo'lim tugashiga 1 daqiqa qolganda ogohlantiring va keyingi bo'limni e'lon qiling; kech qolganga vaqt qo'shilmaydi.

4. A Listening tartibi (6 daq): 45 soniya — o'quvchilar 1–5 gaplarni o'qiydi; skript 1-marta o'qiladi (oddiy tezlikda, raqamlarni aniq); 20 soniya tanaffus; 2-marta o'qiladi; qolgan vaqt (taxminan 2 daq) — javoblarni tekshirish va toza yozish. Distraktorlarni (first → third, football/basketball → volleyball, 120,000 → 150,000, trophy → medal, healthy food → time management) ovoz bilan ta'kidlamang va takrorlamang.

5. B–D bo'limlar: o'quvchi mustaqil ishlaydi, ustoz savolga javob bermaydi (faqat 'Instruksiyani qayta o'qing'). E Writing (12 daq): 2 daq — reja, 9 daq — yozish, 1 daq — so'z sonini sanab, oxiriga yozish.

6. 35-daqiqada varaqlar yig'iladi. Kalit va natija test paytida aytilmaydi; natija tahlili 16-darsda ('PROGRESS TEST 3 tahlili', 8 daqiqa): har bo'limdan eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 band doskada tuzatiladi (asl C va D kaliti shu tariqa qisman ochiladi — shuning uchun qayta topshirish PARALLEL variantda); Writing — 2 ta umumiy xato + namuna paragrafdan 1 ta yaxshi gap. To'liq namuna paragraf tahlildan keyin guruh chatiga yuboriladi.

7. Tekshirish (24 soat ichida): A — har bo'shliq 1 ball; ikki so'zdan uzun javob 0; 1-savol: 3 / 3rd / third qabul qilinadi; 3-savol: FAQAT raqam bilan (150,000 / 150 000 / 150000) — so'z bilan yozilsa ikki so'z chegarasidan oshadi, 0; ma'noni buzmaydigan imlo xatosi kechiriladi (volleybol → 1), boshqa so'zga aylansa 0 (metal ≠ medal). B — har band 1 ball; TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN (T / F / NG ham qabul); YES / NO — 0. C — har band 1 ball, bitta harf tanlanadi. D — har band 1 ball; 5–8 da bitta harf imlo xatosi — 0.5. E — W-B1 rubrikasi, 4 mezon × 0–3 = 12; 54 so'z va undan kam bo'lsa Task Response ko'pi bilan 1 ball (rubrikadagi '2/3 qismidan kam' bilan bir xil chegara). Bitta xatboshi — talab, CC bo'yicha jarima emas (CC qatori bitta xatboshiga moslangan).

8. Ball jadvali: A Listening 5; B Reading 5; C Grammar 10; D Vocabulary 8; E Writing 12; JAMI 40 (70% = 28, 85% = 34, 50% = 20). Natijani tizim/jurnalga bo'limlar kesimida (A, B, C, D, E va jami) kiriting.
answers: 20–27 ball (50–69%) — QAYTA ISHLASH: xato qilingan bo'limlar bo'yicha individual uy vazifasi (C da 6 dan kam — 11–14-darslar formulalari bilan har mavzuga 3 tadan o'z gapi; D da 5 dan kam — 4 dars CORE so'zlaridan 16 ta flashcard + har biriga gap; B da 3 dan kam — 11–14-darslar reading matnidan T/F/NG mashqi; E da 6 dan kam — ustoz izohlari bo'yicha 2 xatoni tuzatib qayta yozish) + 5 savollik og'zaki qayta tekshiruv (pastdagi varaq): 16-darsning Sinf mashqlari bosqichida, boshqalar mustaqil ishlayotganda, yakka tartibda (har biriga ~1 daq; vaqt yetmasa — darsdan keyin 5 daqiqada); natija (x/5) jurnalga yoziladi. Tahlil bosqichining 8 daqiqasiga kirmaydi.

0–19 ball (< 50%) — O'TMADI: ota-onaga xabar beriladi; 7 kun ichida qayta topshirish (22 daq): C Grammar va D Vocabulary — PARALLEL variant (xuddi shu mavzular va taqsimot, yangi gaplar va so'zlar, boshqa tartibda; 'Qayta topshirish' bo'limlari) + E Writing zaxira mavzuda; A va B ballari birinchi urinishdan olinadi. Yangi jami yuqoridagi shkala bo'yicha baholanadi.
Writing qoidasi: E bo'limdan 0–3 ball olgan o'quvchi umumiy natijadan qat'i nazar writing'ni zaxira mavzuda qayta yozadi (7 kun ichida, 12 daq); yangi ball jurnalga yoziladi.

items: Good afternoon, and welcome to the Green Valley Sports Club open day. I'm Dilnoza, the head coach.
Let me tell you about our summer programme for young athletes. Our old posters say that it starts on the first of June, but that has changed: we now start on the third of June.
Every group trains three times a week. Both the football and the basketball groups are already full, so the only places left are in volleyball.
Last year the programme cost 120,000 sums a month. This year it costs 150,000 sums, and that includes a club T-shirt.
At the end of the summer, all teams will play in a small tournament. The trophy goes to the winning team only, but every player will get a medal.
We also care about personal development. Talks about healthy food will start in autumn, but this summer, every Saturday, one of our coaches will give a short talk on time management.
To register, please come to the reception. See you on the court!

class_ex.title: B. Reading: matn — A Coach Made of Data
class_ex.instr: Read the text. Then answer questions 1–5 in the next part. (Matnni o'qing va keyingi qismdagi 1–5-savollarga javob bering.)
items: A Coach Made of Data
The number of football clubs using artificial intelligence is growing every year. A number of top teams now have their own data experts, and each of these experts works closely with the coach.

Trained on thousands of old matches, an AI system can find patterns that people often miss. Watching every player for ninety minutes, it measures speed, distance and even tiredness. Neither the players nor the coach has to write anything down: the data collected by the cameras is ready as soon as the game ends.

One of the biggest advantages is fewer injuries. Warned by the system, a coach can rest a tired player before he gets hurt. Several clubs say that the number of injuries in their team has fallen since they started using AI.

However, not everyone is happy. Both fans and some former athletes worry that football is becoming too scientific. "Every decision is based on numbers now," says one retired captain. "Playing with your heart is important too."
Smaller clubs face another problem: none of them can pay for the most expensive software, so the gap between rich and poor teams may grow.
Still, most experts agree that AI will not replace coaches. Used carefully, it is simply another tool, and the final decision is always made by a person.
class_ex.answers: Matn — savollar va kalit keyingi bo'limda (B. Reading: savollar). Matn original (Jony Academy), 216 so'z; klublar va iqtibos egasi to'qima.

2. After each match, the players have to write down how far they ran.
3. The first AI system for football was made in England.
4. Some clubs have had fewer injuries since they began using AI.
5. Smaller clubs are planning to share one AI system.

2-xatboshi: "Neither the players nor the coach has to write anything down" — ma'lumotni kameralar yig'adi.
Matnda AI tizimi qaysi davlatda yoki kim tomonidan yaratilgani aytilmagan.
3-xatboshi: "Several clubs say that the number of injuries in their team has fallen since they started using AI."
5-xatboshi: kichik klublar qimmat dasturni ololmaydi — lekin birgalikda bitta tizim olish rejasi haqida hech narsa yo'q.

class_ex.title: C. Grammar — 10 ball (10 × 1), 6 daqiqa
class_ex.instr: Choose the correct answer: A, B, C or D. (To'g'ri javobni tanlang — faqat bitta harfni aylantiring.)
items: 1. You can take bus 10 or bus 25 to the stadium — ____ bus stops right next to the main entrance. A) either B) every C) all D) both
2. It was 0–0 at half-time because ____ of the two teams scored in the first 45 minutes. A) none B) both C) every D) neither
3. ____ student in our class can join the volunteer club — you don't need any experience. A) All B) Any C) Both D) None
4. I sent emails to five charities last week, but ____ of them replied. A) none B) neither C) either D) both
5. The number of teenagers who read books about self-improvement ____ growing. A) are B) have C) is D) were
6. Neither my brother nor my parents ____ good at time management. A) is B) has C) was D) are
7. One of my worst habits ____ checking my phone during homework. A) are B) is C) were D) have been
8. ____ on millions of photos, the new app can recognise a face in two seconds. A) Training B) Trains C) Trained D) Is trained
9. ____ the chatbot a simple question, I got a very strange answer. A) Asking B) Asked C) Ask D) Asks
10. The app ____ my English homework every evening was made by two students from our school. A) checked B) checking C) checks D) is checking
why: L11: ikkita narsadan istalgani — either + birlik ot + birlik fe'l. every/all — 3+ uchun; both + ko'plik ot.
L11: ikkitadan hech biri — neither of + ko'plik ot (0–0 — hech kim gol urmagan). none — 3+ uchun.
L12: istalgan biri — any + birlik ot. All/Both + ko'plik ot kerak; None of… bo'lardi.
L12: 3+ (beshta xayriya tashkiloti) — none of them. neither/either — faqat 2 ta uchun; both — ma'noga zid (javob kelmagan).
L13: the number of + ko'plik ot + BIRLIK fe'l (son bitta).
L13: neither … nor — fe'l yaqin (oxirgi) egaga mos: my parents → are.
L13: one of the / one of my + ko'plik ot + BIRLIK fe'l.
L14: -ed clause — ilova o'rgatilgan (passiv): Trained on…, the app…
L14: -ing clause — ega (I) o'zi so'radi (aktiv): Asking…, I got…
L14: otdan keyin -ing — the app (which is) checking my homework (aktiv: ilova o'zi tekshiradi). checked — passiv ma'no beradi, checks / is checking — ikkinchi kesim bo'lib qoladi.
class_ex.note: Taqsimot: 1–2 — L11 (each / every / either / neither), 3–4 — L12 (any / both / all / none), 5–7 — L13 (ega–kesim mosligi), 8–10 — L14 (-ing / -ed clauses).

2. the situation when people want to work but cannot find a job

6. ________ between rich and poor families is growing in many countries.
7. She failed the exam twice, but she didn't give up. Her ________ helped her to pass it on the third try.

class_ex.title: E. Writing — 12 ball (W-B1: 4 mezon × 0–3), 12 daqiqa
class_ex.instr: Write ONE paragraph of 80–100 words. (80–100 so'zli bitta xatboshi yozing.)
items: 1. Question: Some people think that AI tools, such as chatbots, will make students lazy. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
2. Give your opinion in the first sentence. (Birinchi gapda fikringizni ayting.)
3. Give two reasons and one example from your life. (Ikki sabab va hayotingizdan bitta misol keltiring.)
4. Use at least 3 words from Lessons 11–14 (for example: chatbot, prompt, motivation, responsibility, habit, focus). (11–14-darslardan kamida 3 ta so'z.)
5. Use at least 2 structures from Lessons 11–14: each / every / both / none, the number of / one of the, an -ing or -ed clause. (Kamida 2 ta dars grammatikasi.)
6. Finish with a conclusion and write the number of words. (Xulosa bilan tugating va so'z sonini yozing.)
answers: Baholash — W-B1 rubrikasi (keyingi bo'lim), 4 mezon × 0–3 = 12 ball. 54 so'z va undan kam — Task Response ko'pi bilan 1 ball; savolga javob bermagan / yodlangan matn — Task Response 0.

Tekshiruv ro'yxati: aniq pozitsiya (agree / disagree / partly agree), 2 sabab + 1 misol, 3+ bog'lovchi (On the one hand, However, For example, Therefore), 11–14-darslar grammatikasi 2+ marta to'g'ri, 3+ CORE so'z.

ZAXIRA mavzu (qayta topshirish va 0–3 ball olganlar uchun, o'quvchiga oldindan ko'rsatilmaydi): Some people think that every school should give students one hour of sport every day. Do you agree or disagree? — xuddi shu talablar, 80–100 so'z, 12 daq; tavsiya etilgan so'zlar (L11, L13): athlete, coach, habit, routine, willpower, confidence.

class_ex.title: E. Writing: namuna paragraf (faqat ustozga)
class_ex.instr: Namuna — 12 ball darajasi uchun mo'ljal. Test paytida ko'rsatilmaydi. 16-darsdagi tahlilda undan faqat 1 ta yaxshi gap ko'rsatiladi (L16 timeline: '1 ta yaxshi namuna gap'); to'liq paragraf tahlildan keyin guruh chatiga yuboriladi. Hajmi: 97 so'z.
items: I partly agree with this statement. On the one hand, a number of students already use chatbots to do their homework, and copying the answers, they learn nothing. When this becomes a habit, their own skills become weaker. On the other hand, used carefully, artificial intelligence can make learning faster. For example, when I write an essay, I give a chatbot a short prompt to find my mistakes, and then I correct each mistake myself. In my opinion, the problem is not the technology but the student's motivation and responsibility. Therefore, AI makes only some students lazy.
answers: TR 3: pozitsiya aniq (I partly agree), ikki tomon, misol (essay + chatbot), xulosa.
CC 3: On the one hand / On the other hand / For example / In my opinion / Therefore — mantiqiy tartib.
LR 3: 6 ta CORE so'z o'z o'rnida — chatbot, prompt, artificial intelligence (L14); habit, motivation, responsibility (L13).
GRA 3: a number of students + ko'plik fe'l (L13); copying the answers, they… / used carefully, artificial intelligence… (L14); each mistake (L11); oddiy va murakkab gaplar aralash.

class_ex.instr: Choose the correct answer: A, B, C or D. (To'g'ri javobni tanlang — faqat bitta harfni aylantiring.)
items: 1. A number of students in our group ____ trying to improve their time management this term. A) is B) has C) are D) was

why: L13: a number of + ko'plik ot + KO'PLIK fe'l (ko'p odam).
L11: ikkitadan hech biri — neither of + ko'plik ot + birlik fe'l (shuning uchun ovqatni o'zimiz olib kelamiz).
L14: -ing clause — ega (she) o'zi qaragan (aktiv).
L12: 3+ (o'nta ko'ngilli), hammasi rozi bo'ldi — all of them. none — ma'noga zid; both / either — faqat 2 ta uchun.
L14: -ed clause — robot yaratilgan (passiv): Designed by…, the robot…
L13: gerund (V-ing) ega + BIRLIK fe'l.
L11: har birini alohida, birma-bir — each + birlik ot. all / both + ko'plik ot; either — 2 ta uchun.
L14: otdan keyin -ed — the photos (which were) collected by the app (passiv).
L13: either … or — fe'l yaqin (oxirgi) egaga mos: the teacher → is.
L12: ikkita (my two sisters) — both + ko'plik fe'l. all — 3+ uchun.
class_ex.note: Taqsimot (aralash tartib): L13 — 1, 6, 9; L11 — 2, 7; L14 — 3, 5, 8; L12 — 4, 10.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Travelling abroad: benefits and challenges
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ relative clause (who / which / that).
items: Part 1: Have you ever been abroad? Where did you go?
Part 1: Which country would you most like to visit?
Part 3: What can people learn when they visit a country which has a different culture?
Part 3: What are the main challenges for people who travel abroad for the first time?
Part 3: Is travelling abroad too expensive for most young people in Uzbekistan?
Part 3: Do people who travel a lot become more open-minded?
Part 3: Should young people travel abroad before they start university or work?
answers: Yes, once. Two years ago I went to Turkey with my family. We stayed in a small hotel which was near the sea in Antalya.
I'd most like to visit Japan, because it is a country which mixes old traditions and modern technology. I also want to try the food that people eat there.

I think they learn that there are many ways to live. For example, a tourist who visits Japan sees that people are very quiet on trains, which is different from our noisy buses in Tashkent. They also learn small things, like greetings, that help them respect other people.

The biggest challenge is the language barrier. A traveller who doesn't speak English or the local language can't even ask for directions. Another problem is money: people who don't understand currency exchange often pay too much. On the other hand, most problems become easier after the first few days.

Well, I'd say it is expensive, but not impossible. Plane tickets and visas cost a lot for a student who doesn't work. However, there are cheap flights to countries which don't need a visa, like Georgia or Turkey. For example, my cousin saved for six months and travelled to Tbilisi.

Yes, I think so. People who travel a lot meet others who have different opinions and habits, so they stop judging quickly. For example, my uncle, who works in Dubai, used to be very strict, but now he accepts new ideas easily. Travel really broadens your mind.

I believe it's a good idea if they can afford it. A short trip which they plan themselves teaches them independence. For example, a student who organises a week in Istanbul learns to book hotels and manage a budget. On the other hand, a long gap year can delay their studies, so a summer trip is better.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Travelling abroad: benefits and challenges
class_ex.instr: Every year more and more people travel to other countries for their holidays. What are the benefits and challenges of travelling abroad? Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval; uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: advantages/disadvantages (benefits = afzalliklar, challenges = qiyinchiliklar); ikkala tomon ham yoritiladi
2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: more and more people / travel to other countries / for their holidays / benefits / challenges

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: afzalliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + fikr, agar savol so'rasa)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of … is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, … also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: relative clause (who / which / that) 2+ marta
answers: Namuna kirish (37 so'z): Nowadays, more and more people from Uzbekistan spend their holidays in other countries, such as Turkey or Georgia. Travelling abroad can be exciting and useful, but it also has some difficulties. This essay will discuss both sides.

Namuna AD jadval: Afzalliklar — 1) broadens your mind: new culture (the old mosques of Istanbul); 2) local food and memories (khachapuri in Georgia); Kamchiliklar — 1) expensive: flights, hotels, visa fees; 2) language barrier, culture shock, currency exchange and card fees

Namuna insho (188 so'z) — kirish: Nowadays, more and more people from Uzbekistan spend their holidays in other countries, such as Turkey or Georgia. Travelling abroad can be exciting and useful, but it also has some difficulties. This essay will discuss both sides.

Namuna insho — body 1: One major advantage of travelling abroad is that it broadens your mind. Tourists who visit a new country see a different culture, for example the old mosques of Istanbul. Another benefit is local food. Trying dishes which you cannot find at home, like Georgian khachapuri, is a great experience.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, travelling abroad also has some drawbacks. Firstly, it can be expensive, because flights, hotels and visa fees cost a lot for a family. Secondly, many tourists face a language barrier and culture shock. For example, a traveller who does not speak English may find it hard to order food. Currency exchange is confusing too, and a card transaction abroad often has an extra fee.

Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, travelling abroad helps people learn about the world, but it needs money and careful planning. In my opinion, the benefits are greater than the challenges, especially for young people who prepare well.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — Tourists who visit…, dishes which you cannot find…, a traveller who does not speak…, young people who prepare well (4 ta); bog'lovchilar — One major advantage, Another benefit, On the other hand, Firstly, Secondly, For example, because, In conclusion; mavzu so'zlari — culture, local food, visa, language barrier, culture shock, currency exchange, broadens your mind, transaction (CORE)
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 15-qator ("The benefits and challenges of traveling abroad."); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). PEER-AD (juftlik, Ha/Yo'q): 1) savol o'z so'zlari bilan? 2) afzallik va kamchilik alohida xatboshida? 3) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol? 4) 4+ bog'lovchi? 5) dars grammatikasi 2+? 6) 150+ so'z? Namuna insho o'quvchiga uy inshosi tekshirilgandan keyin ko'rsatiladi. L17 (Studying abroad) bilan farq: bu yerda faqat sayohat va dam olish g'oyalari.

reading.title: Satoshi Nakamoto — the person who invented Bitcoin and disappeared
text: On 31 October 2008, someone who called himself Satoshi Nakamoto sent a nine-page document to an online mailing list for cryptography experts. It was a whitepaper which described a new kind of money: a currency that no bank, no government and no company would control. In January 2009 the first Bitcoin block, which is now called the "genesis block", was created. Inside it Satoshi included a newspaper headline about a government plan to rescue banks — a message which many people read as a warning about the banking system.

For about two years Satoshi worked by email with the programmers who joined the project. He wrote many messages, but he never gave an interview, never showed his face, and nobody knows where he lived. Then, in April 2011, he wrote in his last known email that he had moved on to other things. After that, he disappeared.

Who is he? Nobody knows. Some think he is a British cryptographer whose writing style is similar to Satoshi's; others think Satoshi is a group. A man who was named by a magazine in 2014 denied everything. The wallets which are believed to belong to Satoshi hold about one million bitcoins — worth many billions of dollars — and, as far as anyone knows, not one coin has ever been moved.

Today Bitcoin is a currency that millions of people own, and many banks study the blockchain technology which Satoshi designed. Some people think it could one day replace ordinary money; others think it is too risky. The idea behind it was simple: a system that works without trust in any single person — including its creator.
