kahoot.q: The girl ___ called you is my cousin.
kahoot.explain: Odam + ega vazifasida → who (who + fe'l: who called). whom — faqat to'ldiruvchi.

kahoot.q: The app ___ I use every day is free.
kahoot.explain: Narsa (app) → which/that. who — faqat odam uchun.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: The phone which she bought it is new.
The boy you met is my friend.
The car which broke down was expensive.
Satoshi, who invented Bitcoin, is unknown.
kahoot.explain: which o'zi to'ldiruvchi o'rnida — "it" ortiqcha: The phone which she bought is new.

kahoot.q: Bitcoin, ___ was created in 2009, has no bank.
kahoot.explain: Vergulli (qo'shimcha ma'lumot) gapda that ishlatilmaydi; narsa → which.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda which/who ni TUSHIRIB qoldirsa bo'ladi?
options: The phone which she bought is new.
The car which broke down was expensive.
The girl who called you is my cousin.
The man who sold me the coin left.
kahoot.explain: Faqat to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa tushadi: which + ega (she) + fe'l. which/who + fe'l bo'lsa — tushmaydi.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: The man who sold me the coin was a scammer.
The man which sold me the coin was a scammer.
The man who he sold me the coin was a scammer.
The man whom sold me the coin was a scammer.
kahoot.explain: Odam + ega → who + fe'l. which — narsa; "he" ortiqcha; whom ega bo'lmaydi.

kahoot.q: The exchange ___ I trade on is safe.
kahoot.explain: Birja — narsa → which; predlog oxirida: the exchange (which) I trade on.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Men uchrashgan investor boy."
options: The investor I met is rich.
The investor who I met him is rich.
The investor which I met is rich.
The investor met me is rich.
kahoot.explain: to'ldiruvchi who tushirilgan: the investor (who) I met. "him" ortiqcha, which — narsa uchun.

kahoot.q: Vergulli (non-defining) gapda qaysi so'z ISHLATILMAYDI?
kahoot.explain: Non-defining gapda that bo'lmaydi: Bitcoin, which... / Satoshi, who...

kahoot.q: Satoshi Nakamoto, ___ invented Bitcoin, never showed his face.
kahoot.explain: Odam + ega + vergul → who. that vergul bilan ishlatilmaydi.

kahoot.q: A wallet ___ has no private key is useless.
kahoot.explain: Hamyon — narsa, ega vazifasida → which + fe'l (which has).

kahoot.q: People ___ invest in crypto must accept high risk.
kahoot.explain: People — odamlar → who + fe'l (who invest).

kahoot.q: The price of Bitcoin goes up and down very fast. This is called ___.
kahoot.explain: volatility — o'zgaruvchanlik: narx tez ko'tarilib-tushadi.

kahoot.q: A ___ is a fake project that steals investors' money.
kahoot.explain: scam — firibgarlik, aldov loyiha.

kahoot.q: Money issued by a government, like the dollar or the som, is ___ money.
kahoot.explain: fiat money — davlat chiqaradigan pul (dollar, so'm).

kahoot.q: "decentralized" so'zining antonimi qaysi?
kahoot.explain: decentralized (markazsiz) ↔ centralized (markazlashgan, masalan bank).

kahoot.q: You buy and sell crypto on an ___.
kahoot.explain: exchange — kripto birja, u yerda coin sotib olinadi va sotiladi.

kahoot.q: A ___ is a crypto coin whose value is tied to the US dollar.
kahoot.explain: stablecoin — qiymati dollarga bog'langan barqaror coin (masalan USDT).

kahoot.q: Never share your ___ key — it opens your wallet.
kahoot.explain: private key — maxfiy kalit, hamyonni ochadi. public key — ochiq manzil.

kahoot.q: "bull market" nimani bildiradi?
kahoot.explain: bull market — narxlar o'sayotgan bozor; bear market — tushayotgan bozor.

You will hear a bank security specialist giving a talk to teenagers about keeping digital money safe.

transcript: MS YUSUPOVA: Good morning, everyone. I'm Dilnoza Yusupova, and I work in a bank's security team. Today I'll talk about keeping your digital money safe.

MS YUSUPOVA: Let's start with passwords. A good password is a password which nobody else knows. Many people use their birthday, which is a big mistake. Your password should have at least ten — sorry, I mean twelve — characters. [Q1]

MS YUSUPOVA: Next, the code which the bank sends to your phone. Never share this code [Q2] with anyone. A person who calls you and asks for the code is not from the bank. It's a scam, so just end the call.
MS YUSUPOVA: Now, apps. Only use an app that comes from the official store [Q3] — not an app that someone sends you in a message.
MS YUSUPOVA: Check your account regularly. I used to tell students to do it every month, but now I say every week. [Q4] Then you can quickly see any transaction which you don't recognise.
MS YUSUPOVA: If you have a digital wallet for crypto, remember that the risk is high. Keep your private key [Q5] on paper at home. People who keep it in a photo on their phone can lose everything.
MS YUSUPOVA: And finally, if you lose money, call your bank within 24 hours. [Q6] Any questions?

lessons.title: Relative Clauses: Which vs Where
lessons.grammar_topic: ANIQLOVCHI ERGASH GAPLAR — WHICH vs WHERE (joy haqida: where / in which)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 16 (jadval 4 qator; E-COMMERCE 60 so'z); Reading — Jack Ma (Jony Academy matni, moslashtirilgan); AUDIO 126–130, Topic 101–103 — ixtiyoriy.
objectives: where va which ni farqlash: 8 bo'shliqdan 7 tasi to'g'ri.
in/at/on which va predlog oxiridagi which ni to'g'ri ishlatish.
Test: gapni joy oti bilan qaytaring. Predlog yo'q (I like the shop) → which/that yoki tushiriladi; predlog bor (I work IN the shop) → where / in which; darhol fe'l kelsa (the shop … sells) → which.
Listening (IELTS Part 1): RETURNS FORM — 6 bo'shliqdan 5 tasi to'g'ri.
Speaking Part 1–2–3 va Writing 7 (Task 2): reja + kirish.
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 16 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.

Writing/Speaking rubrikasi — L01 dagi W-B1 va S-B1 jadvallari; juftlik varag'i peer-b1.
timeline: Warm-up: which yoki where?
"I bought my phone in the shop" → the shop where I bought my phone; "The shop sells phones" → the shop which sells phones. Nega ikkinchisida where emas?
TAKROR: Kahoot — L15 (Relative clauses: who / which)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi — L15 savollari (shu darsniki emas). Faqat 1–12-savollar × 15 s (qolgani uyga havola); izohni faqat yarmidan ko'pi xato qilgan savollarga bering.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — L15 Cryptocurrency CORE 20
Ustoz 20 so'zni o'zbekcha aytadi, o'quvchi inglizcha yozadi (4 daq); 1 daq juftlikda tekshirish, kalit — L15 Lug'at tabi. 17/20+ — bajarildi (2 coin).
PROGRESS TEST 3 tahlili

(1) Har bo'limdan eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 band doskada — o'quvchilar o'z varag'ida tuzatadi (4 daq); (2) Writing: 2 umumiy xato + 1 yaxshi namuna gap (2 daq); (3) 50–69% — individual vazifa, <50% — qayta topshirish sanasi e'lon qilinadi (2 daq). L15 WRITING — Travelling abroad: benefits and challenges insholari yig'iladi (ustoz W-B1-AD bilan darsdan keyin baholaydi; jadval — L15 dars sahifasida); SPEAKING ovozli javoblari — ilova natijasi.
YANGI MAVZU: Which vs where (in which)

10 daq: jadval 4 qator (grammar.formulas) + presentation 1–5. Test: gapni joy oti bilan qaytaring. Predlog yo'q (I like the shop) → which/that yoki tushiriladi; predlog bor (I work IN the shop) → where / in which; darhol fe'l kelsa (the shop … sells) → which. CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq: 'which yoki where' (1-mashq, yakka).
Lug'at: E-commerce — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

10 so'z: e-commerce, online store, marketplace, customer, product, cart, checkout, order, delivery, refund — so'z → ma'no → where/which bilan 1 gap; 'E-tijorat lug'ati' (match, juftlikda, 2 daq). Qolgan CORE, STRONG — uyda flashcard; SUPER — ixtiyoriy.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 4 qator)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. Me'yor — normativ[2].
Sinf mashqlari: in which bilan (5 daq) + Ikki gapni birlashtiring (8 daq)

1-si yakka, 2-si juftlikda; 3 daq javoblar. ZAXIRA: Xatoni toping. Vaqt yetmasa: avval 'Xatoni toping', keyin 'Ikki gapni birlashtiring' 4–5-bandlari (uyga). Shu vaqtda ustoz pt3 da 20–27 ball olganlar bilan birma-bir 5 savollik og'zaki qayta tekshiruv o'tkazadi (~1 daq); natija jurnalga.
Listening (IELTS Part 1): form completion

2 daq tayyorgarlik; 1-tinglash; 1 daq solishtirish; 2-tinglash; 3 daq javoblar (dalil — skriptdan); 2 daq target gaplarni tiklash (the address where I live now / a jacket which arrived yesterday). Ikki xil ovozda o'qing.
Reading: T/F/NG + sentence completion
3 daq gist: 'Why is Jack Ma's story useful for students?' (rad etilgan, lekin taslim bo'lmagan); 5 daq T/F/NG; 4 daq sentence completion. ZAXIRA topshiriq — uyga yoki kuchlilarga.
Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Shopping online
Part 1 juftlikda 3 daq; Part 2: 1 daq tayyorgarlik, A 1.5 daq, B 1.5 daq (sherik peer-b1 checklist); Part 3 — 2 daq; ustoz 1 daq feedback (S-B1: 1 kuchli tomon + 1 tuzatish).
Writing (IELTS Task 2): problem–solution — Writing 7 reja + kirish
2 daq savol tahlili (tur: problem–solution — muammolar + yechimlar; kalit so'zlar); 2 daq reja; 6 daq kirish (40–50 so'z, 1+ where/which); 2 daq juftlikda peer-b1 bilan tekshirish. Uyda to'liq insho.
Exit ticket

Qog'ozda, chiqishda topshiradi: 1) The shop ___ I work sells phones. / The shop ___ opened yesterday is big. (where / which) 2) "Pulni qaytarish" inglizcha? (refund) 3) Gapiruvchi "on the 14th — sorry, the 15th" desa, javob? (15th — tuzatilgani)
Uyga vazifa
MAJBURIY (~45 daq): flashcard, Writing 7, tarjima, og'zaki normativ. IXTIYORIY — uy vazifasi tabida.

intro: WHERE — ish o'sha joyda bo'ladi: joy + where + ega + fe'l (the café where we met). IN/AT/ON WHICH — uning rasmiy shakli.
WHICH — joy gapning egasi yoki predlogsiz to'ldiruvchisi: which + fe'l (the house which was built in 1920) / which + ega + fe'l (the shop which I like).
Test: gapni qaytaring — "I studied IN the school" → where / in which; "The school was built" → which.
formulas: The city where I was born is beautiful.
This is the café where we met.
This is the house which was built in 1920.
This is the school in which I studied.
This is the school (which) I studied at.
The year when Alibaba started / the flat where it started
presentation: Is Uzum the marketplace where you buy clothes?
Yes, Uzum is the marketplace where I buy clothes.
Which store sells the cheapest phones?
The store which sells the cheapest phones is online.
Which app do you use?
I use the app which my sister recommended.
In which category do you shop most?
Electronics is the category in which I shop most.
Where do you collect your orders?
At a pick-up point where they keep parcels for three days.
notes: where + to'liq gap (ega + fe'l), predlogsiz: "the shop where I work" (work in — emas).
which ega bo'lsa — fe'l: "the shop which opened yesterday"; to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa that ham bo'ladi yoki tushiriladi: "the app (which/that) my friend recommended".
"where" = "in/at/on which"; "when" = "on/in which" (vaqt); "why" = "for which".
CCQ: This is the shop where I work. — Do I work in the shop? (Yes)
CCQ: This is the shop which sells phones. — Does the shop sell? (Yes) Is there a preposition? (No)
CCQ: The shop which I like is closed. — Do I like the shop? (Yes) Do I say 'like in'? (No → which / that / tushiriladi)

The city where I was born is beautiful. / …which I was born in…

This is the house which was built in 1920.

The café where we met… / The café (which) we met at…
The shop in where I work…
The shop where I work… / The shop in which I work…

class_ex.title: Writing (IELTS Task 2): problem–solution — Writing 7
class_ex.instr: In many towns, small local shops and markets are closing because more and more people buy things online. What problems does this cause, and what can be done to help local shops? Write 180–200 words. — Sinfda: reja + kirish paragrafi (40–50 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 180–200 so'z, kamida 3 ta where/which.
items: 1) Tur: problem–solution — 2 qism: problems (muammolar) + solutions (yechimlar); ikkalasiga ham javob kerak.
2) Kalit so'zlar: local shops, closing, problems, what can be done.
3) Reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1 — muammolar: ish o'rinlari, mahalla hayoti, keksalar uchun qiyinchilik → Body 2 — yechimlar → Xulosa.
4) Boshlanmalar: 'Nowadays, …', 'One serious problem is that…', 'Another problem is…', 'One possible solution is to…', 'In conclusion, …'
answers: Namuna kirish (48 so'z): Nowadays, many small shops and markets in our towns, where people used to buy everyday goods, are closing because customers prefer online marketplaces. This change causes problems for local workers and neighbourhoods. This essay will describe these problems and suggest some ways which can help local shops survive.

Namuna reja: Body 1 — muammolar: 1) sotuvchilar ishsiz qoladi (the shop where a family worked for years closes); 2) mahalla hayoti susayadi — qo'shnilar uchrashadigan joy yo'qoladi; 3) ilova ishlata olmaydigan keksalar uchun qiyin — yaqin do'kon yo'q. Body 2 — yechimlar: 1) kichik do'konlar ham onlayn sotsin (Telegram kanal, marketpleysdagi sahifa, uyga yetkazib berish); 2) hokimiyat ijara va soliqni kamaytirsin, bozorlarda 'local market' kunlari; 3) odamlar har hafta kamida bir marta mahalla do'konidan xarid qilsin. Xulosa — muammolar jiddiy, lekin do'konlar va jamiyat birga harakat qilsa, yechim bor.
Namunada where/which: 'towns, where people used to buy…', 'ways which can help…'; uy inshosida yana 1+ (masalan, 'the shop where neighbours meet').
class_ex.note: Tekshirish: W-B1 rubrika (L01), sinfda juftlik peer-b1 varag'i bilan; ustoz 2 ta ishni doskada ko'rsatadi. Manba: savol L13 'Online shopping' bilan takrorlanmasligi uchun almashtirildi; savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original.

reading.title: Jack Ma — the English teacher who built an online giant
text: Jack Ma was born in 1964 in Hangzhou, a city where tourists come to see the West Lake. As a boy he waited near the hotel where foreigners stayed and offered them free tours in exchange for English practice. He failed the university entrance exam twice. Later he applied for 30 jobs, including one at KFC, where 24 people applied and 23 were accepted — he was the only one rejected. So he became an English teacher, earning about 12 dollars a month.

In 1995 he visited the USA, where he saw the internet for the first time. He typed "beer" and found results from many countries, but none from China. Back home, in 1999, he gathered 17 friends in his small flat — the flat which became the company's first office — and founded Alibaba, a marketplace where small Chinese factories could sell to the world.

Alibaba grew into a company which serves millions of sellers and buyers. Taobao, the site where ordinary people sell to each other, has hundreds of millions of users. On Singles' Day (11 November), the shopping festival which Alibaba made famous, shoppers spend billions of dollars in one day.

Ma stepped down as Alibaba's chairman in 2019 and said he wanted to return to education. The lesson which he repeats most is that today is hard and tomorrow is harder, but the day after tomorrow is beautiful — and most people give up tomorrow night.

kahoot.q: The city ___ I was born is beautiful.
kahoot.explain: I was born IN the city → predlog bor → where (= in which).

kahoot.q: This is the house ___ was built in 1920.
kahoot.explain: The house was built → uy ega, predlog yo'q → which + fe'l.

kahoot.q: This is the school ___ I studied.
kahoot.explain: I studied IN the school → in which (= where). "in where" — xato.

kahoot.q: The shop ___ I like is closed.
kahoot.explain: I like the shop — predlogsiz to'ldiruvchi → which.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: The city which I was born is beautiful.
This is the café where we met.
This is the school I studied at.
The warehouse where they keep goods is big.
kahoot.explain: born IN the city → where yoki which ... born in. Predlogsiz "which I was born" xato.

kahoot.q: The warehouse ___ we store our products is in Chirchiq.
kahoot.explain: We store products IN the warehouse → where + ega + fe'l.

kahoot.q: The website ___ I bought my shoes on was fake.
kahoot.explain: Predlog (on) oxirida → which. where bilan predlog qo'shilmaydi.

kahoot.q: That was the year ___ our online store started.
kahoot.explain: Vaqt (the year) → when. where — faqat joy uchun.

kahoot.q: "where" qachon ishlatiladi?
options: Joy haqida, ish o'sha joyda bo'lsa (where + ega + fe'l)
kahoot.explain: where + ega + fe'l: the café where we met. Joy ega bo'lsa → which + fe'l.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: The shop in which I work sells phones.
The shop in where I work sells phones.
The shop where I work in sells phones.
The shop which I work sells phones.
kahoot.explain: in which = where. "in where" xato; where + in ortiqcha; which ... work in kerak.

kahoot.q: The online store ___ sells cheap phones is popular.
kahoot.explain: Do'kon o'zi sotadi (ega) → which + fe'l (which sells).

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Bu — biz uchrashgan kafe."
options: This is the café where we met.
This is the café which we met.
This is the café where we met at.
This is the café when we met.
kahoot.explain: We met AT the café → where. where bilan "at" qo'shilmaydi.

kahoot.q: You put products in your ___ before you pay.
kahoot.explain: cart — savat: tovarlarni to'lovdan oldin shu yerga qo'yasiz.

kahoot.q: If a product is not available now, it is ___.
kahoot.explain: out of stock — omborda yo'q, tugagan. in stock — bor.

kahoot.q: I returned the broken phone and got a full ___.
kahoot.explain: refund — pulni qaytarish. Tovarni qaytarib, pulingizni olasiz.

kahoot.q: You pay when the parcel arrives at your door. This is ___.
kahoot.explain: cash on delivery — yetkazib berilganda naqd to'lash.

kahoot.q: A code that gives you a discount is a ___.
kahoot.explain: promo code / coupon — chegirma beradigan kod.

kahoot.q: With ___, you can see where your parcel is now.
kahoot.explain: tracking — posilkani kuzatish (hozir qayerdaligini ko'rish).

kahoot.q: A big building where an online store keeps its goods is a ___.
kahoot.explain: warehouse — ombor: tovarlar saqlanadigan katta bino.

kahoot.q: "supplier" so'zining ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: supplier / vendor — do'konga tovar yetkazib beruvchi kompaniya.

lessons.title: Relative Clauses: Whose, Why, When
lessons.grammar_topic: ANIQLOVCHI ERGASH GAPLAR — WHOSE (egalik) / WHY (sabab) / WHEN (vaqt)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 17 – Clauses (when, whose, why) (3 qatorli jadval); RENEWABLE ENERGY (52 so'z); Reading — Nikola Tesla (Jony Academy matni, moslashtirilgan); AUDIO 131–135 va Topic 111–113 — ixtiyoriy, uyda; SPEAKING/WRITING mavzusi — rahbar rejasi (IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 17-qator): "Studying abroad: benefits and challenges."
objectives: whose bilan egalik (odam va narsa uchun): 8 bo'shliqdan 7+ to'g'ri.
the reason why / the day when bilan ikki gapni birlashtirish; why/when ni tushirish yoki that bilan almashtirish.
7 relative so'zni (who, which, that, where, whose, why, when) farqlash: 6 gapdan 5+ to'g'ri.
Listening (IELTS Part 4): quyosh energiyasi tarixi haqidagi ma'ruzadan note completion.

SPEAKING (IELTS Part 3): Studying abroad: benefits and challenges — 4–5 savolga 3–4 gapli javob (javob → sabab → misol), whose / why / when bilan; WRITING: Studying abroad: benefits and challenges — AD jadval va kirish sinfda, 150–200 so'zli insho uyda (W-B1-AD).
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 17 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.
CORE 20 varag'i — dars sahifasining Lug'at tabidan (PDF).

Ustoz 2 gapni bittaga aylantiradi: "Tesla is a scientist. His inventions light our homes." → "…whose inventions…"; "1888 was the year. He sold his patents then." → "…the year when…".

YANGI MAVZU: whose / why / when

Lug'at: Renewable energy — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

To'liq insho — uyda (Writing 8).
Exit ticket
1) Iceland is a country ___ electricity is almost all renewable. (whose) 2) "Qazilma yoqilg'i" inglizchasi? (fossil fuel) 3) Listening: Why did solar panels become cheaper? (mass production)
Uyga vazifa

intro: WHOSE — egalik ("…ning"): whose + ot (the man whose car…); narsalar uchun ham: a country whose energy…
WHY — sabab: the reason why + ega + fe'l (why tushishi mumkin).
WHEN — vaqt: the day/year/time when + ega + fe'l (when tushishi yoki that bo'lishi mumkin).
Xarita: odam → who; narsa → which/that; joy → where; egalik → whose; sabab → why; vaqt → when.
formulas: The man whose car was stolen called the police.
Mashinasi o'g'irlangan odam politsiyaga qo'ng'iroq qildi.
A country whose energy is renewable pollutes less.
Energiyasi qayta tiklanuvchi mamlakat kamroq ifloslaydi.
That is the reason why I left early.
I remember the day when we first met.
the reason (why) / the day (when) / the year (that)
1888 was the year (when) Tesla sold his patents.
Tesla, whose ideas were ahead of his time, died poor.
G'oyalari o'z davridan oldinda bo'lgan Tesla kambag'al holda vafot etdi.
presentation: Who is Nikola Tesla?
He's the inventor whose ideas helped bring AC electricity to our homes.
In which year did he arrive in America?
1884 was the year when he arrived in New York.
Why did he have little money at the end of his life?
One reason why he was poor is that he cared about ideas, not money.
Which country's electricity is almost all renewable?
Iceland, whose electricity comes almost 100% from water and geothermal heat.
When do solar panels work best?
Midday is the time when they produce the most.
notes: whose ≠ who's (who is): "the man whose car" — "the man who's here".
"the reason because" — xato; why/when ni tushirish yoki that bilan almashtirish mumkin: the reason (why) I left, the day (when) we met; whose ni tushirib bo'lmaydi.
when o'rniga in/on which (rasmiy): "the year in which he was born".
CCQ: Tesla is the scientist whose ideas changed our homes. — Whose ideas? (Tesla's)
CCQ: 1888 was the year when he sold his patents. — Is 'when' about time? (Yes) Can we say 'the year that'? (Yes)
CCQ: That's the reason why coal is still used. — Is 'why' about a reason? (Yes) Can we drop 'why'? (Yes)
CCQ: The man whose car was stolen called the police. — Whose car was stolen? (the man's) Who called? (the man)
mistakes: The man who's car was stolen…
The man whose car was stolen…
That is the reason because I left.
That is the reason why I left.
The man whose he lives here…
I remember the day when we first met on it.
I remember the day when we first met.

how: CORE — energiya turlari va asosiy tushunchalar; STRONG — texnologiya va yangi manbalar (hydrogen, tidal); SUPER — elektr tarixi (AC/DC, Tesla), sarmoya.
Har so'zga whose / why / when bilan 1 gap (namunalar — misol ustunida).
core: Renewable energy is the reason why some countries have clean air.
Qayta tiklanuvchi energiya — ba'zi mamlakatlarda havo toza bo'lishining sababi.
Coal is a non-renewable fuel whose supply will end.
The 20th century was a time when fossil fuels ruled.
XX asr — qazilma yoqilg'i hukmronlik qilgan davr.
Oil is the reason why some desert countries are rich.
Neft — ba'zi cho'l mamlakatlari boy bo'lishining sababi.
Solar energy is a source whose price has fallen fast.
Quyosh energiyasi — narxi tez tushgan manba.
A house whose roof has solar panels pays less.
Tomida quyosh paneli bo'lgan uy kamroq to'laydi.
Wind turbines work best on days when the wind is strong.
Shamol turbinalari shamol kuchli bo'lgan kunlarda eng yaxshi ishlaydi.
A wind turbine, whose blades are 80 metres long, powers 1,500 homes.
Parraklari 80 metr bo'lgan shamol turbinasi 1500 uyni ta'minlaydi.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Studying abroad: benefits and challenges
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ whose / why / when (yoki who / which / where).
items: Part 1: Would you like to study in another country? Why or why not?
Part 1: Do you know anyone who is studying abroad now?
Part 3: What is the main reason why young people want to study abroad?
Part 3: What difficulties do students whose English is weak have at a foreign university?
Part 3: Is studying abroad worth the money? Why?
Part 3: How does living far from your family change a young person?
Part 3: Should students come back to their home country when they finish their studies abroad?
answers: Yes, I would. I'd like to study in South Korea, because it is a country whose universities are strong in IT. It would also improve my English.
Yes, my cousin Dilnoza studies medicine in Turkey. I still remember the day when we said goodbye at Tashkent airport — her mum cried a lot.

I think the main reason why young people go abroad is a better education. Some foreign universities have modern labs and famous teachers. For example, my neighbour got a scholarship in Germany, and now he studies engineering there. Of course, some students also simply want to see a new country.

Well, students whose English is weak often have problems in lectures, because teachers speak fast and use difficult words. For example, a friend of mine in Malaysia needed three hours to read ten pages. On the other hand, after one year most students improve a lot because they hear English every day.

I'd say it depends. Tuition fees and rent in the UK are very high, and that's the reason why many families have to borrow money. However, if a student gets a scholarship, it is definitely worth it. For example, a degree from a good university can lead to a well-paid job back home.

In my view, it makes young people more independent. At home our parents cook and pay the bills, but abroad you do everything yourself. For example, my brother couldn't even fry an egg, but now he cooks plov for his flatmates. Still, the first months are a time when many students feel homesick.

I think most of them should, because Uzbekistan needs young specialists. If all the best students stay abroad, we get a brain drain. For example, doctors who studied in Korea can open modern clinics in Samarkand. But I understand graduates whose families live abroad too — for them, staying may be the right choice.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Studying abroad: benefits and challenges
class_ex.instr: Many young people now go to study at universities in other countries. What are the benefits and challenges of studying abroad? Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval + kirish (35–45 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi (Writing 8)
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: benefits and challenges (advantages/disadvantages) — ikkala tomon yoritiladi; savol fikr so'ramaydi, xulosada qisqa fikr bo'lishi mumkin

2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: young people / study at universities / other countries / benefits / challenges; mavzu so'zlari: scholarship, tuition fees, degree, homesick, independent, international experience, brain drain

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: afzalliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + fikr, agar savol so'rasa)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of studying abroad is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, studying abroad also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: whose / why / when (students whose families… / the reason why… / the moment when…) 2+ marta
answers: Namuna kirish (36 so'z): Every year, more young people from countries like Uzbekistan leave home to get a degree at a foreign university. This essay will discuss the main benefits of studying abroad and the challenges which these students face.

Namuna AD jadval: Afzalliklar — 1) sifatli ta'lim, hamma joyda tan olinadigan diplom (degree) — misol: zamonaviy laboratoriyalar; 2) xalqaro tajriba va mustaqillik — misol: 20 mamlakatdan kelgan kursdoshlar bilan jamoada ishlash; Kamchiliklar — 1) xarajat (tuition fees, ijara) — misol: oilalar kredit oladi; 2) uyni sog'inish (homesick) — misol: birinchi oylarda har kuni uyga qo'ng'iroq.

Namuna insho (183 so'z) — kirish: Every year, more young people from countries like Uzbekistan leave home to get a degree at a foreign university. This essay will discuss the main benefits of studying abroad and the challenges which these students face.

Namuna insho — body 1: One major advantage of studying abroad is a better education than students can often get at home. Many foreign universities have modern laboratories, and their degrees are respected by employers all over the world. Another benefit is international experience. For example, students whose classmates come from twenty different countries learn to work in mixed teams and become more independent.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, there are also some challenges. The first is cost: high tuition fees and rent are the main reason why many families have to take a loan. Secondly, many students feel homesick, especially in the first months when everything is new and nobody speaks Uzbek. For example, many first-year students call home every evening.

Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, studying abroad offers a good degree and useful experience, but it is expensive and emotionally difficult. In my view, it is worth it for students who get a scholarship.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — whose (students whose classmates…), why (the main reason why…), when (the first months when…), qo'shimcha which / who; bog'lovchilar — One major advantage…, Another benefit…, For example, On the other hand, Secondly, In conclusion, In my view; mavzu so'zlari — degree, foreign university, tuition fees, scholarship, homesick, independent, international experience.
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 17-qator ("Studying abroad: benefits and challenges."); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). PEER-AD (juftlik, Ha/Yo'q): 1) savol o'z so'zlari bilan? 2) afzallik va kamchilik alohida xatboshida? 3) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol? 4) 4+ bog'lovchi? 5) dars grammatikasi 2+? 6) 150+ so'z (sinfda kirish 35–45)? Namuna insho o'quvchiga uy inshosi tekshirilgandan keyin ko'rsatiladi.

reading.title: Nikola Tesla — the inventor whose ideas were ahead of his time
text: Nikola Tesla was born in 1856 in a small village in today's Croatia. His father was a priest, but Nikola wanted to be an engineer. He was famous for his imagination: he said that he could see a machine in his head before he built it. In 1884 he arrived in New York with very little money and a letter of recommendation to Thomas Edison, whose company used direct current (DC). Tesla believed in alternating current (AC), a system whose electricity could travel much further. The two men disagreed, and Tesla soon left Edison's company.

1888 was the year when he sold his AC patents to George Westinghouse, and 1893 was the year when AC lit the Chicago World's Fair. In 1896 electricity from Niagara Falls reached the city of Buffalo on an AC system — an important moment when the idea of a modern power grid became real.

Tesla worked on hundreds of ideas, including the AC motor, early radio, remote control and wireless electricity. In his laboratory he even made artificial lightning. But he was a scientist whose interest was ideas, not money. According to a famous story, he gave up the money from one of his contracts because he did not want Westinghouse's company to have problems. This is one reason why he had little money later in life. He died in 1943 in a New York hotel room, alone and poor.

Today his name is used for a unit in physics and for an electric-car company. Most power grids in the world use AC, a system whose development owes a lot to Tesla. So electricity from solar, wind and hydro power plants reaches our homes partly thanks to his ideas.

transcript: LECTURER: Good morning, everyone. Today's talk is about the history of solar energy.

LECTURER: Our story starts in 1839. That was the year when a young French scientist, Edmond Becquerel, noticed that light could produce a small amount of electricity. He was only eighteen — sorry, nineteen — at the time. [Q1]

LECTURER: For more than a hundred years, not much happened. Then 1954 was the year when three scientists in the USA made the first practical solar cell. It was made from silicon, [Q2] a material which we still use in most solar panels today.
LECTURER: At first, solar cells were very expensive. That's the reason why one of the first big users was the space industry: in 1958 solar cells powered a satellite. [Q3]

LECTURER: So why are solar panels cheap now? The main reason why they became cheaper is mass production. [Q4] Factories became huge, especially in China. Some people say prices fell by eighty per cent between 2010 and 2020, but the real figure is closer to ninety. [Q5]

LECTURER: Finally, Uzbekistan — a country whose deserts get a lot of sunlight. Many people guess that one of its first large solar power plants is near Samarkand, but in fact it opened in 2021 in the Navoi region. [Q6] Today renewable energy is growing, and new solar farms join the national grid every year.

intro: Ega ergash gap = butun gap ega o'rnida: "[What he said] is true." Fe'l — BIRLIK (is).
WHAT — nima ekanligi: "What matters is time." HOW — qanday qilib: "How he solved it is amazing."
WHETHER — ikki imkoniyat (if — ega bo'la olmaydi!). THAT — fakt: "That she passed is surprising." (= It is surprising that she passed.)
WHOEVER / WHATEVER — "kim …sa" / "nima …sa" (= anyone who / anything that): "Whoever arrives first will get a prize."
Ega ergash gap ichida so'z tartibi — gapdek (ega + fe'l), savol tartibi emas: "What he does" (what does he — xato).
formulas: How he solved the problem is amazing.

That + ega + fe'l + birlik fe'l (= It is … that …)
That she passed the exam is surprising. = It is surprising that she passed.

I'd like to talk about my aunt, who runs a small bakery. She isn't rich, but she is very good with money. What she does first every month is pay herself: 20% of her income goes into a savings account. Whatever she buys for the bakery must be something she really needs. Her emergency fund saved her when her oven broke last winter. What I have learned from her is that small amounts matter. I think she is good with money because she plans, she is patient and she never takes a loan for things she doesn't need.
How to make a budget. It is also important that they understand interest, because many young people take loans without thinking.
It depends. Whether you can spend on experiences depends on your savings. What I prefer is a balance: save first, then enjoy a trip.

reading.title: Warren Buffett — what he did with money was simple
text: Warren Buffett was born in 1930 in Omaha, a city in the USA. What he loved as a boy was numbers. At six he sold chewing gum door to door; at eleven he bought his first shares; as a teenager he delivered newspapers and saved almost every dollar. That a teenager could save thousands of dollars in the 1940s was unusual — but Buffett was unusual.

How he became one of the world's most famous investors is surprisingly simple. He bought companies that he understood, that had honest managers and that would still exist in thirty years — and then he waited. Whether the market went up or down next month did not interest him; he once wrote that his favourite holding period was forever. What made him rich was not clever trading but compound interest and patience: most of his wealth came after his 50th birthday.

Whoever reads about Buffett's life is surprised by how he lived. He did not move to a palace: for decades his home was the house he bought in 1958 for 31,500 dollars. He drove ordinary cars and liked cheap fast-food breakfasts. What he spent on himself was tiny. What he gave away was enormous: he promised to give more than 99% of his fortune to charity.

For decades he wrote a letter to his shareholders every year, and many ordinary people read it like a textbook. His first rule, he often said, was never to lose money; his second rule was never to forget the first one. What he advised beginners was just as short: spend less than you earn, and start early.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 1 — table completion. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear a conversation between a student, Madina, and a bank adviser about her monthly budget.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): jadvalni o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (raqam, ot) belgilang.

transcript: ADVISER: Good morning, Madina. So, you'd like to make a monthly budget?
MADINA: Yes. What I get each month is about two million so'm, but by the end of the month it's all gone.
ADVISER: Let's start with transport. How much do you spend?
MADINA: About 200,000 — oh, sorry, with my student card it's 180,000. [Q1]
ADVISER: Then buy a monthly bus pass. What matters most is that you pay once. Now, food?
MADINA: Around 900,000. I often eat in cafés.
ADVISER: What I suggest is cooking at home and taking lunch to university. [Q2]
MADINA: OK. My phone is 100,000 a month — well, it was last year. Now it's 70,000. [Q3]
ADVISER: Choose a cheaper tariff. Next, savings. Whether you save ten per cent depends on discipline, not on your income.
MADINA: Should I keep it in a box at home?
ADVISER: No! Keep it in a savings account [Q4] — it pays interest.
MADINA: And emergencies?
ADVISER: Whoever has an emergency fund sleeps better. Put 50,000 into it every month until it covers three months of expenses. [Q5]
MADINA: OK. And my goal is a new phone — no, actually, a laptop for my studies. [Q6] I want it by next summer.
ADVISER: Good. How you spend small amounts decides whether you reach that goal.

intro: WH-so'zlar: I don't know where she lives. (where + ega + fe'l — savol tartibi EMAS).
WHETHER / IF — ikki imkoniyat: I don't know if/whether she will come.
Ega (18) vs to'ldiruvchi (19): What she said is true (ega) — I know what she said (to'ldiruvchi).
formulas: She said that she was tired.

Xohlagan odamingni taklif qilishing mumkin. / Xohlagan narsangni qil.

presentation: What do scientists say about the climate?
They say that the planet has warmed by more than one degree.
Do you know why the glaciers are melting?

notes: that tushiriladi (og'zaki): "I think (that) it's true"; wh-/whether tushirilmaydi.
Reported speech: said + that + odatda zamon orqaga: "She said that she was tired" (is → was). Agar gap hali ham haqiqat bo'lsa, present qolishi mumkin: She said the Earth is round.
ask/wonder/know + if/whether; "I wonder if…" — muloyim savol.
CCQ: I don't know where she lives. — Is it a question? (No) — Word order? (she lives)
CCQ: He asked if I was ready. — Did he ask a yes/no question? (Yes)
CCQ: Scientists say that the planet is warming. — Can we drop 'that'? (Yes) — And 'where' in 'I know where she lives'? (No)

Yesterday she said that she is tired, but today she feels fine.

Holat endi haqiqat emas → is → was.
I don't know that she will come or not.
I don't know whether/if she will come.
Can you explain how does it work?

I don't understand why did she leave.
I don't understand why she left.

class_ex.title: Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Weather and climate
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda; har javobda to'ldiruvchi ergash gap (I think that… / I'm not sure whether… / I know how…).
items: Part 1: What is the weather like in your city?
Part 1: Do you prefer hot or cold weather?
Part 1: Has the weather changed since you were a child?
Part 1: What do you do on very hot days?
Part 2 card: Describe a time when the weather changed your plans. You should say: when it was / what you planned / what happened — and explain how you felt.
Part 3: Do you think that Uzbekistan is affected by climate change?
Part 3: What can ordinary people do?
answers: Summers in Tashkent are very hot and dry, and winters are quite cold. I think that spring is the best season.
I prefer cold weather, to be honest. I don't understand how people can enjoy 40 degrees in July!
Yes, I think so. My grandmother says that summers are much hotter now than when she was young.
I usually stay at home in the afternoon and drink a lot of water. I go out in the evening when it gets cooler.

I'd like to talk about a day last spring when the weather changed my plans. My friends and I had planned a picnic in the mountains near Chimgan. The forecast said that it would be sunny, so we left early in the morning. But when we arrived, dark clouds appeared and a strong storm started. Nobody knew how long it would last, so we sat in the car and waited. After an hour we decided that we would go home. I felt disappointed, but then we had the picnic at my friend's house and it was really fun. That day I understood that the weather is not always easy to predict.
Yes, I think that it is. Summers are getting hotter, and many experts say that water scarcity is a serious problem in Central Asia.
I believe that small actions matter. If people know how their habits affect the planet, they save water, use public transport and plant trees.

class_ex.title: Writing (IELTS Task 2): causes–solutions
class_ex.instr: Climate change is a serious problem. What are its main causes, and what can individuals do to help? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. — Sinfda: 'solutions' body paragraf, 70–90 so'z, kamida 2 ta to'ldiruvchi ergash gap.
items: 1) Tur: causes–solutions — ikkala savolga javob.
2) Kalit so'zlar: main causes, individuals, help.
3) Reja: fikr + 2–3 yechim + sabab/misol + yakuniy gap.
4) Boshlanmalar: As for solutions, I believe that… / Many experts say that…
answers: Namuna 'solutions' paragraf (88 so'z): As for solutions, I believe that individuals can do a lot to reduce their carbon footprint. First, people should find out how much energy they use at home and switch off lights and devices they do not need. Second, many experts say that eating less meat can cut greenhouse gas emissions. Finally, young people can use public transport or cycle instead of asking their parents for a lift. Nobody knows whether these small steps are enough, but if millions of people take them, the impact will be significant.
Butun insho rejasi: kirish → causes (fossil fuels, deforestation) → solutions (energy at home, less meat, transport) → xulosa.

reading.title: Greta Thunberg — the girl who asked the world to listen to science
text: A. Greta Thunberg was born in 2003 in Stockholm, Sweden. When she was about eight, she learned at school what climate change was doing to the planet. She could not stop thinking about it. She read everything she could find and understood that scientists had been warning the world for many years.

B. In August 2018, at fifteen, she decided that she would not go to school. Instead, she sat in front of the Swedish parliament with a hand-painted sign: "School strike for the climate." She said that there was no point in studying for a future that adults were destroying. At first she sat alone, but later she continued her strike every Friday. Within about a year, millions of young people around the world had joined climate strikes.

C. In 2019 she was invited to a climate summit at the United Nations in New York. Because she believes that flying produces too much carbon, she crossed the Atlantic on a racing sailing boat, and the trip took about two weeks. At the UN she angrily told world leaders that their empty words had stolen her dreams and her childhood. Later that year, Time magazine named her Person of the Year, when she was only sixteen.

D. Greta has often said that she is not a scientist and that people should listen to the science, not to her. Whether her strikes really changed politics is a matter of debate. What nobody doubts is that a teenager made the whole world talk about how fast the ice is melting.
glossary: a matter of debate — bahsli masala

kahoot.q: I don't know where she ___.
kahoot.explain: Ergash gapda savol tartibi yo'q: where + ega + fe'l (she lives).

kahoot.q: Last week she said that she ___ tired, but now she feels fine.
kahoot.explain: said (o'tgan), holat endi haqiqat emas → am → was.

kahoot.q: I don't know ___ she will come.
kahoot.explain: Keladimi-yo'qmi → if / whether.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: Can you explain how does it work?
I don't understand why she left.
You can do whatever you want.
kahoot.explain: does yo'qoladi: Can you explain how it works?

kahoot.q: Scientists don't know ___.
options: how fast the ice is melting
how fast is the ice melting
how fast melting is the ice
how the ice fast is melting
kahoot.explain: how fast + ega + fe'l (savol tartibi emas).

kahoot.q: I don't understand why the glaciers ___ so fast last year.
kahoot.explain: did yo'qoladi, fe'l V2: why the glaciers melted.

kahoot.q: You can invite ___ you like.
kahoot.explain: Odam taklif qilinadi → whoever (kimni xohlasang).

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda ergash gap TO'LDIRUVCHI vazifasida?
kahoot.explain: I know (nimani?) what she said — to'ldiruvchi; qolganlarida — ega.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: I don't know whether the flood will come.
I don't know that the flood will come or not.
I don't know will the flood come.
I don't know whether will the flood come.
kahoot.explain: Ikki imkoniyat → whether + ega + fe'l.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Bu qanday ishlashini tushuntira olmayman."
options: I can't explain how it works.
I can't explain how does it work.
I can't explain how it work.
I can't explain it how works.
kahoot.explain: how + ega + fe'l: it works (does yo'q).

kahoot.q: The report says that CO2 levels ___ rising.
kahoot.explain: says (hozirgi) → zamon o'zgarmaydi; levels — ko'plik → are.

kahoot.q: Tell me ___ causes global warming.
kahoot.explain: Nima sabab bo'ladi → what (bu yerda what — ega: what causes).

kahoot.q: A long period with no rain is a ___.
kahoot.explain: drought — qurg'oqchilik. flood — suv toshqini.

kahoot.q: Cutting down forests is called ___.
kahoot.explain: deforestation — o'rmonlarni kesish. reforestation — qayta o'rmonlashtirish.

kahoot.q: Gases like CO2 and methane trap heat. They are ___ gases.
kahoot.explain: greenhouse gases — issiqxona gazlari.

kahoot.q: Your ___ footprint shows how much CO2 you produce.
kahoot.explain: carbon footprint — uglerod izi.

kahoot.q: "deforestation" so'zining antonimi qaysi?
kahoot.explain: deforestation ↔ reforestation.

kahoot.q: As glaciers melt, the sea ___ rises.
kahoot.explain: sea level — dengiz sathi.

kahoot.q: Reduce, reuse and ___ — the three R's.
kahoot.explain: Reduce, reuse, recycle — kamaytir, qayta foydalan, qayta ishla.

kahoot.q: "net zero" ma'nosi?
options: chiqarilgan va yutilgan CO2 teng — sof nol
kahoot.explain: net zero — chiqarilgan CO2 = yutilgan CO2.

listening.audios: Jony Academy original skripti — ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi (~2 daq). Kitob AUDIO 141–145 — ixtiyoriy, uyda.
intro: IELTS Listening Part 3 — multiple choice. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
You will hear two students, Dilnoza and Sardor, preparing a presentation about a climate report.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): 5 savolni o'qing, har savolda kalit so'zlarni belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: DILNOZA: Sardor, our climate change presentation is on Friday. Have you finished reading the report?
SARDOR: Yes. At first I thought that it was mainly about the Aral Sea, but that's only one short chapter.
DILNOZA: So what's the main conclusion?
SARDOR: The report says that heatwaves are becoming much more common in our region. [Q1]
DILNOZA: Right. And scientists believe that global warming will also bring more droughts.
SARDOR: Now, the graphs. Shall we show the bar chart of rainfall?
DILNOZA: I'm not sure whether people will understand it. The line graph of summer temperatures is much clearer. [Q2]
SARDOR: OK, the line graph. Do you know why the report talks so much about farms?
DILNOZA: Because farms use most of the water here — much more than homes or factories. [Q3] Drip irrigation and sustainable farming could save a lot.
SARDOR: Hmm. I think that we should talk about saving water at home instead — shorter showers, fixing taps. Students can actually do that.
DILNOZA: I don't agree. Farming is the key point of the report. [Q4]
SARDOR: Well, we can mention both. Do you know how long our talk should be?
DILNOZA: Ten minutes — oh, sorry, the teacher changed it on Monday. It's twelve minutes now. [Q5]
SARDOR: Great, then there's time for both ideas.

tasks.title: Multiple choice — A, B or C
tasks.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
items: 1 What is the main conclusion of the report? A) The Aral Sea is disappearing. B) Heatwaves are becoming more common. C) There is more rain than before.
2 Which graph will the students use? A) a bar chart of rainfall B) a map of the Aral Sea C) a line graph of summer temperatures
3 According to Dilnoza, who uses most of the water? A) homes B) factories C) farms
4 What do the students disagree about? A) which solution to focus on B) which graph to show C) who will speak first
5 How long will the presentation be? A) ten minutes B) twelve minutes C) fifteen minutes

lessons.title: Gerund
lessons.grammar_topic: GERUND — V-ing / being + V3 / having + V3 / having been + V3
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 20 – Gerund (4 qatorli jadval); WILDLIFE CONSERVATION (52 so'z); Reading — David Attenborough (Jony Academy matni, moslashtirilgan); kitob Topic 141–143 uyga (ixtiyoriy); kitob AUDIO 146–150 (ixtiyoriy); SPEAKING/WRITING mavzusi — rahbar rejasi (IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 20-qator): "Using public transport vs. owning a car"
objectives: Gerundning 4 shaklini (simple/perfect × active/passive) tanish va tuzish.
Gerund talab qiladigan fe'llar (enjoy, avoid, mind, suggest, finish, keep, practise, consider, deny, admit) va predloglardan keyin gerundni to'g'ri ishlata olish.
Perfect gerund (regret having wasted) va passive gerund (dislike being told) ma'nosini tushuntirish; participle clause'ni (Having seen…, I…) gerunddan farqlash.
Listening (IELTS Part 2): qo'riqxona koordinatorining nutqidan 5 ta ishni joylar bilan (A–F) moslay olish.

SPEAKING (IELTS Part 3): Using public transport vs owning a car — 4–5 savolga 3–4 gapli javob (javob → sabab → misol), gerund bilan; WRITING: Using public transport vs owning a car — AD jadval sinfda, 150–200 so'zli insho uyda (W-B1-AD).
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 20 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.
CORE 20 varag'i — dars sahifasining Lug'at tabidan (PDF).
Kahoot: bu darsda o'ynalmaydi (pt4); shu darsning Kahooti L21 boshida — 'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi (L20).
Progress test 4 (pt4) varaqlari + ustoz kaliti. Listening: skript ustozda (yashirin transcript), ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi; audio fayl kerak emas.

Writing/Speaking rubrikasi — shu darsdagi W-B1-AD va S-B1-P3 jadvallari (WRITING mashqidan keyin); juftlik tekshiruvi — PEER-AD (WRITING mashqi izohida). Progress test 4 Writing bo'limi — test ichidagi W-B1 jadvali.
timeline: Warm-up: 4 gerund shakli
Ustoz doskaga: "I enjoy watching animals. I hate being filmed. He regrets having hunted. She remembers having been taken to a zoo." — o'quvchilar faol/passiv, oddiy/perfect deb belgilaydi.
PROGRESS TEST 4 (pt4) — 15–19-darslar

Listening 6 · Reading 7 · Grammar 6 · Vocabulary 4 · Writing 12 daq — 40 ball (L5 · R5 · G10 · V8 · W12); o'tish 28/40. Varaq va kalit — pt4 (listening skriptini ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi). Vocabulary'da L19 Climate change CORE (2+ so'z) — yozma normativ o'rniga. Tahlil — L21 da.
YANGI MAVZU: Gerund (V-ing / being V3 / having V3 / having been V3)

10 daq taqdimot: jadval (kitob yoki grammar.formulas) + presentation 1, 2, 3, 4, 7-savol-javoblar juftlikda; gerund qachon: fe'ldan keyin, predlogdan keyin, ega sifatida. CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq amaliyot: 'Faolmi, passivmi?' (og'zaki, butun sinf, 1 — namuna).
Lug'at: Wildlife conservation — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

10 so'z: wildlife, conservation, protect / protection, endangered species, extinct / extinction, habitat, wildlife reserve, poaching / poacher, illegal trade, captivity — so'z → ma'no → gerund bilan 1 gap; 'Muhofaza lug'ati' (match) — og'zaki. Qolgan CORE va STRONG — flashcard (uyda), SUPER — ixtiyoriy.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 4 qator)

intro: SIMPLE ACTIVE — V-ing: "I like reading books." Ega bajaradi.
SIMPLE PASSIVE — being + V3: "He dislikes being told what to do." Egaga nisbatan bajariladi.
PERFECT ACTIVE — having + V3: "He regrets having wasted time." (oldin bo'lgan ish).
PERFECT PASSIVE — having been + V3: "She remembers having been given an award."

Gerund keladi: enjoy/avoid/mind/suggest/finish/keep/practise/consider/deny/admit/miss/risk + V-ing; predlogdan keyin (interested in protecting, without asking, after leaving); ega/to'ldiruvchi sifatida.

8. Tekshirish: Listening, Reading, Grammar — har band 1 ball (Listening: so'z chegarasidan oshsa yoki imlo xato bo'lsa — 0; raqam so'z yoki son bilan yozilsa ham to'g'ri; Reading: TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN o'rniga YES/NO — 0; Grammar: ikki harf belgilansa — 0). 9. Jurnalga bo'limlar bo'yicha yozing: L __/5 · R __/5 · G __/10 · V __/8 · W __/12 = __/40 va natija (O'TDI / QAYTA ISHLASH / O'TMADI). Writing ballari 4 mezon bo'yicha alohida yoziladi (masalan 2-2-3-2).

10. Og'zaki qayta tekshiruv (QAYTA ISHLASH o'quvchilari, 21-dars tahlil bosqichi, har o'quvchiga 5 savol, 4/5 — o'tdi): (1) Join: 'This is the shop. I bought my phone there.' → This is the shop where I bought my phone. (2) Join: 'I have a neighbour. His car is electric.' → I have a neighbour whose car is electric. (3) Correct: 'I don't know where does she live.' → I don't know where she lives. (4) Complete: '___ she saves half her salary is surprising.' → That. (5) Explain in English: What is a drought? → a long period with little or no rain.

11. Qayta topshirish (O'TMADI, 7 kun ichida): Grammar va Vocabulary bo'limlari shu varaqdan, lekin boshqa tartibda chop etiladi — Grammar: 7, 3, 10, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6, 4, 8; Vocabulary: 3, 1, 4, 2, 8, 6, 7, 5 (kalit — har bandning o'z javobi) + Writing — zaxira mavzu (oxirgi bo'limda). items: 1. AGENT: Good morning, GreenBox online store. My name is Lola. How can I help you?
2. CUSTOMER: Hello. I'm calling about an order which arrived yesterday. There's a problem with it.
3. AGENT: I'm sorry to hear that. What's your order number, please?
4. CUSTOMER: It's four, seven, two, nine, one.
5. AGENT: Thank you. So you ordered a solar power bank, the one which charges in sunlight?
6. CUSTOMER: Yes. The power bank itself is fine, but the cable that came with it is broken, so I can't charge my phone.
7. AGENT: I see. Would you like a new cable, or would you prefer a full refund?
8. CUSTOMER: A refund, please. I don't want to wait for another delivery.
9. AGENT: No problem. First, please send the item back. You'll find a free return label inside the box.
10. CUSTOMER: When do I need to send it back?
11. AGENT: You have two weeks, so before the eighteenth of May.
12. CUSTOMER: And how long will the refund take? Three days?
13. AGENT: Not quite. The money usually comes back to your bank account in five working days.
14. CUSTOMER: Great. Thank you for your help.
15. AGENT: You're welcome. Have a nice day.

class_ex.title: Reading — matn: "A School That Runs on Sunshine" (7 daqiqa, savollar bilan birga)
class_ex.type: Original matn (200 so'z), qayta tiklanuvchi energiya; relative clause'lar bilan; maktab va qahramon to'qima
class_ex.instr: Read the text. Then answer questions 1–5 in the next part. (Matnni o'qing va keyingi qismdagi 1–5-savollarga javob bering.)
items: A School That Runs on Sunshine

Five years ago, a small school in a village near Samarkand had a serious problem: its electricity bills were higher than its budget for books. The head teacher, Mrs Karimova, who had taught physics for twenty years, decided to find a cleaner and cheaper solution.

With help from parents, the school put forty solar panels on the roof of the sports hall. The panels, which cost about the same as two new school buses, were paid for by a local company whose owner was a former student. On sunny days, the panels now produce more electricity than the school uses. The extra energy goes to the village grid, where it helps to light the streets at night.

The project also changed the lessons. Every week, students measure the school's energy consumption and write short reports which explain why the numbers go up or down. Winter is the season when the panels produce the least energy, so the school still buys some electricity from a power plant that burns coal.
What surprised the teachers most was the students' interest. Several former students now study engineering at university, and one of them wants to build a small wind turbine for the school.

9. Scientists still don't know exactly how fast ___. A) will the sea level rise B) does the sea level rise C) the sea level will rise D) the sea level rise
10. Our teacher asked us ___ we had ever seen a flood. A) that B) what C) if D) whoever
why: L15: odam + ega vazifasida → who (who + fe'l 'bought').
L15: vergulli (non-defining) gap → which; 'that' vergul bilan ishlatilmaydi.
L16: joy + to'liq gap (all our orders are packed THERE) → where.
L16: gap oxirida 'from' bor → which (…which I order from); where / in which + from — ikki marta predlog.
L17: egalik ('families' homes') → whose + ot; who's = who is — xato.
L17: the reason + why + ega + fe'l; 'the reason because' — xato.
L18: ikki imkoniyat, ega ergash gap → whether; 'if' ega o'rnida kelmaydi.
L18: ega ergash gap + birlik fe'l → is; 'it is' — ortiqcha 'it'.
L19: to'ldiruvchi ergash gapda darak tartibi: how fast + ega + fe'l (the sea level will rise).
L19: bilvosita umumiy savol (Have you ever seen a flood?) → asked + if/whether; 'asked us that' — xato; what/whoever uchun gapda bo'sh o'rin yo'q (a flood bor).

Second, they should save a small part of every payment, even if it is only ten percent. class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Using public transport vs owning a car
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ gerund (Owning a car…, Using the metro…, avoid waiting, instead of driving, being stuck in traffic).
items: Part 1: Does your family have a car?
Part 1: Would you like to learn to drive? Why?
Part 3: Why is owning a car so important for many families in Uzbekistan?
Part 3: What are the hidden costs of owning a car?
Part 3: In what situations is driving better than taking a bus or the metro?
Part 3: How does driving instead of using public transport affect a city?
Part 3: What could persuade car owners to leave their cars at home?
answers: Yes, we have an old Chevrolet Cobalt. My father uses it for driving to work, and at weekends we use it for visiting my grandparents in the village.
Yes, definitely. Being able to drive gives you freedom. I'm thinking about taking lessons after my eighteenth birthday, because driving my mother to the bazaar would help her a lot.

Well, I think the main reason is freedom. Owning a car means you can leave home whenever you want, even late at night. It is also about status: for many people, having a nice car shows success. For example, families use their car for visiting relatives in other regions and for going to weddings.

Most people only think about the price of the car, but keeping it is expensive too. You pay for fuel every week, insurance every year and repairs when something breaks. Parking in the city centre costs money as well. For example, my uncle spends almost a quarter of his salary on running his car.

I'd say driving is better when you carry heavy things or travel with small children. It is also better outside the city, because there are few buses in villages. For example, when we go to Chimgan in winter, going by car is much easier than changing buses three times.

Mostly in a bad way. If everyone drives instead of using buses, the roads become full and being stuck in traffic becomes normal. The air also gets dirtier, especially in winter. For example, on Amir Temur Street in the evening, cars hardly move, and the smell of petrol is very strong.

I think saving time and money would persuade them. If there were a fast bus line from every suburb, many people would stop driving to work. Paying more for parking in the centre could also help. However, some people simply enjoy driving, so the city should make walking and cycling more pleasant too.
class_ex.note: ICQ: Necha gapda javob berasiz? (3–4) — Misol kerakmi? (Ha). Gap boshlanmalari: Well, I think… / The main advantage is that… / On the other hand, … / For example, … / So overall, … Gerund: ega sifatida (Owning a car is…), fe'ldan keyin (avoid / enjoy / stop + V-ing), predlogdan keyin (instead of / for / without + V-ing). Baholash — S-B1-P3 (pastdagi jadval). Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 20-qator ("Using public transport vs. owning a car"); savollar va namunalar — Jony Academy, original.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Using public transport vs owning a car
class_ex.instr: Some people think that owning a car is necessary in modern life, while others prefer to use public transport. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of both and give your own opinion. Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval; uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: ikki variantni taqqoslash (advantages and disadvantages of both) + o'z fikringiz — fikr kirishda va xulosada aniq bo'lsin.
2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: owning a car / necessary in modern life / prefer to use public transport / advantages and disadvantages of both / your own opinion.

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + fikringiz) → Body 1: shaxsiy mashina — afzallik va kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: jamoat transporti — afzallik va kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (o'z tanlovingiz va sababi)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of … is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, … also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …

5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: gerund 2+ marta — ega sifatida (Owning a car…, Using the metro…), fe'ldan keyin (avoid paying, enjoy driving), predlogdan keyin (instead of driving, without asking); xohlasangiz being + V3 (being stuck in traffic). Mavzu so'zlari: fuel, insurance, parking, repairs, freedom, status, traffic, passengers.
answers: Namuna kirish (38 so'z): Nowadays, many people believe that having a car is essential, while others happily travel by bus and metro. Both options have strengths and weaknesses, but in my view, using public transport is the wiser choice for city people.

Namuna AD jadval: Shaxsiy mashina — Afzalliklar — 1) erkinlik: istalgan vaqtda chiqish, og'ir xarid tashish; 2) status: ko'p oilalar uchun muvaffaqiyat belgisi; Kamchiliklar — 1) xarajat: fuel, insurance, parking, repairs; 2) tirbandlik: Toshkentda kechqurun qisqa yo'l 1 soat. Jamoat transporti — Afzalliklar — 1) bu xarajatlar yo'q, yo'lda kitob o'qish yoki dam olish mumkin; 2) mashinani uyda qoldirish — havoda tutun kamroq; Kamchiliklar — 1) har qishloqqa bormaydi; 2) kechasi qatnov qiyin.

Namuna insho (188 so'z) — kirish: Nowadays, many people believe that having a car is essential, while others happily travel by bus and metro. Both options have strengths and weaknesses, but in my view, using public transport is the wiser choice for city people.

Namuna insho — body 1: Owning a car gives people freedom, and for many families it is also a sign of success. Drivers can leave at any time and carry heavy shopping easily. However, fuel, insurance, parking and repairs make a car expensive to keep. Moreover, being stuck in traffic wastes time. For example, a short trip across Tashkent in the evening can take an hour.

Namuna insho — body 2: Using public transport, on the other hand, has different strengths. Passengers avoid these bills and can read or rest instead of watching the road. In addition, leaving the car at home means less smoke in the air. The main drawback is that buses do not reach every village, and travelling late at night can be difficult.
Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, a car offers freedom and status, but it is costly and adds to traffic. Personally, I would use the metro every day and rent a car only for long family trips.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — gerund: having a car, using public transport, Owning a car, Using public transport, instead of watching, leaving the car at home, travelling late at night; being + V3: being stuck in traffic; bog'lovchilar — while, but, However, Moreover, For example, on the other hand, In addition, so, The main drawback, In conclusion, Personally; mavzu so'zlari — freedom, status, fuel, insurance, parking, repairs, traffic, passengers, metro, smoke.
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 20-qator ("Using public transport vs. owning a car"); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). Taqqoslash tuzilmasi: Body 1 — shaxsiy mashinaning afzallik/kamchiliklari, Body 2 — jamoat transportiniki, Xulosa — o'z tanlovi va sababi. PEER-AD (juftlik, Ha/Yo'q): 1) savol o'z so'zlari bilan? 2) afzallik va kamchilik alohida xatboshida (taqqoslashda — har variant alohida xatboshida)? 3) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol? 4) 4+ bog'lovchi? 5) dars grammatikasi 2+? 6) 150+ so'z? Namuna insho o'quvchiga uy inshosi tekshirilgandan keyin ko'rsatiladi.

homework.title: MAJBURIY: WRITING — Using public transport vs owning a car (uy inshosi)
homework.instr: Some people think that owning a car is necessary in modern life, while others prefer to use public transport. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of both and give your own opinion. Sinfdagi AD jadvaldan davom eting: 4 xatboshi (kirish — mashina — jamoat transporti — xulosa), 150–200 so'z; gerund (Owning a car… / instead of driving / avoid paying) 2+ marta (~25 daq)

Tekshiruv: (1) mashina va jamoat transporti alohida xatboshida, har birida afzallik va kamchilik; (2) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol; (3) gerund 2+; (4) 4+ bog'lovchi; (5) 150–200 so'z; (6) xulosada o'z tanlovi va sababi.
Namuna insho — sinfdagi WRITING mashqi javobida.

homework.title: IXTIYORIY: Speaking Part 2 (og'zaki) — Wildlife
homework.instr: 1 daq tayyorgarlik, 1–2 daq gapirib ilovaga yuboring (~5 daq)
items: Part 2 card: Describe a wild animal you find interesting. You should say: what it is / where it lives / how you learned about it — and explain why you find it interesting.
answers: I'd like to talk about the snow leopard. It is a big wild cat that lives high in the mountains of Central Asia, including Uzbekistan. I learned about it from a nature documentary. Filming snow leopards is very difficult, because they are shy and avoid being seen by people. I find this animal interesting for two reasons. First, it is perfectly adapted to cold weather and can jump very far. Second, it is an endangered species. Its habitat is getting smaller, and poaching is still a problem. I think protecting snow leopards means protecting the whole mountain ecosystem, and I would be interested in becoming a volunteer in a reserve one day.

reading.title: David Attenborough — seventy years of filming the wild
text: David Attenborough was born in 1926 near London. As a boy he enjoyed collecting fossils and stones, and he dreamed of seeing animals from all over the world. After studying natural sciences at Cambridge, he joined the BBC in 1952. In 1954 he was sent to West Africa to film animals for a new series, 'Zoo Quest'. Being given this job so young changed his life, and he never forgot having been chosen for it.

For more than seventy years he made and narrated nature documentaries, such as 'Life on Earth', 'The Blue Planet' and 'Planet Earth', which were watched by millions of people. Filming wild animals often meant waiting for months: getting good footage of a snow leopard hunting in the mountains took his team a very long time. The work was sometimes dangerous — snakes, storms, high cliffs — and being afraid was part of the job. But he kept travelling and filming for decades.

Later his message changed. Instead of only showing the beauty of nature, he kept warning people that many wild animal populations had become much smaller since he started filming. He believed that explaining the problem clearly was the most important task. In 2017 his series 'Blue Planet II' showed how much plastic ends up in the ocean. After watching it, many people started using fewer plastic bags and bottles.

In his late nineties he was still working and recording narration for new films. Many viewers remember having watched his documentaries as children. His films carry a simple message: caring about nature is the first step, and protecting it comes next.

tasks.title: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: Do the statements agree with the information in the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
items: Attenborough studied natural sciences before he joined the BBC.
His first trip for 'Zoo Quest' was to South America.
Filming a snow leopard hunting was quick and easy.
Attenborough was once badly hurt by a snake.
After 'Blue Planet II', many people used less plastic.
'Blue Planet II' was filmed in only one year.
answers: FALSE (it took a very long time)
tasks.note: NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q; FALSE — matn teskarisini aytadi.

tasks.title: Multiple choice
tasks.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. (To'g'ri javob harfini tanlang.)
items: Why was the 'Zoo Quest' job important for Attenborough? A It made him rich. B It changed his life. C It was his first job at the BBC.
What did Attenborough warn people about? A Many wild animal populations were getting smaller. B Zoos were closing. C Documentaries were too expensive.
What happened after people watched 'Blue Planet II'? A They stopped swimming in the sea. B They used less plastic. C They visited the ocean more.
According to the text, what is the message of his films? A Wild animals should live in zoos. B Caring about nature comes before protecting it. C Only scientists can protect nature.

kahoot.q: I enjoy ___ animals in the wild.
kahoot.explain: enjoy + V-ing (gerund): I enjoy watching animals.

kahoot.q: He dislikes ___ what to do.
kahoot.explain: Unga aytishadi (passiv) → being + V3: being told.

kahoot.q: He regrets ___ so much time.
kahoot.explain: Oldin bo'lgan ish, o'zi qilgan → having + V3: having wasted.

kahoot.q: She remembers ___ an award by the president.
kahoot.explain: Unga berilgan (passiv) + oldin → having been + V3.

kahoot.q: Poachers were arrested for ___ elephants.
kahoot.explain: Predlogdan (for) keyin → V-ing: for killing.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: He admitted to kill the deer.
She is interested in protecting wildlife.
They avoided being seen by the lions.
kahoot.explain: admit + V-ing: He admitted killing / having killed the deer.

kahoot.q: Rangers keep ___ the park at night.
kahoot.explain: keep + V-ing: keep patrolling (patrul qilishda davom etadi).

kahoot.q: "being + V3" gerundning qaysi shakli?
kahoot.explain: V-ing — Simple Active; being V3 — Simple Passive; having V3 — Perfect Active.

kahoot.q: The tiger was saved from ___ by hunters.
kahoot.explain: Yo'lbarsni o'ldirishardi (passiv) + predlog from → being killed.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: Would you mind closing the cage?
Would you mind to close the cage?
Would you mind close the cage?
Would you mind to closing the cage?
kahoot.explain: mind + V-ing: Would you mind closing...?

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Men hayvonlarni himoya qilishga qiziqaman."
options: I am interested in protecting animals.
I am interested in protect animals.
I am interested to protecting animals.
I am interested on protecting animals.
kahoot.explain: interested IN + V-ing: interested in protecting.

kahoot.q: The bear escaped without ___.
kahoot.explain: without (predlog) + passiv gerund → being + V3: without being noticed.

kahoot.q: An animal that eats only plants is a ___.
kahoot.explain: herbivore — o'txo'r; carnivore — go'shtxo'r; omnivore — hammaxo'r.

kahoot.q: Animals that may soon disappear are ___ species.
kahoot.explain: endangered species — yo'qolib ketish xavfidagi turlar. extinct — allaqachon yo'qolgan.

kahoot.q: Illegal hunting of wild animals is ___.
kahoot.explain: poaching — brakonyerlik (noqonuniy ov).

kahoot.q: The natural home of an animal is its ___.
kahoot.explain: habitat — tabiiy yashash muhiti. captivity — asirlik (qafas, hayvonot bog'i).

kahoot.q: The dodo no longer exists — it is ___.
kahoot.explain: extinct — butunlay yo'qolib ketgan (dodo qushi).

kahoot.q: "wild" so'zining antonimi qaysi?
kahoot.explain: wild (yovvoyi) ↔ domestic (xonaki: it, mushuk, sigir).

kahoot.q: A person whose job is to protect a national park is a ___.
kahoot.explain: ranger — qo'riqxona/bog' qo'riqchisi. poacher — brakonyer.

kahoot.q: "prey" nimani bildiradi?
kahoot.explain: prey — o'lja; predator — yirtqich (ovlaydigan hayvon).

listening.audios: Jony Academy original skripti — ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi (~1.5–2 daq). Kitob AUDIO 146–150 — ixtiyoriy, uyda.
intro: IELTS Listening Part 2 — matching. Where will volunteers do each job? Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to questions 1–5.
You will hear the volunteer coordinator of a nature reserve talking to a group of new volunteers.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollar va A–F joylarni o'qing; bitta joy ortiqcha — u ishlatilmaydi.
Ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi: 1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: COORDINATOR: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Greenvale Wildlife Reserve. I'm Dilnoza, the volunteer coordinator. I know you all enjoy spending time in nature, so here are the five jobs.

COORDINATOR: First, bird counting. The job involves counting birds early in the morning during the spring migration. You might think we do this at the lake, but the lake birds are counted by our scientists. Volunteers count birds in the wetland. [Q1]

COORDINATOR: Next, tree planting. Most volunteers enjoy planting trees more than anything else. This year we aren't planting in the forest — it's too wet there after the rain. Instead, you'll plant young trees along the mountain path. [Q2]
COORDINATOR: Then there's cleaning. After being trained by a ranger, you'll collect plastic and other rubbish around the lake. [Q3] Please wear gloves and avoid touching broken glass.

COORDINATOR: Some of you are interested in taking photos, so you'll be checking our camera traps. They're in the forest, where the deer live. [Q4] And remember: avoid feeding the animals, even if they come close. Feeding them makes them lose their fear of people.

COORDINATOR: Finally, children's tours. School groups used to meet at the car park — sorry, that was last year. Now they meet at the visitor centre, [Q5] and you'll tell them about the endangered species we protect and why their habitat matters.
COORDINATOR: Does anyone mind working at weekends? No? Great.

tasks.title: Volunteer jobs — Greenvale Wildlife Reserve
tasks.instr: Where will volunteers do each job? Write the correct letter, A–F. There is ONE extra place.
items: 1 counting birds
2 planting trees
3 collecting rubbish
4 checking camera traps
5 meeting school groups for tours
answers: E (visitor centre; chalg'itgich: car park). A — ortiqcha
tasks.note: Har ishga bitta harf yozing; bitta joy ortiqcha.

lessons.title: Infinitive
lessons.grammar_topic: INFINITIV — to V1 / to be V3 / to be V-ing / to have V3 / to have been V3

objectives: Infinitiv shakllarini tuzish: to V1 / to be V3 / to be V-ing / to have V3 / to have been V3.
want / hope / seem / claim / manage / refuse + to V1; stop / remember / forget / try / regret + to V1 yoki V-ing ma'no farqi.

CORE 20 varag'i — dars sahifasining Lug'at tabidan (PDF).

timeline: Warm-up: infinitiv shakllari
Doskada: "She wants to fly. The rocket needs to be checked. He seems to be sleeping. He claims to have seen a UFO." — har gapda: faol/passiv? oddiy/davomli/perfect?
TAKROR: Kahoot — L20 (Gerund)

Ustoz 20 so'zni o'zbekcha aytadi, o'quvchi inglizcha yozadi (4 daq); 1 daq juftlikda tekshirish, kalit — L20 Lug'at tabi. 17/20+ — bajarildi (2 coin).
PROGRESS TEST 4 tahlili

Ustoz testni oldindan tekshiradi. (1) Har bo'limdan eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 band — doskada, o'quvchilar o'z varag'ida tuzatadi (4 daq); (2) Writing: 2 umumiy xato + 1 yaxshi namuna gap (2 daq); (3) 50–69% (20–27/40) — individual vazifa, <50% — qayta topshirish sanasi (2 daq).
