YANGI MAVZU: Infinitive — 6 shakl + to V1 / V-ing ma'no farqi

10 daq: presentation 1–5 + jadval 6 qator (to be being V3 — faqat tanib olish); farq stop / remember / forget / try / regret — grammar.intro 2, presentation 7–8. CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq: class_ex 1 (yakka).
Lug'at: Space exploration — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

space exploration, universe, galaxy, planet, orbit, astronaut / cosmonaut, spacecraft, satellite, space station, mission — so'z → ma'no → infinitivli 1 gap; class_ex 5 (juftlik, 2 daq). Qolgan CORE va STRONG — uyda flashcard, SUPER — kuchlilarga.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 6 qator)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. Me'yor — normativ 2-qator.
Sinf mashqlari: Gerund yoki infinitiv? (8 daq) + Fe'l tanlang (6 daq)

Gerund yoki infinitiv? — yakka, juftlikda tekshirish (8 daq); Fe'l tanlang — juftlik (6 daq); 2 daq javoblar. ZAXIRA: Xatoni toping. Vaqt yetmasa: avval 'Xatoni toping', keyin 'Fe'l tanlang' 5–6-bandlari uyga.
Listening (IELTS Part 4): sentence completion
2 daq tayyorgarlik; 1-tinglash; 1 daq juftlikda solishtirish; 2-tinglash; 3 daq javoblar — dalil gap skriptdan o'qiladi; 2 daq 2 ta target gapni og'zaki tiklash.
Reading: T/F/NG + short-answer questions
3 daq gist: 'Why is Dzhanibekov famous?' (he repaired a dead, frozen station; the Dzhanibekov effect); 5 daq T/F/NG; 4 daq short-answer. ZAXIRA topshiriq — uyga.
Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Future plans and space
Part 1 juftlikda 3 daq; Part 2: 1 daq tayyorgarlik, A 1.5 daq, B 1.5 daq (sherik peer-b1 ni belgilaydi); Part 3 — 2 daq; ustoz 1 daq feedback (S-B1: 1 kuchli tomon + 1 tuzatish).
Writing (IELTS Task 2): opinion — Writing 9 reja + kirish
2 daq savol tahlili (opinion: 'To what extent…', kalit so'zlar); 2 daq reja; 6 daq kirish (40–50 so'z); 2 daq juftlikda peer-b1. Uyda to'liq insho.
Exit ticket
Qog'ozda: 1) He claims ___ (meet) an astronaut last year. (to have met) 2) Joining two spacecraft in space — bitta so'z? (docking) 3) Opinion essay kirishida nima shart? (aniq pozitsiya)
Uyga vazifa
MAJBURIY: flashcard, Writing 9, tarjima, og'zaki normativ. IXTIYORIY: Topic 146–148, jadval + STRONG 20, 'Kelajak rejalarim'.

intro: 6 shakl — grammar.formulas. Passive (to be V3) — ishni boshqa kishi bajaradi; Continuous (to be V-ing) — hozir davom etayotgan ish; Perfect (to have V3) — asosiy fe'ldan OLDIN bo'lgan ish; to be being V3 — faqat tanib olish uchun.

Farq: stop to rest (dam olish uchun to'xtadi) / stop resting (dam olishni to'xtatdi); remember to call (qo'ng'iroq qilishni unutma) / remember calling (qo'ng'iroq qilganini eslaydi); forget to lock (qulflashni unutmoq) / never forget seeing (ko'rganini unutmaslik); regret to inform (afsus bilan ma'lum qilmoq) / regret saying (aytganiga afsuslanmoq); try to open (urinib ko'rmoq) / try pushing (sinab ko'rmoq).
formulas: The book needs to be read.
The project seems to be being delayed.
He claims to have seen a ghost.
She is happy to have been given the award.
presentation: What does she want to do?
She wants to become an astronaut.
Does the rocket need to be checked?
Yes, every rocket needs to be checked before launch.
What does the crew seem to be doing?
They seem to be preparing for a spacewalk.
Does he claim to have seen a UFO?
Yes, he claims to have seen one over the desert.
Is she happy to have been chosen?
She is very happy to have been chosen for the mission.
Did Dzhanibekov manage to save the station?
Yes, he managed to repair Salyut-7 in 1985.
Did you remember to watch the launch?
Yes — and I remember watching my first launch on TV when I was a child.
Why did they stop the countdown?
They stopped to check the fuel.
notes: Infinitiv inkori: not to + V1: "He decided not to go."
Fe'l + ob'ekt + infinitiv: want/ask/tell/allow + somebody + to do: "The commander asked him to fly again."
Modal va make/let dan keyin to yo'q: "let him go", "made us wait".
CCQ: He seems to have left. — Did he leave in the past? (probably yes) Are we 100% sure? (No)
CCQ: The rocket needs to be checked. — Who checks? (someone else) Is it done yet? (No)
CCQ: We stopped to check the fuel. — Did we stop our journey? (Yes) Why? (to check the fuel)
CCQ: I'll never forget seeing the launch. — Did I see it? (Yes, in the past)
mistakes: The book needs to be read.
He claims to see a ghost last year.
He claims to have seen a ghost last year.

reading.title: Vladimir Dzhanibekov — the Tashkent cosmonaut who saved a dead station
text: Vladimir Dzhanibekov was born in 1942 in the Bostanlyk district of Tashkent region. As a boy he wanted to be a physicist, but later he decided to become a pilot. In 1970 he was chosen to be trained as a cosmonaut. He is known to have flown into space five times and to have been named Hero of the Soviet Union twice.

His most famous flight was in 1985. The Salyut-7 space station had stopped answering: its batteries had died, and it was flying uncontrolled, frozen and dark. Nobody had ever tried to dock with a dead station by hand. Dzhanibekov and his partner Viktor Savinykh were asked to do it. They managed to approach the station, to dock manually and to open the door. Inside it was far below zero, and there was ice on the walls. Working in winter clothes and hats, they managed to repair the electrical system over several days. The mission is often described as one of the most difficult repairs in the history of spaceflight.

During one of his flights he noticed something strange: a small wing nut spinning in zero gravity seemed to flip over by itself every few seconds. Today this is called the Dzhanibekov effect, and it helps scientists understand how spinning objects behave.

After his last flight in 1985 he did not fly into space again, but he later became a general. He is also known as a talented painter. In Uzbekistan he is remembered as a national hero, and many children who hope to fly to space one day learn his story.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 4 — sentence completion. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear part of a lecture about how astronauts are selected and trained.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (raqam, nom, sifat, ot) belgilang.

transcript: LECTURER: Today's talk is about how astronauts are selected and trained.

LECTURER: A space agency receives thousands of applications from people who hope to fly into space. To be selected, candidates need to have a degree in science or engineering, and most of them seem to have worked as pilots or engineers before.
LECTURER: People often think astronauts are very young. In fact, the average age of new candidates is about thirty — sorry, I mean thirty-four [Q1].
LECTURER: All astronauts need to speak good English, and anyone who hopes to live on the space station is expected to learn Russian [Q2] as well. French and German are useful, but not required.
LECTURER: There are medical checks, of course, but many candidates seem to find the psychological [Q3] test the most difficult.

LECTURER: Basic training takes about twelve months — no, let me check — eighteen [Q4] months. It is important to be trained in real conditions, so astronauts practise in a huge pool. In a heavy space suit, they can work underwater for up to six [Q5] hours in one session.
LECTURER: Finally, every crew member has to be trained to repair equipment and to give first aid [Q6], because there is no hospital in orbit.

intro: GERUND EGA — tabiiy, umumiy: "Swimming is good for health." "Exporting cotton was Uzbekistan's main income."
INFINITIV EGA — rasmiy/she'riy: "To swim is fun." Odatda "It is fun to swim." / "It is hard to compete with China."
Fe'l birlik: "Trading is…", "To trade is…" (are — xato).

Xarita (20–22-darslar): faqat gerund / faqat infinitiv — formulas 4–5; IKKALASI (ma'no deyarli bir xil): like / love / hate / start / begin / continue / prefer + V-ing yoki to V1; ma'no farqi — formulas 6.
formulas: It is hard to compete with China.
enjoy / avoid / mind / suggest / finish / keep / consider / deny + V-ing
Countries avoid raising tariffs in a crisis.
want / decide / hope / plan / refuse / manage / afford / agree + to V1
The company decided to expand abroad.
Kompaniya chet elga kengayishga qaror qildi.
stop / remember / forget / try / regret + V-ing / to V1
They stopped trading with that firm. / They stopped to trade at the border.
Ular o'sha firma bilan savdoni to'xtatdi. / Ular chegarada savdo qilish uchun to'xtadi.

notes: Gerund ega — og'zaki va yozma; "To V1" ega — faqat rasmiy/she'riy; imtihonda "It is … to V1" xavfsiz.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Living with parents vs living alone
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda: Part 1 — 2 savol; Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing. Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ gerund yoki infinitiv ega (Living with parents is… / It is hard to… / To live alone means…).
items: Part 1: Who do you live with?
Part 1: What housework do you do at home?
Part 3: Is it common for young people in Uzbekistan to live alone? Why or why not?
Part 3: What are the main advantages of living with your parents?
Part 3: What are the biggest challenges of living alone for the first time?
Part 3: Is it important for young people to learn to live independently?
Part 3: How is family life today different from your grandparents' time?
answers: I live with my parents, my younger brother and my grandmother. Living in a big family is noisy sometimes, but it is never boring at home.
I usually wash the dishes and take out the rubbish. On Sundays I help my mother clean the flat, and cleaning together is actually quite fun.

Well, I think it is not very common. In our culture, it is normal to stay with your parents until you get married. Also, renting a flat in Tashkent is expensive for a student. For example, my cousin studies at university, but he still lives with his parents in Chilonzor.

The main advantage is that living with parents saves a lot of money, because you don't pay rent or bills. Another benefit is support. For example, during my exams, having my mother at home made life much easier, because she cooked for me and I could just study.

I'd say the biggest challenge is money. Paying rent and bills every month is not easy for a young person. It is also hard to do all the housework alone. For example, my friend from Namangan moved to Tashkent and spent his whole monthly budget in two weeks.

Yes, I think it is very important to learn this. Managing a budget alone is a useful skill for life. For example, my sister studied in Samarkand for a year and came back much more responsible. On the other hand, parents can teach this skill at home too.

Family life has changed a lot. In my grandparents' time, having three generations in one house was completely normal. Today, many young couples prefer to rent their own flat. For example, my parents lived with my grandparents for ten years, but my older brother moved out soon after his wedding. Having privacy matters more now.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Living with parents vs living alone
class_ex.instr: Some young people prefer to live with their parents until they get married, while others prefer to live alone. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of both and give your own opinion. Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval + kirish (35–45 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi (Writing 10)
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: ikki variant taqqoslash (ota-ona bilan yashash va yolg'iz yashash) — ikkala variantning afzallik va kamchiliklari + o'z fikringiz

2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: live with their parents, until they get married, live alone, advantages and disadvantages of both, your own opinion; mavzu so'zlari: rent, bills, cost of living, independent, privacy, support, housework, responsibility, income

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: ota-ona bilan yashash — afzalliklar va kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: yolg'iz yashash — afzalliklar va kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + o'z tanlovingiz va sababi)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of … is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, … also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: gerund yoki infinitiv ega 2+ marta (Living with parents saves… / Paying rent is… / It is not easy to… / To manage a budget is…)
answers: Namuna kirish (36 so'z): In Uzbekistan, most young people stay at home until their wedding, but some choose to rent their own flat. Each lifestyle has benefits and drawbacks, but I believe staying with parents makes more sense for students.

Namuna AD jadval: OTA-ONA BILAN — Afzalliklar: 1) pul tejaladi — ijara (rent) va kommunal to'lov (bills) yo'q 2) oila yordami (support) — masalan, ota o'g'lini kursga olib boradi, dars qoldirilmaydi; Kamchiliklar: 1) shaxsiy hayot (privacy) kam 2) mustaqil qaror qabul qilishni o'rganmaydi. YOLG'IZ — Afzalliklar: 1) mas'uliyat (responsibility) o'rganiladi 2) mustaqillik (independent) — byudjet, uy ishlari; Kamchiliklar: 1) ijara daromadning (income) katta qismini oladi 2) yolg'izlik — uyda yordam beradigan odam yo'q.

Namuna insho (189 so'z) — kirish: In Uzbekistan, most young people stay at home until their wedding, but some choose to rent their own flat. Each lifestyle has benefits and drawbacks, but I believe staying with parents makes more sense for students.

Namuna insho — body 1: On the one hand, living with parents saves money, because young people do not pay rent or bills. They also get family support. For example, my classmate's father drives him to his English course, so he never misses a lesson. However, it is not easy to have privacy in a busy home, and some never learn to make their own decisions.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, living alone teaches responsibility, because a person cooks and does the housework without help. Paying their own bills also makes young people independent. For example, my older brother rented a flat in Tashkent and learned to manage his budget. Nevertheless, rent takes a large part of his income, and he often feels lonely without his family.

Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, each way of living suits a different stage of life. Personally, I would stay with my parents while studying, because saving money for my education matters more to me now.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — living with parents saves, it is not easy to have, living alone teaches, Paying their own bills … makes, saving money … matters, staying with parents makes (6 marta); bog'lovchilar — On the one hand, because, For example, However, On the other hand, Nevertheless, In conclusion, so; mavzu so'zlari — rent, bills, support, privacy, responsibility, housework, independent, income (Global economy CORE: income).

Namuna insho o'quvchiga uy inshosi tekshirilgandan keyin ko'rsatiladi.

reading.title: Jeff Bezos — selling everything to everyone
text: Jeff Bezos was born in 1964 in New Mexico. Working on his grandfather's ranch in summer taught him to repair machines with his hands. Studying computer science at Princeton taught him to think like an engineer. In 1994, working at an investment company in New York, he read that the internet was growing 2,300% a year. Leaving his job to sell books online seemed crazy to many people, but his parents invested about 250,000 dollars in the idea.

Choosing the name Amazon was deliberate: he wanted the biggest river for the biggest shop. Starting in a garage near Seattle, the company sold its first book in 1995. To make a profit was not the goal; to grow was. For years Amazon lost money, and investors kept asking when it would stop. Bezos refused to change. In his view, it was better to think in decades than in quarters.

His strategy was simple. Keeping prices low brought customers; having more customers attracted more sellers; having more sellers lowered prices again. Building warehouses near big cities made next-day delivery possible. Then, in 2006, Amazon started renting its computers to other companies. Today these cloud services bring Amazon a large part of its profit.

Bezos stepped down as CEO in 2021. In 2000 he also founded the space company Blue Origin, which plans to build a business station in orbit. Critics say that paying warehouse workers more would be a better way to spend the money. Bezos often talks about his favourite rule, 'Day One': a company should always act as if it has just started, because being finished is the beginning of the end.

tasks.title: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: Do the statements agree with the information in the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
items: Bezos learned about the fast growth of the internet while he was a student at Princeton.
Amazon started in a garage.
Amazon made a profit in its first year.
Bezos chose the name Amazon after a trip to South America.
Amazon started renting its computers to other companies in 2006.
Bezos's parents worked for Amazon in its first years.
tasks.note: NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q; FALSE — matn teskarisini aytadi.

tasks.title: Matching information
tasks.instr: Which paragraph (1–4) contains the following information? You may use any number more than once.
items: the reason for the company's name
a criticism of Bezos
how low prices led to more sellers
the place where Bezos learned practical skills
how investors reacted to years of losses

tasks.title: ZAXIRA: Gerund/infinitiv egalarni toping
tasks.instr: Yakka: matndan 8 ta ega (gerund / infinitiv / It … to) toping.
items: gerund 1
gerund 2
gerund 3
gerund 4
infinitive 1
It … to
gerund 5
gerund 6
answers: Leaving his job to sell books online
To make a profit (was not the goal) / to grow (was)
it was better to think in decades (It … to)
Keeping prices low / having more customers / having more sellers
Building warehouses near big cities (yana: paying warehouse workers more, being finished)

kahoot.q: Exporting cotton ___ Uzbekistan's main income for many years.
kahoot.explain: Gerund ega (Exporting cotton) — birlik: was.

kahoot.q: ___ hard to compete with China.
kahoot.explain: Ingliz gapida ega shart: It is hard to compete... ("Is hard" — xato).

kahoot.q: Countries avoid ___ tariffs in a crisis.
kahoot.explain: avoid + V-ing: avoid raising tariffs.

kahoot.q: The company decided ___ abroad.
kahoot.explain: decide + to V1: decided to expand.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: He enjoys to invest in startups.
It is important to save money.
They refused to pay the tariff.
kahoot.explain: enjoy + V-ing: He enjoys investing in startups.

kahoot.q: Trading with neighbours ___ good for the economy.
kahoot.explain: Gerund ega birlik: Trading ... is good.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Ular o'sha firma bilan savdoni TO'XTATISHDI."
options: They stopped trading with that firm.
They stopped to trade with that firm.
They stopped to trading with that firm.
They were stopped to trade with that firm.
kahoot.explain: to'xtatish → stop + V-ing. stop to V1 = ...ish UCHUN to'xtash.

kahoot.q: Qaysi fe'ldan keyin FAQAT gerund (V-ing) keladi?
kahoot.explain: consider + V-ing. want/decide/hope + to V1.

kahoot.q: Qaysi fe'ldan keyin FAQAT infinitiv (to V1) keladi?
kahoot.explain: afford + to V1. enjoy/avoid/mind + V-ing.

kahoot.q: We can't afford ___ more debt.
kahoot.explain: afford + to V1: can't afford to take on more debt.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: It is difficult to find a job in a recession.
Is difficult to find a job in a recession.
It is difficult find a job in a recession.
It difficult is to find a job in a recession.
kahoot.explain: It is + sifat + to V1: It is difficult to find a job.

kahoot.q: To save money ___ important for students.
kahoot.explain: Infinitiv ega ham birlik: To save ... is. (Tabiiyroq: It is important to save money.)

kahoot.q: A tax on goods coming into a country is a ___.
kahoot.explain: tariff — import boji (chetdan kelgan tovarga soliq).

kahoot.q: Goods a country sells to other countries are its ___.
kahoot.explain: exports — eksport (chetga sotish); imports — import.

kahoot.q: When prices rise across the whole economy, it is ___.
kahoot.explain: inflation — inflyatsiya (narxlarning umumiy o'sishi).

kahoot.q: The total value of goods and services a country produces in a year is its ___.
kahoot.explain: GDP — yalpi ichki mahsulot (YaIM).

kahoot.q: "surplus" so'zining antonimi qaysi?
kahoot.explain: surplus (ortiqcha, profitsit) ↔ deficit (kamomad, taqchillik).

kahoot.q: A company that works in many countries is a ___ company.
kahoot.explain: multinational — ko'p davlatda ishlaydigan (transmilliy) kompaniya.

kahoot.q: Money the government gives farmers to help them is a ___.
kahoot.explain: subsidy — davlat yordami (subsidiya).

kahoot.q: "supply chain" ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: supply chain — xomashyodan tayyor mahsulot xaridorga yetguncha bo'lgan zanjir.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 3 — multiple choice. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
You will hear two students, Malika and Aziz, preparing a class presentation about global trade.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, kalit so'zlarni (what, who, how long) belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: MALIKA: Aziz, our presentation on global trade is on Friday. Let's check the slides.
AZIZ: OK. Slide one is about what Uzbekistan exports. I wrote that exporting cotton is our main income.
MALIKA: That's old information. Exporting raw cotton is much less important now — selling gold and textiles brings in more money. [Q1]
AZIZ: Right, so I'll change slide one. What about slide two, on imports? Shall we add a photo?
MALIKA: No photo. But it is important to compare imports and exports on one chart. Then people can see the difference quickly. [Q2]
AZIZ: Good idea. And the slide on tariffs has a photo of the border and a lot of text.
MALIKA: Let's keep the photo but cut the text. Reading long text on a slide is boring for the audience. [Q3]
AZIZ: Agreed. Now, who talks about foreign investment — you or me?
MALIKA: I'll do it… no, wait, you did more research on international trade and investment. You take it. [Q4]
AZIZ: Fine. And at the end, let's say that buying local products helps the economy, and ask the class: 'Do you check where your clothes are made?'
MALIKA: Nice. How long do we have? Ten minutes?
AZIZ: The teacher said fifteen — sorry, I mean twelve minutes, with questions. [Q5] To finish on time, we should practise tonight.

intro: KAUZATIV — ishni boshqa odam qiladi, men so'rayman yoki to'layman: "I have my room cleaned."
Qolip: HAVE (zamonda) + OB'EKT + V3. Zamon have da: had / will have / is having / has had / had had.
GET + ob'ekt + V3 — og'zaki: "I got the tractor fixed."
Odam bilan: have + odam + V1 ("I had the mechanic fix it"); get + odam + to V1 ("I got my brother to help").
Salbiy voqea: "He had his phone stolen."
formulas: Every day I have my room cleaned.
She will have the report written.
She is having the car repaired. / We were having the house painted.
U mashinasini ta'mirlatyapti. / Biz uyni bo'yatayotgan edik.
S + have/has had (had had) + ob'ekt + V3
I have had the emails sent. / He had had the roof repaired by 2020.
Men emaillarni jo'nattirdim. / U 2020-gacha tomni ta'mirlatgan edi.
get + ob'ekt + V3; have + odam + V1; get + odam + to V1
I got the soil tested. / I had the farmer plant trees. / I got him to help.
Tuproqni tekshirtirdim. / Fermerga daraxt ektirdim. / Uni yordam berishga ko'ndirdim.
presentation: Do you have your soil tested every year?
Yes, we have it tested every spring.
Did the farmer have the tractor repaired?
Yes, he had it repaired last week.
Is she having the greenhouse built?
Yes, she's having it built by a local company.
Have you had the compost delivered?
Yes, I've had two tons delivered.
Had the king had the first fields certified by 1990?
Yes, by 1990 he had had the first fields certified organic.
Who did you have plant the trees?
I had my cousins plant them.
notes: V3 doim: "have it repaired" (repair / repairing — xato).
Zamon faqat have da; "had had" — to'g'ri: "He had had the roof repaired by 2020." (Past Perfect kauzativ).
Kauzativ savol: "Did you have it fixed?" / "Are you having it built?"
CCQ: I had my hair cut. — Did I cut it myself? (No) Who did? (a hairdresser)
CCQ: I had my car repaired. / I had repaired my car. — Who repaired the car in each sentence? (a mechanic / I)
CCQ: I got my brother to help me. — Did my brother help? (Yes) Did I ask him? (Yes)
mistakes: I had repaired my car. (boshqa odam)
She is having the house paint.
She is having the house painted.
We will have build a greenhouse.
We will have a greenhouse built.
Ob'ekt have va V3 orasida; V3.
I got him to help me.

reading.title: King Charles III — the prince who had his farm made organic
text: Charles became king in 2022, at the age of 73. During the long years before that, he had time for his real passion: farming. In 1980 Highgrove, an old house with a large estate in the west of England, became his country home, and in 1985 he made a decision that many farmers laughed at: he decided to have the farm converted to organic farming.

At that time very few farmers worked without chemicals. Converting a farm is a slow process. First, the farmer has all chemical pesticides and fertilizers stopped. Next, crop rotation is introduced, so that the soil can rest and become fertile again. Then hedgerows are planted to give homes to birds and insects that eat pests. Finally, inspectors test the soil, and if it is clean, the farmer can have the fields certified organic.

At Highgrove, Charles had kilometres of hedgerows planted, had rare breeds of sheep and cattle brought back and had beehives placed in the orchards. Journalists mocked him when he said that he talked to his plants. By 1990 he had had the first fields certified organic.

In 1990 he also had a brand created, Duchy Originals. One of its first products was a biscuit made with organic oats. The profit from the brand has been given to charity — millions of pounds over the years. Today many supermarkets have whole shelves filled with organic food.
The king is known for gardening at Highgrove himself, though he has the heavy work done by others. Many people who once laughed at him later agreed that he was ahead of his time.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 1 — form completion. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear a phone call between a teacher and the manager of a farm about a school visit.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): formani o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (ism, sana, raqam, ot) belgilang.

transcript: HELEN: Green Valley Farm, Helen speaking.
TEACHER: Hello. I'd like to book a visit to your farm for my class.
HELEN: Of course. Which school are you from?
TEACHER: Riverside School. That's R-I-V-E-R-S-I-D-E. [Q1]
HELEN: And when would you like to come?
TEACHER: On Wednesday the 14th of October — sorry, I mean Friday the 16th. [Q2]
HELEN: Fine. How many students?
TEACHER: There are thirty-two in the class, but four have a competition that day, so twenty-eight. [Q3]
HELEN: On our organic farm they can visit the greenhouse, help with the apple harvest and see how we have the soil tested. We can also have lunch prepared for you — soup or sandwiches.
TEACHER: Soup is difficult to eat outside. Let's have sandwiches prepared, please. [Q4]
HELEN: Are you coming by train?
TEACHER: No, the station is too far, so the school is having a bus booked for us. [Q5]
HELEN: Good. Our paths were muddy last year, but we had them repaired last month.
TEACHER: And how much is it per student?
HELEN: It's twelve pounds — oh, wait, with lunch it's fifteen. [Q6] And you'll need to get the forms signed by the parents.
TEACHER: Of course. Thank you!

intro: Muloyimlik shkalasi (taxminiy): Any idea…? (do'st) < Could you tell me…? < I was wondering if you could… / Would you mind + V-ing…? (taxminan teng) < I'd be grateful if you could… (eng rasmiy: xat, ofis).
"Do you happen to know…?" — "tasodifan bilmaysizmi?"; "Any idea…?" — og'zaki.
formulas: Can you tell me what time the train leaves?
Could you tell me where the post office is?
Intro + WH/if + ega + has V3 / was V3
Do you know when the novel was written?
I was wondering if I could borrow this book.
Would you mind telling me + WH + ega + fe'l
Would you mind telling me who wrote this poem?
Bu she'rni kim yozganini aytsangiz, malol kelmaydimi?
I'd be grateful if you could tell me + WH + ega + fe'l
I'd be grateful if you could tell me how the story ends.
Hikoya qanday tugashini aytsangiz, minnatdor bo'lardim.
presentation: Could you tell me who wrote "O'tkan kunlar"?
Abdulla Qodiriy wrote it. It's often called the first Uzbek novel.
Do you know when it was published?
It came out as a book in the 1920s.
I was wondering if you could recommend a good novel.
I'd recommend "Mehrobdan chayon".
Would you mind telling me what genre it is?
It's historical fiction with a love story.
Do you happen to know whether the library has it?
Yes, I think it's on the second floor.
notes: Bilvosita savol ichida "?" faqat asosiy gap savol bo'lsa: "Could you tell me…?" — ha; "I was wondering if…" — nuqta.
Would you mind + V-ing (telling, explaining); "Would you mind if I borrowed…" — Past Simple (muloyim).
IELTS Speaking: javobda ham ishlating — "I'm not sure what the title is, but…"
CCQ: Could you tell me where the library is? — Is the word order like a question? (No — like a statement: the library is) Why the question mark? ('Could you tell me' is a question)
CCQ: I wonder whether he will come. — Do I know? (No) Is it a direct question? (No — so no question mark)
CCQ: Would you mind telling me who wrote it? — Is it polite? (Yes) mind + to V or V-ing? (V-ing)
CCQ: I was wondering if I could borrow this book. — Is it about the past? (No — it's a polite request now)
mistakes: Could you tell me who did write this?
Could you tell me who wrote this?
Do you know when was it published?
Do you know when it was published?
Would you mind to tell me…?
I was wondering can I borrow it.
I was wondering if I could borrow it.
I'd be grateful if you tell me.
I'd be grateful if you could tell me.

class_ex.title: FINAL-S: Part 1 + Part 2 — Books (ustoz baholaydi, S-B1)
class_ex.instr: Ustoz navbatdagi 4 o'quvchini baholaydi (final-S): Part 1 — 4 savol; Part 2 — 1 daq tayyorgarlik (oldingi o'quvchi gapirayotganda), 1–2 daq gapiradi. Javobda 1+ bilvosita ibora (I'm not sure whether…, I don't know why…).
items: Part 1: Could you tell me what kind of books you like?
Part 1: Do you know when you last read a book?
Part 1: Do you prefer paper books or e-books?
Part 1: Who chooses books for you?
Part 2 card: Describe a book you enjoyed reading. You should say: what it was about / when you read it / who wrote it — and explain why you enjoyed it.
answers: I mostly like fiction, especially detective stories. Short stories are good too because they are quick to finish.
I'm not sure exactly when, but I think it was last month. It was a novel for school.
Paper books, because my eyes get tired on a screen. But e-books are useful when I travel.
Usually I choose them myself. Sometimes my literature teacher recommends an author.

I'd like to talk about "O'tkan kunlar" by Abdulla Qodiriy. I read it last year for my literature class. It is a historical novel and a love story about Otabek and Kumush, set in the nineteenth century. At first I wasn't sure whether I would like it, because the language is quite old. But the plot was so exciting that I couldn't stop reading, and I often wondered what the characters would do next. I enjoyed it because it showed me how people lived in the past. I still don't know why the ending is so sad, but that is why I remember it.
class_ex.note: ICQ: How long do you prepare? (1 minute) — Do you write full sentences? (No, key words) — How long do you speak? (1–2 minutes). CCQ: I'm not sure whether I liked the ending. — Do I know? (No) Is it a question? (No). Kuchsizlar uchun gap boshlanmalari: I'd like to talk about… / I'm not sure whether… / I enjoyed it because… Baholash — S-B1 (pastdagi jadval), jurnalda final-S.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Being famous: benefits and challenges
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda (FINAL-S baholanayotgan paytda): Part 3 — A so'raydi, B javob beradi, 3-savoldan keyin almashing (Part 1 — FINAL-S mashqida). Har javob 3–4 gap: javob → sabab → misol. Har javobda 1+ bilvosita ibora (I'm not sure whether… / I wonder why… / It's hard to say how… / Nobody knows how long…).
items: Part 3: Why do so many teenagers dream of becoming famous?
Part 3: What are the main benefits of being famous?
Part 3: What problems do famous people have with their private life?
Part 3: Should famous people be role models for young people?
Part 3: Could you tell me how social media has changed the way people become famous?
answers: Well, I think it's mainly because of social media. Teenagers see bloggers with millions of fans and expensive cars, and they want the same life. For example, half of my classmates want to be YouTubers. I'm not sure whether they really understand how hard that job is, though.

The main advantage is that famous people usually have a good income. They also have a strong voice, so they can help others. For example, some Uzbek singers give concerts to collect money for sick children. I can understand why people want that kind of influence.

I'd say the biggest problem is privacy. Photographers and fans follow them everywhere, so they can't even walk around the bazaar or the park quietly. For example, a famous footballer once said that he couldn't take his kids to school. I wonder how they stay calm under so much pressure.

Yes, I think they should, because teenagers copy their favourite stars. If a singer says that education is important, fans listen. On the other hand, celebrities are normal people, and they make mistakes too. It's hard to say how many young people really follow good examples, but stars should try.

Well, now anyone with a phone can become famous. In the past you needed television or a big film studio. For example, a boy from Namangan became popular in just a few months with funny cooking videos. However, nobody knows how long this kind of fame will last.
class_ex.note: ICQ: Necha gapda javob berasiz? (3–4) — Misol kerakmi? (Ha). Gap boshlanmalari: Well, I think… / The main advantage is that… / On the other hand, … / For example, … / So overall, … Baholash — S-B1-P3 (pastdagi jadval). CCQ: "I wonder how they stay calm." — Do I know the answer? (No) Is it a question? (No — so no question mark) · Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 23-qator ("Being famous: benefits and challenges"); savollar va namunalar — Jony Academy, original.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Being famous: benefits and challenges
class_ex.instr: Many young people today dream of becoming famous. What are the benefits and challenges of being famous? Write 150–200 words. — Sinfda: AD jadval + kirish (35–45 so'z); uyda to'liq insho, 4 xatboshi (Writing 11)
items: 1-qadam — savol turi: advantages/disadvantages (benefits and challenges) — mashhurlikning afzalliklari va qiyinchiliklari; savol fikr so'ramaydi, xulosada qisqa fikr bo'lishi mumkin
2-qadam — kalit so'zlar: young people, dream of becoming famous, benefits, challenges; mavzu so'zlari: celebrity, fame, fans, privacy, pressure, role model, income, criticism

3-qadam — reja: Kirish (savol o'z so'zlaringiz bilan + reja) → Body 1: afzalliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Body 2: kamchiliklar (topic sentence + 2 g'oya + misol) → Xulosa (qisqa xulosa + fikr, agar savol so'rasa)
4-qadam — foydali iboralar: One major advantage of … is that… / Another benefit is… / On the other hand, … also has some drawbacks. / For example, … / In conclusion, …
5-qadam — dars grammatikasi: embedded clause (bilvosita savol gap ichida, so'z tartibi gapdek) 2+ marta: It is easy to see why… / Many people wonder how… / Nobody knows how long fame will last.
answers: Namuna kirish (40 so'z): Today many teenagers want to become celebrities, and it is easy to see why fame looks so attractive. However, life in the spotlight is not always easy. This essay will look at the main benefits and challenges of being famous.

Namuna AD jadval: Afzalliklar — 1) yuqori daromad (income): qo'shiqchi, aktyor, bloger oddiy ishchidan ko'p topadi, oilasini ta'minlaydi; 2) ta'sir (role model): mashhur o'zbek yozuvchisi kitob o'qishga chaqirsa, yoshlar romanlarini sotib oladi; Kamchiliklar — 1) shaxsiy hayot yo'q (privacy): muxlislar va jurnalistlar hamma joyda; 2) bosim va tanqid (pressure, criticism): ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda har bir rasmga baho beriladi.

Namuna insho (183 so'z) — kirish: Today many teenagers want to become celebrities, and it is easy to see why fame looks so attractive. However, life in the spotlight is not always easy. This essay will look at the main benefits and challenges of being famous.

Namuna insho — body 1: One major advantage of being famous is a high income. Popular singers, actors and bloggers earn much more than ordinary workers, so they can support their families. Another benefit is influence, because a famous person can be a good role model. For example, when a well-known Uzbek writer talks about reading, many young people start buying his novels.

Namuna insho — body 2: On the other hand, fame also has some serious drawbacks. The biggest one is the lack of privacy, because fans and journalists follow celebrities everywhere. In addition, famous people face constant pressure and criticism on social media. Many people wonder how stars can stay calm when thousands of strangers judge every photo they post.

Namuna insho — xulosa: In conclusion, fame brings money and influence, but it also takes away privacy and peace. Nobody knows how long fame will last, so young people should build a real career first.

Namunada: dars grammatikasi — it is easy to see why fame looks…, Many people wonder how stars can stay calm…, Nobody knows how long fame will last (3 marta, so'z tartibi gapdek); bog'lovchilar — However, One major advantage, so, Another benefit, because, For example, On the other hand, In addition, In conclusion, but; mavzu so'zlari — celebrities, fame, income, role model, fans, journalists, privacy, pressure, criticism; Literature CORE — writer, novels.
class_ex.note: Manba: rahbar rejasi — IELTS 3.0 xlsx, 23-qator ("Being famous: benefits and challenges"); savol va namuna — Jony Academy, original. Baholash: W-B1-AD (pastdagi jadval). PEER-AD (juftlik, Ha/Yo'q): 1) savol o'z so'zlari bilan? 2) afzallik va kamchilik alohida xatboshida? 3) har tomonda 2 g'oya + misol? 4) 4+ bog'lovchi? 5) dars grammatikasi 2+? 6) 150+ so'z (sinfda kirish 35–45)? Namuna insho o'quvchiga uy inshosi tekshirilgandan keyin ko'rsatiladi.

answers: I'd like to talk about "O'tkan kunlar" by Abdulla Qodiriy. I read it last year for my literature class. It is a historical novel and a love story about Otabek and Kumush, set in the nineteenth century. At first I wasn't sure whether I would like it, because the language is quite old. reading.title: Abdulla Qodiriy — do you know why his novel matters?
text: If you ask Uzbek students who wrote the first Uzbek novel, most of them will name Abdulla Qodiriy at once. He was born in 1894 in Tashkent, in a poor family; his father was a gardener. Do you know how he learned to write? He studied at school and in a madrasa, but he also taught himself a lot by reading newspapers. As a young man he was already publishing stories, and later he wrote humorous articles under the pen name Julqunboy.

In the early 1920s the first chapters of "O'tkan kunlar" (Bygone Days) appeared in a magazine, and later the whole novel came out as a book. Could you tell me why it was so important? Because Uzbek literature had poetry, tales and epics, but no modern novel — no long story with real characters, a plot and a setting in a real city. The love story of Otabek and Kumush, set in Tashkent and Margilan in the nineteenth century, became a book that everyone wanted to read. His second novel, "Mehrobdan chayon" (Scorpion from the Altar), followed a few years later.

Qodiriy was also a satirist: his humorous articles laughed at bad officials and old-fashioned habits, and that made him enemies. In the 1920s he was arrested for the first time; in 1937, during the great repression, he was arrested again, and in 1938 he was shot. Many readers still wonder how he could write so honestly in such hard times. For many years his books were banned.

He was rehabilitated in the 1950s, and today "O'tkan kunlar" is studied in schools across Uzbekistan, has been made into a film and has been translated into English. Would you mind reading it before you finish IELTS 3.0?

kahoot.q: Do you know when the novel ___?
kahoot.explain: Bilvosita savolda gap tartibi: when + ega + was + V3 (the novel was written).

kahoot.q: Could you tell me who ___ this poem?
kahoot.explain: who ega → did ishlatilmaydi: who wrote this poem.

kahoot.q: Would you mind ___ me where the library is?
kahoot.explain: Would you mind + V-ing: Would you mind telling me...?

kahoot.q: I was wondering ___ I could borrow this book.
kahoot.explain: Ha/yo'q savol → if/whether + ega + could: I was wondering if I could...

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: Do you know when was it published?
Could you tell me where the post office is?
I'd be grateful if you could tell me how it ends.
Do you happen to know who the author is?
kahoot.explain: To'g'risi: Do you know when it was published? (gapdek tartib)

kahoot.q: Can you tell me what time the train ___?
kahoot.explain: does yo'qoladi, fe'lga -s qo'shiladi: what time the train leaves.

kahoot.q: "Has she finished the book?" — bilvosita shakli qaysi?
options: Could you tell me whether she has finished the book?
Could you tell me whether has she finished the book?
Could you tell me whether she finished has the book?
Could you tell me that she has finished the book?
kahoot.explain: whether/if + ega + has + V3; that — ha/yo'q savolda ishlatilmaydi.

kahoot.q: Could you tell me where the post office ___?
kahoot.explain: where + ega + to be: where the post office is.

kahoot.q: Bilvosita savolda so'z tartibi qanday?
kahoot.explain: Gapdek: ega + fe'l (where she lives), do/does/did yo'q.

kahoot.q: Eng muloyim (rasmiy) so'rovni tanlang.
options: I'd be grateful if you could tell me...
kahoot.explain: I'd be grateful if you could… — eng rasmiy; Tell me… — buyruq.

kahoot.q: I'd be grateful if you ___ tell me how the story ends.
kahoot.explain: I'd be grateful if you could tell me... — muloyim so'rov qolipi.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Bu kitobni kim yozganini bilasizmi?"
options: Do you know who wrote this book?
Do you know who did write this book?
Do you know who did he write this book?
Do you know who this book wrote?
kahoot.explain: who ega → did yo'q, fe'l V2: who wrote this book.

kahoot.q: The main character of a story is the ___.
kahoot.explain: protagonist — bosh qahramon. antagonist — unga qarshi turgan qahramon.

kahoot.q: A short story with animals that teaches a moral lesson is a ___.
kahoot.explain: fable — masal: hayvonlar, oxirida saboq.

kahoot.q: A book about a person's life written by that same person is ___.
kahoot.explain: autobiography — o'zi yozadi; biography — boshqa odam yozadi.

kahoot.q: Stories that are imagined by the writer, not true, are ___.
kahoot.explain: fiction — to'qima; non-fiction — haqiqiy voqealar.

kahoot.q: A person who writes plays for the theatre is a ___.
kahoot.explain: playwright — dramaturg (pyesa yozuvchi).

kahoot.q: The ___ of a story is the time and place where it happens.
kahoot.explain: setting — voqea joyi va vaqti. plot — syujet.

kahoot.q: A story about a terrible future society is a ___.
kahoot.explain: dystopia — qo'rqinchli kelajak jamiyati; utopia — ideal jamiyat.

kahoot.q: "metaphor" nima?
options: bir narsani boshqa narsa deb ta'riflash (Time is money)
kahoot.explain: metaphor — metafora: "Time is money".

intro: IELTS Listening Part 1 — form completion. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
You will hear a conversation between a student and a librarian about joining a library.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): savollarni o'qing, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (raqam, ism, vaqt, ot) belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: LIBRARIAN: Good afternoon. How can I help you?
STUDENT: Hi. I'd like to join the library. Could you tell me what I need to do?
LIBRARIAN: Of course. I just need to fill in this form. What's your name?
STUDENT: Dilnoza Karimova. That's K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A. [Q1]
LIBRARIAN: Thank you. And what do you like reading?
STUDENT: Mostly fiction — novels and short stories. Some poetry too. Do you know what time the library closes?
LIBRARIAN: On weekdays we're open from nine until eight — sorry, until seven. The evening hours changed last month. [Q2]
STUDENT: OK. I was wondering how many books I can borrow.
LIBRARIAN: Students can take five books at a time. [Q3] Teachers can take ten.
STUDENT: And could you tell me how long I can keep them?
LIBRARIAN: For two weeks. Some people think it's three, but that was the old rule. [Q4]
STUDENT: Would you mind telling me what happens if I return a book late?
LIBRARIAN: There's a late fee. It used to be three hundred so'm a day, but now it's five hundred so'm a day for each book. [Q5]
STUDENT: One more thing. I was wondering if you have e-books.
LIBRARIAN: Yes, thousands — literature, history, science. Download our app. It's called ReadMore, R-E-A-D-M-O-R-E, one word. [Q6]
STUDENT: Great, thank you.
LIBRARIAN: You're welcome. Here's your card.

10 daq: formulas 1–5, presentation 1–5; qoida: bir martalik o'tgan ish qisqarmaydi (the drama which won ✓ / winning ✗); having / being + V3 — kuchlilarga. CCQ — grammar.notes. 5 daq — 1-majburiy mashq 'V-ing yoki V3' (yakka).
Lug'at: Film genres — CORE 10 ta asosiy so'z

Doskaga: genre, comedy, drama, thriller, horror, documentary, sequel / prequel, plot twist, cast, director — so'z → ma'no → participle bilan gap. So'ng 'Kino lug'ati' (juftlikda, 3 daq). Qolgan CORE va STRONG — flashcard, SUPER — ixtiyoriy.
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 4 qator)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. 1 daqiqada 3 marta — warm-up, 4 — normativ, 5 — a'lo.
Sinf mashqlari: Relative → participle (7 daq) + His-tuyg'u sifatlar (6 daq)

'Relative → participle' — juftlikda, 7 daq; 'His-tuyg'u sifatlar' — yakka, 6 daq; 5 daq — xatolar tahlili. ZAXIRA: Xatoni toping. Vaqt yetmasa: avval ZAXIRA (uyga), keyin 'His-tuyg'u sifatlar' 5–6-bandlari tashlanadi.

3 daq gist: What makes Nolan's films special? (unusual stories; real effects instead of CGI). 5 daq — T/F/NG; 4 daq — MCQ.

Ustoz navbatdagi 4 o'quvchini S-B1 bilan baholaydi (Part 1 + Part 2), jurnalga 'final-S'. Qolganlar juftlikda: Part 1 — 3 daq; Part 2: 1 daq tayyorgarlik, A va B 1.5 daqdan (sherik peer-b1 bilan); Part 3 — 2 daq; ustoz 1 daq feedback.

2 daq savol tahlili (opinion; cinemas, disappear, at home); 2 daq reja; 6 daq body paragraf (70–90 so'z, 2+ participle); 2 daq juftlikda peer-b1.

intro: PARTICIPLE 1 — V-ing, FAOL, ot o'zi bajaradi: "the running water" (suv oqadi), "the girl sitting by the window" (qiz o'tiradi).
PARTICIPLE 2 — V3, PASSIV, otga nisbatan bajarilgan: "the broken window" (oyna sindirilgan), "the house built in 1990" (uy qurilgan).
Sifat sifatida his-tuyg'u: boring (film) / bored (tomoshabin).
formulas: The girl sitting by the window is my sister.
Deraza yonida o'tirgan qiz — mening singlim.
The house built in 1990 is very old.
the film (which was) directed by… → the film directed by…
The film directed by Nolan won an Oscar.
Nolan suratga olgan film Oskar yutdi.
Having watched the trailer, I bought a ticket. / The film being shown now is a thriller.
Treylerni ko'rib, chipta oldim. / Hozir ko'rsatilayotgan film — triller.
presentation: Which film won the Oscar?
The film directed by Nolan — "Oppenheimer".
Who is the man standing by the camera?
He's the cinematographer working with Nolan.
What is a sequel?
A film made after a successful one, continuing the story.
Is the audience bored or excited?
The audience watching the last scene is completely silent — excited.
Which scenes were filmed without computer effects?
The scenes showing the plane crash were real.
notes: Otdan keyingi participle vergulsiz (defining); vergul bilan qo'shimcha: "The film, released in 2010, …"
His-tuyg'u sifatlar: interesting/interested, exciting/excited, terrifying/terrified — film tili.
Bir martalik o'tgan ish (won, broke) V-ing ga qisqarmaydi: the man who broke the window (the man breaking ✗). V-ing — hozirgi, davomli yoki doimiy holat: the girl sitting there.
CCQ: a boring film / a bored audience — Who feels? (the audience) What causes the feeling? (the film)
CCQ: the broken window — Did the window break something? (No) Did someone break it? (Yes)

reading.title: Christopher Nolan — the director making films inside dreams
text: Christopher Nolan was born in London in 1970. As a boy of seven, he started making short films with his father's camera, using his toys as actors. Studying English literature at university, he ran the film society. After university, he made his first feature film, "Following", at weekends — a black-and-white thriller shot for about 6,000 dollars with actors working for free.

His second film, "Memento" (2000), made him famous. It is a detective story told backwards: the viewer, knowing only what the hero remembers, is as confused as he is. Many critics praised it. Then came the Batman trilogy, released between 2005 and 2012, with the Joker played by Heath Ledger, an actor given an Oscar after his death.

"Inception" (2010) is a heist film set inside dreams, with a corridor rotating 360 degrees, built for real, and a spinning top at the end never explained. "Interstellar" (2014) is science fiction based on real physics: its black hole was designed with help from a famous physicist. Nolan prefers real effects to CGI: the plane crash shown in "Tenet" was filmed with a real plane, and the atomic explosion in "Oppenheimer" was made without computer graphics.

"Oppenheimer" (2023), a biopic telling the story of the man building the atomic bomb, earned almost a billion dollars and won seven Oscars, including Best Director — Nolan's first Oscar. He usually shoots on real film, not digital, and many of his films are made for giant IMAX screens. Audiences leaving his films often say that they need to watch them again.

intro: IELTS Listening Part 2 — Multiple choice. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
You will hear a radio presenter talking about the programme of a city film festival.
Tinglashdan oldin (2 daq): 5 savol va variantlarni o'qing, kalit so'zlarni (kun, joy, narx) belgilang.
1-tinglash — javob yozing; juftlikda solishtiring; 2-tinglash — tekshiring.
transcript: PRESENTER: Good morning, and welcome to City Radio. This week our city film festival opens, and here is a short guide to the programme.

PRESENTER: The festival starts on Friday — sorry, I mean on Saturday [Q1] — with a comedy directed by a young Uzbek director. It tells the story of a lonely old man and the boy living next door, who teaches him to use a smartphone. [Q2]
PRESENTER: Most films will be shown at the Navoi Cinema. Documentaries were shown at the city library last year, but the library is closed for repairs, so this year they are at the Youth Centre. [Q3]

PRESENTER: Now, tickets. Tickets sold online cost thirty thousand som, and tickets bought at the door cost forty thousand. Students showing their student card don't pay for the morning shows — they get a free ticket. [Q4]

PRESENTER: And on the last night we have an exciting thriller filmed in the mountains near Chimgan. Be ready for a real plot twist! There won't be a prize ceremony this year, but the cast will stay after the film to answer questions from the audience. [Q5]
PRESENTER: So, see you at the festival!

lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 3.0: Lesson 26 – Future in the past (4 qatorli jadval); Reading — O'zbekiston terma jamoasi, Jahon chempionati yo'li (Jony Academy matni, moslashtirilgan).
objectives: FINAL TEST (final): 1–25-darslar bo'yicha yozma qismni 45 daqiqada bajarish.
would + V1 va was/were going to bilan o'tgan nuqtadan qaralgan kelajakni aytish; reported speech'da will → would.
Listening (IELTS Part 2): nutqdan 6 bo'shliqli qaydlarni to'ldira olish.
Reading: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN savollariga matndan dalil topib javob bera olish.
Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): 'Looking back' mavzusida future in the past bilan 1–2 daqiqa gapira olish.
materials: Kitob: Student's book IELTS 3.0, Lesson 26 jadvali (qog'oz); formulalar grammar.formulas da ham bor — kitobsiz o'quvchi uchun proyektorga shuni chiqaring.
FINAL TEST (final) varaqlari, kalit va ball varag'i; Speaking kartochkalari — final varag'ida.
Kahoot: bu darsda o'ynalmaydi (FINAL TEST); L25 Kahooti — L25 uy vazifasida. Shu darsning Kahooti (kurs takrori) — ixtiyoriy, uyda yoki IELTS 4.0 1-darsida.
Listening: skript ustozda (yashirin transcript), ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi; audio fayl kerak emas.
Writing/Speaking rubrikasi — L01 dagi W-B1 va S-B1 jadvallari; juftlik varag'i peer-b1.
timeline: Warm-up: they said they would
Ustoz: "In 2022 fans said: 'We will play at a World Cup one day.' Now, in 2026, we can say: they said they WOULD play — and they did!" — kelajak o'tganga ko'chdi: will → would.
FINAL TEST (final) — 1–25-darslar

Instruksiya 2 · Listening 6 · Reading 10 · Grammar 7 · Vocabulary 5 · Writing 15 — yozma 48 ball + Speaking 12 (L24–L26) = 60; o'tish 42/60. Material, kalit, ball varag'i — final varag'i; Vocabulary'da L25 Film genres CORE so'zlari (2+).
YANGI MAVZU: Future in the past (would + V1, was going to)

8 daq: jadval (kitob yoki grammar.formulas) — asosiy: would + V1 va was/were going to; reported speech: will → would. would be V-ing / would have V3 — kuchlilar uchun, faqat tanib olish (1 daq). presentation 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 — juftlikda. CCQ — grammar.notes. 4 daq: 'will → would' (yakka).
Lug'at: kurs takrori — 10 so'z

10 so'z: comprehension, innovation, revenue, evidence, masterpiece, well-being, itinerary, underdog, resilience, algorithm. Ustoz o'zbekcha aytadi → sinf inglizcha → 1 gap would bilan ('I thought my comprehension would improve.'). Qolganlari — flashcard (uyda).
Kombinatsiya (kitob jadvali, 4 qator)

Kombinatsiya — o'quvchi kitob jadvalidagi formulalarni tartib bilan aytib, har biriga o'zi gap tuzadi va uni o'zbekchaga tarjima qiladi (formula → gap → tarjima); ustoz vaqtni o'lchaydi. Me'yor — normativ[2].
Sinf mashqlari: Would yoki was going to · Kurs xaritasi · Kurs lug'ati

Would yoki was going to — 4 daq (yakka; Challenge bandlari kuchlilarga); Kurs xaritasi — 5 daq (juftlikda); Kurs lug'ati — 3 daq (yakka); 1 daq kalit. ZAXIRA: Xatoni toping (3 daq). Vaqt yetmasa: avval 'Xatoni toping', keyin 'Kurs lug'ati' tashlanadi (uyga).
Listening (IELTS Part 2): note completion

2 daq tayyorgarlik; 1-tinglash; 1 daq juftlikda solishtirish; 2-tinglash; 3 daq javoblar — ustoz dalil gapni skriptdan o'qiydi; 2 daq target gaplarni tiklash (We were sure we would finish it in May. / I was going to join the robotics club.).
Reading: T/F/NG
2 daq gist: 'How long did fans wait for the World Cup?' (more than thirty years); 6 daq T/F/NG. ZAXIRA topshiriqlar — kuchlilarga yoki uyga.
Speaking — FINAL speaking baholash (4 o'quvchi) + Part 2

Ustoz oxirgi 4 o'quvchini final varag'i bo'yicha baholaydi (har biriga ~3 daq: Part 1 — 3 savol + Part 2 kartochka; S-B1, 12 ball). Qolganlar juftlikda 'Looking back': Part 1 — 3 daq; Part 2: 1 daq tayyorgarlik, A 1.5 daq, B 1.5 daq (sherik peer-b1 checklistini belgilaydi); Part 3 — 2 daq; oxirgi 1 daq — ustoz feedback (1 kuchli tomon + 1 tuzatish).
Kurs yakuni + uyga vazifa

Final natijasi 3 ish kuni ichida: har o'quvchiga fikr-kartochka (bo'limlar bo'yicha ball + 2 kuchli tomon + 2 ishlash kerak bo'lgan joy); tahlil — IELTS 4.0 1-darsida 8 daq. 42/60+ — IELTS 4.0; 30–41 — shartli o'tish; <30 — 2 haftalik takror va qayta final. Eng yaxshi 3 o'quvchi e'lon qilinadi (coin — normativ[1]). Uy vazifasi — homework.

intro: FUTURE IN THE PAST — o'tgan nuqtadan qaralganda kelajak: "In 2022 he said he would call" (o'shanda kelajak edi).
Asosiy (B1): would + V1 (Future Simple in the Past) va was/were going to (o'tgandagi reja). Kuchlilar uchun: would be + V-ing, would have + V3; would have been + V-ing — faqat tanib olish.
Qo'llanish: reported speech (said/thought/knew/promised + would), hikoya ("She didn't know that she would become champion"), was/were going to (reja).

Kurs xaritasi: 1 zamonlar → 2–5 used to/tags/pronouns/modal+V3 → 6–9 ravishlar va taqqoslash → 10 shart → 11–13 taqsimlovchi/moslik → 14, 25 sifatdosh → 15–19 ergash gaplar → 20–22 gerund/infinitiv → 23 kauzativ → 24 bilvosita savol → 26 future in the past.
formulas: He said he would call me.
Future Continuous in the Past (kuchlilar uchun)
He said he would be studying at 6 pm.
U soat 6 da o'qiyotgan bo'lishini aytdi.
Future Perfect in the Past (kuchlilar uchun)
She thought she would have finished the project by Monday.
U loyihani dushanbagacha tugatgan bo'lishini o'yladi.
Future Perfect Continuous in the Past (faqat tanib olish)
He said he would have been working for 10 hours by 8 pm.
U soat 8 gacha 10 soat ishlayotgan bo'lishini aytdi.
They were going to play football in the park, but it rained.
Ular parkda futbol o'ynamoqchi edi, lekin yomg'ir yog'di.
The coach promised that the team would qualify.
Murabbiy jamoa saralashdan o'tishini va'da qildi.
presentation: What did fans say in 2022?
They said the team would play at a World Cup one day.
When you were ten, what did you think you would be?
I thought I would be a pilot.
Did the players know the decisive match would end 0–0?
No, they didn't know it would end 0–0.
What were you going to do last weekend?
I was going to study, but my cousins visited us.
What was the plan for our class trip?
We were going to go to Samarkand, but it rained, so we went to a museum.
What did fans hope in 2010?
They hoped that one day Uzbekistan would reach the World Cup.
(Kuchlilar uchun) What did your friend say he would be doing at 8 pm?
He said he would be watching the match.
What did you think you would achieve in this course?
I thought I would learn 1,000 words; I have learned 1,500.
What did your teacher say you would be able to do?
She said I would be able to write a 150-word essay.
What are you going to do after IELTS 3.0?
I'm going to start IELTS 4.0 — and I said I would in September!
notes: will → would; is going to → was going to; can → could; may → might (reported speech).
Hikoya uslubi: "Nobody knew that this boy would one day play in the Premier League."
Final test (bu dars boshida, 45 daq): Listening 8 · Reading 8 · Grammar 10 · Vocabulary 10 · Writing 12 (Task 2, 120–150 so'z) = 48 + Speaking 12 (L24–L26) = 60; o'tish 42/60.
Kurs tugadi — lekin "It is always Day One".
CCQ: In 2024 I thought I would pass. — Was 'passing' in the future then? (Yes) Is it past now? (Yes)
CCQ: He said he would call. — Did he speak in the past? (Yes) Was the call in the future at that time? (Yes)
CCQ: We were going to go to Samarkand, but it rained. — Was it a plan? (Yes) Did we go? (No)
mistakes: He said he will call me. (o'tgan)
He said he would call me.
She thought she would finished by Monday.
She thought she would have finished by Monday.
They were going play football in the park.
They were going to play football in the park.
He said he would studying at 6.
He said he would be studying at 6.
I knew that I will pass.
I knew that I would pass.

how: CORE 20 — 1–10-darslardan (har darsdan 2 ta); STRONG 20 — 11–20-darslardan; SUPER 1–10 — 21–25-darslardan; SUPER 11–20 — reading'dagi yangi so'zlar (ixtiyoriy). Har so'zga future in the past bilan gap.
Uyda: 'Sentabrdagi men' inshosida kamida 5 ta kurs so'zini ishlating.

class_ex.title: FINAL TEST — IELTS 3.0 (1–25-darslar): ustoz uchun o'tkazish tartibi va ball jadvali
class_ex.instr: Test 26-dars boshida, Warm-up'dan keyin (timeline 2-qator), 45 daqiqa. Yozma qism 48 ball: Listening 8 + Reading 8 + Grammar 10 + Vocabulary 10 + Writing 12. Speaking 12 ball — yozma testdan TASHQARI, 24, 25 va 26-darslarning Speaking bosqichida. Umumiy jami 60 ball.
items: 1. Tayyorgarlik (24-darsgacha): o'quvchi varag'ini chop eting — o'quvchilar soni + 2 nusxa. O'quvchi varag'iga faqat quyidagilar kiradi: Listening savollari (1–8), Reading matni va savollari (1–8), Grammar (1–10), Vocabulary (1–10, so'zlar ro'yxati bilan), Writing savoli va 150 so'zlik chiziqli joy. Listening skripti, kalitlar, namuna javoblar, rubrikalar va Speaking kartochkalari FAQAT ustozda qoladi.

2. Speaking (yozma testdan tashqari): 24, 25 va 26-darslarning Speaking bosqichida har darsda 4 o'quvchi baholanadi (Part 1 — 3 savol + Part 2 — kartochka, 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik + 1–1.5 daqiqa gapirish; ketma-ket o'tkazilsa har o'quvchiga ~3 daqiqa, 4 kishiga 12 daqiqa — bosqich esa 10 daqiqa). Part 2 kartochkasini oldingi o'quvchi gapirayotgan paytda bering — tayyorgarlik parallel ketadi, shunda har o'quvchiga ~2.5 daqiqa ketadi va 4 kishi 10 daqiqaga sig'adi. 24-dars boshida ro'yxat tuzing: kim qaysi darsda. Qolgan o'quvchilar shu vaqtda juftlikda Part 1–2 ni mashq qiladi (peer-b1 varag'i bilan). Ball darhol S-B1 rubrikasi bo'yicha ball varag'iga yoziladi (jurnalda 'final-S'). 12 dan ortiq o'quvchi bo'lsa yoki kimdir dars qoldirsa — 26-darsning Speaking bosqichida (faqat parallel tayyorgarlik bilan vaqt qolsa, 1 kishigacha) yoki kurs yakunidan keyin, IELTS 4.0 ning 1-darsigacha alohida kelishilgan vaqtda baholanadi.

3. Test boshida (Instruksiya — 2 daqiqa): telefonlar yig'iladi, partalar alohida. Varaqlar yuzi pastga qarab tarqatiladi. Ovoz chiqarib ayting: 5 bo'lim, 48 ball; o'tish uchun yozma 48 + speaking 12 = 60 balldan kamida 42 ball kerak. Ism-familiya va sanani yozdiring.
4. Proyektorda FAQAT: joriy bo'lim nomi, uning ko'rsatmasi (instr) va taymer. Listening skripti, kalitlar va namuna javoblar proyektorga CHIQMAYDI.

5. Vaqt tartibi (jami 45 daqiqa): Instruksiya 2 → Listening 6 (birinchi bo'lib, butun sinf birga tinglaydi) → Reading 10 → Grammar 7 → Vocabulary 5 → Writing 15. Reading, Grammar va Vocabulary uchun bo'lim tugashidan 1 daqiqa oldin ogohlantiring; tez tugatgan o'quvchi keyingi bo'limga o'tishi mumkin, lekin Writing uchun kamida 15 daqiqa qolishi kerak.

6. Listeningni qanday o'qish: avval o'quvchilarga 30 soniya savollarni o'qish uchun bering. Skriptni 2 rolda (ovoz yoki joyni o'zgartirib) tabiiy tezlikda 2 marta o'qing; o'qishlar orasida 20 soniya pauza, oxirida 1 daqiqa javoblarni tekshirish uchun. Harflab aytilgan ism va raqamlarni aniq, lekin ta'kidlamasdan ayting. Hech bir gapni qo'shimcha takrorlamang.

7. Test vaqtida ustoz savol mazmunini tushuntirmaydi va so'z tarjima qilmaydi — faqat ko'rsatmani o'zbekcha qaytarishi mumkin. Ko'chirish aniqlansa — o'sha bo'lim 0 ball, sababi ball varag'iga yoziladi.

8. Tekshirish (kalit bo'yicha, har band 1 ball, yarim ball yo'q): Listening 1–5 — so'z chegarasi (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER) oshsa yoki imlo xato bo'lsa 0; katta-kichik harf farqi xato emas. Listening 6–8, Reading 1–8, Grammar 1–10, Vocabulary 1–5 — faqat to'g'ri harf yoki javob. TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN o'rniga T/F/NG yozilsa — qabul qilinadi; YES/NO — 0. Vocabulary 6–10 — so'z to'g'ri tanlangan va imlosi to'g'ri bo'lsa 1 ball.

9. Writing (12 ball): W-B1 rubrikasi — 4 mezon × 0–3. Avval so'zlarni sanang: 100–119 so'z — Task Response ko'pi bilan 2; 100 dan kam — ko'pi bilan 1; 20 dan kam yoki yodlangan tayyor matn — 0. Faqat bitta paragraf yozilgan bo'lsa — Coherence ko'pi bilan 1. Shubhali ishni ikkinchi ustoz ham baholaydi, o'rtacha butun songa yaxlitlanadi.

10. Natija: yozma qism 26-dars kunining o'zida tekshiriladi, speaking ballari qo'shiladi. 3 ish kuni ichida har o'quvchiga individual fikr-kartochka (bo'limlar bo'yicha ball + 2 kuchli tomon + 2 ishlash kerak bo'lgan joy) va ota-onaga natija yuboriladi. Umumiy xatolar tahlili — IELTS 4.0 ning 1-darsidagi takror bosqichida (8 daqiqa).
answers: Ball → natija → keyingi qadam (jami 60 = yozma 48 + speaking 12):
O'TDI: 42–60 ball (≥ 70%) → IELTS 4.0 ga o'tadi. Coin: 54–60 ball — 5 coin; 42–53 ball — 3 coin.

QAYTA ISHLASH: 30–41 ball (50–69%) → IELTS 4.0 ga SHARTLI o'tadi: 4.0 ning 1–3-darslarida qo'shimcha takror (zaif bo'limi bo'yicha uy vazifasi + dars oldidan 15 daqiqa) va 4.0 Progress test 1 da ≥ 70% sharti. Shart bajarilmasa — ota-ona bilan uchrashuv va individual reja.

O'TMADI: 0–29 ball (< 50%) → ota-onaga xabar (ustoz qo'ng'iroq qiladi); 2 haftalik takror (grammatika — 1–25-darslar formulalari, lug'at — 5 blok CORE, reading — T/F/NG va headings, listening — form completion, writing — 4 paragrafli reja), so'ng qayta final: zaxira Writing mavzusi, Grammar va Vocabulary bandlari boshqa tartibda va variantlar almashtirilgan holda.

Ko'nikma sharti (jami balldan qat'i nazar): Writing < 4/12 bo'lsa — zaxira mavzuda Writing qayta yoziladi (1 hafta ichida, 15 daqiqa); Speaking < 4/12 bo'lsa — boshqa kartochka bilan Speaking qayta topshiriladi. Qayta topshirilgan ball eskisining o'rniga yoziladi; qayta topshirilgan ko'nikma uchun coin berilmaydi.

Hisob misollari: (1) L 7, R 6, G 8, V 9, W 9, S 10 = 49 → O'TDI, 3 coin. (2) L 6, R 5, G 7, V 7, W 3, S 9 = 37 → QAYTA ISHLASH + Writing qayta yoziladi (3 < 4). (3) L 8, R 8, G 9, V 10, W 11, S 11 = 57 → O'TDI, 5 coin. (4) L 3, R 3, G 4, V 5, W 4, S 5 = 24 → O'TMADI: ota-onaga xabar, 2 haftalik takror, qayta final.

class_ex.title: Listening skripti (faqat ustozga, o'qib beriladi)
class_ex.type: Listening — ustoz o'qiydigan original skript (IELTS Part 1 uslubi, 2 rol, 2 marta)
class_ex.instr: Faqat ustoz uchun: proyektorga chiqarilmaydi, o'quvchi varag'iga kirmaydi. Skript ~245 so'z, bir o'qish ~1.5–2 daqiqa. 2 rolni ovoz yoki joy o'zgartirib o'qing; o'qishlar orasida 20 soniya pauza.
items: Roles: AGENT (travel agency) and DILNOZA (teacher). (Ikki rol: sayohat agentligi xodimi va ustoz Dilnoza.)
AGENT: Good morning, Silk Road Tours. How can I help you?
DILNOZA: Hello. I'd like to book a guided tour to Samarkand for my English class.
AGENT: Of course. Could you tell me your name, please?
DILNOZA: Dilnoza Karimova. That's K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A.
AGENT: Thank you. And how many people will be travelling?
DILNOZA: There are fourteen students and two teachers, so sixteen altogether.
AGENT: Sixteen. When would you like to go?
DILNOZA: We were thinking about the fifth of October, but the students have an exam that day. So the twelfth would be better.
AGENT: No problem. The tour lasts two days, so you'll need accommodation. We can offer a hotel in the city centre or a guest house near the Registan.
DILNOZA: The guest house, please. The students would enjoy staying with a local family.
AGENT: Good choice. For a group, the price is ninety-five dollars per person. That includes breakfast and the train tickets.
DILNOZA: Ninety-five. That's fine. Travel insurance is included, isn't it?
AGENT: No, it isn't, but you can buy it from us for five dollars each.
DILNOZA: I see. And what will we do on the first day?
AGENT: In the morning, our guide will take you to the Registan. After lunch, you'll visit Ulugh Beg's observatory. On the second day, there's a workshop where students make their own paper.
DILNOZA: That sounds great. When do we have to pay?
AGENT: We need a deposit of thirty per cent by the end of this month. You can pay the rest when you arrive.
DILNOZA: Perfect. Thank you very much.
class_ex.note: Distraktorlar: 5-oktabr (o'quvchilarda imtihon) → 12-oktabr; hotel in the city centre → guest house; insurance narxga kirmaydi, alohida $5; Registan — ertalab, observatoriya — tushdan keyin, qog'oz ustaxonasi — 2-kun; deposit — oy oxirigacha, qolgani kelganda.

class_ex.title: Reading — 1–4: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN (4 ball)
class_ex.type: Reading — original matn (B1, 5 paragraf) + T/F/NG (4 × 1 ball)
class_ex.instr: Read the text 'The Village That Chose the Sun'. Do the statements agree with the information in the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. (Matnni o'qing. TRUE — matnda shunday yozilgan; FALSE — matnga zid; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q.) Time for Reading (1–8): 10 minutes.
box: The Village That Chose the Sun

A. Ten years ago, Oqtepa was a small village where the electricity often stopped for several hours a day. It was far from the nearest town, and the roads were in bad condition. Families burned coal to heat their homes in winter, and the air was often dirty. Most young people left for the city because there was nowhere to work.

B. Everything changed in 2019, when two teachers at the village school started a science club. The students, who were only fourteen or fifteen, visited every house and measured how much electricity each family used. They found that many families were wasting energy because their lamps and fridges were very old. Their results surprised everyone.

C. Using the students' data, the village council asked a local company to build a small solar power plant on the hill behind the school. It took eight months to finish, and the students helped the engineers by explaining the project to their neighbours. Nobody was sure that it would work in winter, but it produced enough electricity even on cloudy days. Today the plant gives power to 300 homes, the school and the health centre.

D. The project has not been easy, however. The solar panels need to be cleaned every week because of the dust, and the batteries which store the energy are expensive. In 2023 a strong wind damaged part of the plant, and the village had to wait two months for new parts. Some older residents still say that the old way was simpler.

E. Nevertheless, life in Oqtepa is better now. Electricity bills are about forty per cent lower, and many families spend the money they save on their children's education. Several young people who had moved to the city have come back to work as technicians at the plant. The students who started the club are now at university, and one of them is studying energy efficiency.
items: 1. Before the project, people in Oqtepa used coal to keep their homes warm.
2. The science club was started by the village council.
3. The solar power plant does not produce electricity on cloudy days.
4. Some older residents refuse to pay for the new electricity.
why: A: "Families burned coal to heat their homes in winter" (used coal = burned coal; keep warm = heat).
B: klubni "two teachers at the village school" boshlagan; council faqat C da, zavod uchun.
C: "it produced enough electricity even on cloudy days" — zid.
D: keksalar "the old way was simpler" deydi, lekin to'lash haqida hech narsa yo'q.

class_ex.title: Grammar — 1–10 (10 ball)
class_ex.instr: Choose the correct answer, A, B, C or D. (To'g'ri javobni tanlang: A, B, C yoki D. Harfni aylana ichiga oling.) Time: 7 minutes.
items: 1. By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film ___. A) already starts B) has already started C) had already started D) was already start
2. Aziz got 98% in the exam. He ___ very hard. A) must have studied B) can't have studied C) needn't have studied D) should have studied
3. The box was ___ heavy that I couldn't lift it. A) too B) so C) enough D) very
4. If I had learned to swim as a child, I ___ afraid of water now. A) wouldn't have been B) won't be C) wouldn't be D) hadn't been
5. ___ of my two brothers likes football — they both prefer chess. A) Neither B) Both C) None D) All
6. The number of students who study online ___ growing every year. A) are B) have C) were D) is
7. That's the scientist ___ invention changed the way we store energy. A) who B) which C) whose D) where
8. Excuse me, I don't know ___. A) what time does the train leave B) what time the train leaves C) what time did the train leave D) what time leaves the train
9. We ___ our car repaired yesterday because the brakes weren't working. A) had B) have C) made D) did
10. The film ___ by Christopher Nolan won several awards. A) directing B) directed C) was directed D) directs
why: 1-dars (12 zamon): o'tmishdagi bir voqeadan (arrived) OLDIN tugagan ish → Past Perfect: had + V3.
5-dars (modal + have + V3): 98% — o'tmish haqida ishonchli taxmin → must have + V3. should have + V3 — tanqid yoki afsus (u o'qimagan degan ma'no), bu kontekstga to'g'ri kelmaydi.
6-dars (daraja ravishlari): so + sifat + that + gap; too dan keyin that emas, to V1 keladi.
10-dars (mixed conditional): If + Past Perfect (o'tmish), would + V1 (hozir: now).
11–12-darslar (distributive): 2 kishi haqida inkor → Neither of + ko'plik ot + birlik fe'l (likes).
13-dars (ega–kesim): The number of + ko'plik ot + BIRLIK fe'l (is).
17-dars (whose): egalik — scientist ning ixtirosi → whose + ot.
19-dars (to'ldiruvchi ergash gap) / 24-dars: ichki savolda so'z tartibi darak gapdek, do/does/did yo'q → what time the train leaves.
23-dars (causative): have + ob'ekt + V3, o'tgan zamonda had (yesterday).
25-dars (Participle 2): otdan keyin passiv ma'no → the film directed by… (= which was directed).

class_ex.title: Writing — IELTS Task 2 opinion essay (12 ball, W-B1)
class_ex.instr: Write 120–150 words. Write 4 paragraphs. Give your opinion, reasons and examples. (120–150 so'z, 4 paragraf yozing. Fikringizni, sabab va misollarni yozing.) Time: 15 minutes.
box: Some people think that learning English is more important than learning other subjects at school. To what extent do you agree?
Zaxira mavzu (faqat qayta topshirishda yoki qayta finalda): Some people believe that learning online with AI tools is better than learning in a classroom with a teacher. To what extent do you agree?
items: 1. Paragraph 1 — Introduction (2 sentences): paraphrase the question and give your opinion (I agree / I disagree / I partly agree). (Savolni o'z so'zingiz bilan qayta yozing va pozitsiyangizni ayting.)
2. Paragraph 2 — Body 1: first reason + example (because…, for example…). (1-sabab va aniq misol.)
3. Paragraph 3 — Body 2: second reason or the other side + example (However… / On the other hand…). (2-sabab yoki qarshi fikr va misol.)
4. Paragraph 4 — Conclusion (1–2 sentences): repeat your opinion in new words. (Xulosa: fikringizni boshqa so'zlar bilan takrorlang.)

5. Use at least 4 linking words (because, however, for example, in addition, on the other hand, in conclusion) and at least 3 words from our CORE lists. (Kamida 4 ta bog'lovchi va CORE ro'yxatlaridan kamida 3 ta so'z ishlating.)
answers: Namuna javob (partly agree, 137 so'z) — 1-paragraf: Nowadays, many people believe that English is the most important subject at school. I partly agree with this view, because English is very useful, but other subjects are necessary too.

2-paragraf: On the one hand, English opens many doors. Most research, online courses and international companies use English, so students who speak it well have more opportunities. For example, my cousin, who works for a tech startup in Tashkent, uses English every day with foreign clients.

3-paragraf: On the other hand, English is only a tool. Learning maths develops problem-solving and critical thinking, and science helps us understand the world. If my cousin had not studied maths at school, he would not be a programmer now.
4-paragraf: In conclusion, English is extremely important, but it should not replace other subjects. A good curriculum needs a balance of all of them.

Namunadagi kurs elementlari: relative clause (students who speak…, my cousin, who works… — 15-dars), gerund ega (Learning maths develops… — 22-dars), mixed conditional (If my cousin had not studied…, he would not be… now — 10-dars), bog'lovchilar (On the one hand / On the other hand / For example / In conclusion — 7-dars), CORE: research, curriculum, problem-solving, critical thinking (1-dars), tech startup (2-dars). W-B1 bo'yicha taxminiy baho: TR 3, CC 3, LR 3, GRA 3 = 12.

Tekshiruv tartibi: 1) so'z sonini sanang; 2) pozitsiya kirishda va xulosada bir xilmi; 3) har body paragrafda sabab + misol bormi; 4) bog'lovchilar va CORE so'zlarni belgilang; 5) W-B1 jadvali bo'yicha har mezonga 0–3 ball. Zaxira mavzu uchun ham shu reja va rubrika qo'llanadi.

class_ex.title: Speaking — Part 2 kartochkalari (6 ta; 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik + 1–1.5 daqiqa gapirish)
class_ex.type: Speaking — Part 2 (cue card); har o'quvchiga 1 kartochka
class_ex.instr: You will have 1 minute to prepare. You can make notes. Then speak for 1–1.5 minutes. (1 daqiqa tayyorlanasiz, qisqa yozuv qilishingiz mumkin. Keyin 1–1.5 daqiqa gapirasiz.) Ustoz kartochkalarni navbat bilan beradi; yonma-yon o'quvchilarga bir xil kartochka bermang.
items: 1. Describe a film you enjoyed watching. You should say: what the film was; what genre it was and who directed it or acted in it; what happened in the story — and explain why you enjoyed it.
2. Describe a trip you took to an interesting place. You should say: where you went; who you went with; what you saw and did there — and explain why the place was interesting.
3. Describe a piece of technology you use every day. You should say: what it is; when you started using it; what you use it for — and explain how your life would be different without it.
4. Describe a habit you would like to change. You should say: what the habit is; when it started; how it affects your studies or health — and explain what you will do to change it.
5. Describe a book or a story you remember well. You should say: what it was about; who wrote it; who the main character was — and explain why you remember it.
6. Describe a person you know who has a healthy lifestyle. You should say: who this person is; what he or she does every day; what he or she eats — and explain what you have learned from this person.
answers: Kartochka 1 (25-dars, Film genres): kutiladigan so'zlar — genre, thriller/comedy/science fiction, director, plot, plot twist, cast, scene; grammatika — Participle 1/2 (a film directed by…, the scene showing…), indirect/relative clauses. Yakuniy savol (ixtiyoriy): Would you watch it again?

Kartochka 2 (7–8-darslar, Travel/History): itinerary, accommodation, sightseeing, landmark, guided tour, souvenir, ancient, fortress; grammatika — Past Simple/Continuous, contrast (however, whereas), adverbs of place (nearby, everywhere).
Kartochka 3 (2, 14-darslar, Technology/AI): smart devices, user-friendly, tech-savvy, app, AI, chatbot; grammatika — used to / be used to, mixed conditional (If I didn't have it, I would…).

Kartochka 4 (13, 6-darslar, Personal development/Health): procrastination, routine, willpower, time management, priority, well-being; grammatika — gerund ega (Checking my phone takes…), adverbs of degree (too, so…that), infinitive (I want to…).

Kartochka 5 (24-dars, Literature): novel, short story, author, character/protagonist, plot, genre; grammatika — relative clauses (who/which/whose), indirect questions (I can't remember when it was written).

Kartochka 6 (6, 11-darslar, Health/Sport): fitness, balanced diet, nutrition, lifestyle, athlete, coach; grammatika — Present Simple + Present Perfect Continuous (She has been running for…), each/every, adverbs of degree. Hamma kartochkalar uchun baholash — S-B1 jadvali; 30 soniyadan kam gapirsa, ustoz bitta yordamchi savol beradi (What else can you say about…?), lekin Fluency 1 dan oshmaydi.
