class_ex.title: Speaking (IELTS Part 1–2–3): Looking back
class_ex.instr: Part 1 — juftlikda; Part 2 — 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik (kalit so'zlar), 1–2 daqiqa gapirish; Part 3 — muhokama. Kamida 3 ta would + V1 va 1 ta was/were going to.
items: Part 1: What did you think this course would be like?
Part 1: What was going to be your biggest problem?
Part 1: Which lesson did you enjoy most?
Part 1: What will you do in the summer?
Part 2 card: Describe a goal you had at the start of this course. You should say: what the goal was / what you thought would happen / what actually happened — and explain how you feel now.
Part 3: Why do people's plans often change?
Part 3: Is it important to set goals?
answers: I thought it would be very difficult. In fact, it was hard at times, but the lessons were interesting.
I thought grammar was going to be my biggest problem. But now listening is harder for me.
I enjoyed the lesson about film genres most. We talked about our favourite films and it was fun.
I'm going to rest for two weeks. Then I'll start IELTS 4.0 and read English books.

At the start of this course my goal was to write a good essay in English. In September I thought it would take one or two months. I was going to practise every weekend, and I believed I would write without mistakes by December. What actually happened was different. Writing took much more time, and my first essays were full of mistakes. However, my teacher said I would improve if I wrote every week, and she was right. Now I can write a clear 150-word essay with an introduction and a conclusion. I feel proud, because I didn't give up, and I know the next goal will be easier.
Because life is hard to predict. People think they will have time for everything, but new problems and chances appear.
Yes, I think so. A goal shows you where to go, and you can check your progress. But goals should be realistic.
class_ex.note: ICQ: How long do you prepare? (1 minute) — Do you write full sentences? (No, key words) — How long do you speak? (1–2 minutes). CCQ: 'I thought I would pass.' — Was I sure then? (Yes) Is the test in the past now? (Yes). Kuchsizlar uchun: 'My goal was…', 'In September I thought I would…', 'I was going to…, but…', 'Now I feel…'. Sherik peer-b1 varag'i bilan tekshiradi (L01).

homework.instr: 150 so'z: kurs boshida (sentabrda) nima deb o'ylagan edingiz va nima bo'ldi. Kamida 4 ta would + V1, 2 ta was/were going to va 5 ta kurs so'zi (~25 daq)

Namuna reja: 1) Sentabrda nimani kutgandim (I thought I would…) 2) Rejalarim (I was going to…, but…) 3) Nima bo'ldi va hozir nima his qilaman.
Namuna boshlanish: In September I thought English grammar would be too difficult for me. I was going to study only before tests, but my teacher said I would need to practise every day.

reading.title: Uzbekistan's road to the World Cup — they said they would, and they did
text: In 1992 Uzbekistan played its first official international match as an independent country. Fans hoped that one day the team would play at a World Cup. For more than thirty years it seemed that day would never come: in 2006 and 2014 the team lost in the play-offs, and some fans joked that Uzbekistan would always be "the best team that never qualifies".

The team that finally did it was young. Many people said this generation would change history: it included Abdukodir Khusanov, who would later play in the Premier League, Eldor Shomurodov, who had been playing in Europe for years, and players who had won the Asian U-20 championship in 2023. The team played without fear.

On 5 June 2025, in Abu Dhabi, Uzbekistan drew 0–0 with the UAE in the decisive match, and the dream came true: for the first time in history, Uzbekistan would be going to the World Cup. In Tashkent people celebrated in the streets all night, and many fans said they would remember that night for the rest of their lives.

In June 2026 the team played at the World Cup in North America for the first time. The players of 1992 could only hope that this day would come. Now every child in Uzbekistan knows the story: the players said they would qualify — and they did.
glossary: rest of one's life — umrining oxirigacha

transcript: DILNOZA: Good evening, everyone. I'm Dilnoza from class 9B, and tonight I want to tell you what our class thought would happen this year — and what really happened.

DILNOZA: In September we started a science project: a small weather station for the school roof. We were sure we would finish it in May. [Q1] Our teacher, Mr Karimov, said it would take a lot of patience, and he was absolutely right.
DILNOZA: I was going to join the robotics club [Q2], but the project needed me every Wednesday, so I joined the chess club instead — it meets only once a month.
DILNOZA: Nobody knew it would take so long. The hardest part was the software. We needed someone tech-savvy, and luckily a boy from class 10, Sardor, helped us. [Q3]
DILNOZA: We also had to brush up on our maths to understand the data. We thought we would need two sensors — in the end we used five. [Q4]
DILNOZA: The station finally started working on the 12th of June — sorry, the 21st. [Q5] Now it sends weather data to the school website every hour. [Q6]

DILNOZA: What did we learn? The evidence was clear: good plans change. My comprehension of English science texts improved too, because all the instructions were in English. However, the most important thing was teamwork. Thank you!

kahoot.q: In 2022 he said he ___ me the next day.
kahoot.explain: said (o'tgan) → will emas, would + V1: would call.

kahoot.q: He said he ___ at 6 pm that evening.
kahoot.explain: would be + V-ing: would be studying.

kahoot.q: She thought she ___ the project by Monday.
kahoot.explain: by Monday — muddatgacha tugagan → would have + V3.

kahoot.q: They ___ play football in the park, but it rained.
kahoot.explain: O'tgandagi reja → were going to + V1 (they → were).

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: I knew that I will pass the exam.
He said he would be working late.
We were going to travel, but it rained.
kahoot.explain: Asosiy gap o'tgan (knew) → would: I knew that I would pass.

kahoot.q: He said he ___ for 10 hours by 8 pm.
kahoot.sub: Future Perfect Continuous in the Past
kahoot.explain: by 8 pm + for 10 hours → would have been + V-ing.

kahoot.q: The student ___ phone rang had to leave the room.
kahoot.explain: Egalik (talabaning telefoni) → whose + ot.

kahoot.q: I had my laptop ___ yesterday.
kahoot.explain: have + ob'ekt + V3: had my laptop fixed (usta tuzatdi).

kahoot.q: Do you know where the station ___?
kahoot.explain: Bilvosita savolda gap tartibi: where + ega + is.

kahoot.q: She avoided ___ the question.
kahoot.explain: avoid + V-ing: avoided answering.

kahoot.q: ___ by the news, she started crying.
kahoot.explain: Uni xabar hayratga soldi (passiv) → V3: Shocked by the news.

kahoot.q: What matters most ___ your effort.
kahoot.explain: Ega ergash gap (What matters most) → birlik fe'l: is.

kahoot.q: Someone who is very good with technology is ___.
kahoot.explain: tech-savvy — texnologiyani yaxshi biladigan (2-dars).

kahoot.q: A travel plan with dates and places is an ___.
kahoot.explain: itinerary — sayohat rejasi, marshrut (7-dars).

kahoot.q: Before the exam I need to ___ on my grammar.
kahoot.explain: brush up on — bilimni tezda yangilamoq, takrorlamoq (1-dars).

kahoot.q: A team that is expected to lose but still fights is the ___.
kahoot.explain: underdog — yutqazishi kutilgan, zaif hisoblangan tomon (11-dars).

kahoot.q: The ability to recover quickly after problems is ___.
kahoot.explain: resilience — qiyinchilikdan tez tiklanish qobiliyati (13-dars).

kahoot.q: The money a company earns from sales is its ___.
kahoot.explain: revenue — daromad, tushum (3-dars).

kahoot.q: The best and most famous work of an artist is a ___.
kahoot.explain: masterpiece — shoh asar (5-dars).

kahoot.q: "evidence" ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: evidence — dalil (4-dars). hypothesis — taxmin, innovation — ixtiro.
